fact: A sleeve between two moving parts, chosen to be the thing that wears out.

name: Counterweight
fact: Mass on the other side, so the machine lifts the load and not itself.

name: Capstone
fact: The stone on top, which is often the one that makes the rest work.

name: Capital
fact: The block at the top of a column that spreads the load into the beam.

name: Linkage
fact: Bars and pivots arranged so one motion becomes a different one.

name: Harness
fact: Getting an animal's pull to the load without choking it.

name: Webbing
fact: Woven flat strap — far stronger for its weight than the same fibre as rope.

name: Pawl
fact: The tooth that drops in and stops the wheel going back.

name: Substrate
fact: The thing everything else is built on, chosen for flatness and for not moving.

name: Coating
fact: A layer added for a property the thing underneath does not have.

name: Fabric
fact: Cloth considered as an engineering material rather than as clothing.

name: Surfactant
fact: A molecule with a water-loving end and a fat-loving end, standing in the boundary.

name: Blowing Agent
fact: Something that makes gas at the right moment, so a solid comes out full of holes.

name: Pellet
fact: The shape everything plastic ships in, because a bead pours and a sheet does not.

name: Vent
fact: A hole with a reason, and usually a flap or a filter.

name: Ratchet
fact: Motion one way and not the other, with a click to prove it.

name: Yoke
fact: A crosspiece that shares a load between two of something.

name: Nipple
fact: The little nut at the rim end of a spoke, and the only place a wheel is adjusted.

name: Bob
fact: The weight at the bottom, and moving it is how a clock is set.

name: Clapper
fact: The bit that hits, and it must strike and then get out of the way.

name: Injector
fact: Getting fuel and oxidiser to mix completely in about a millisecond.

name: Combustion Chamber
fact: Where it burns, and the walls should not.

name: Turbopump
fact: A pump driven by a turbine burning the same fuel it is pumping.

name: Expansion Valve
fact: A deliberate restriction, so the pressure drops and the liquid gets cold.

name: Impeller
fact: Vanes that throw fluid outward, and the casing turns speed into pressure.

name: Primary Mirror
fact: The whole telescope, effectively — everything else is looking at what it collects.

name: Secondary Mirror
fact: A small mirror that folds the light back out to somewhere usable.

name: Baffle
fact: A plate in the way, put there to stop something going straight.

name: Essential Oil
fact: The volatile part of a plant, separated by steam rather than pressed.

name: Fixative
fact: Something that evaporates slowly, so the fast things do not all leave at once.

name: Universal Joint
fact: Torque round a corner, at the cost of the output speed varying twice a turn.

name: Spline
fact: Teeth cut along a shaft, so it can slide and still turn what it is inside.

name: Heat Shield
fact: Something that survives re-entry by being destroyed slowly and on purpose.

name: Airbag
fact: A bag inflated by a small explosion, and it is deflating by the time you reach it.

name: Air Filter
fact: Catching what would otherwise go through the engine at the speed of the intake.

name: Venturi
fact: A narrowing where the flow speeds up and the pressure falls.

name: Needle Valve
fact: A taper in a seat, so the opening changes smoothly rather than in steps.

name: Choke
fact: Deliberately starving the engine of air, because a cold one needs more fuel.

name: Saturn V
fact: Three stages, 111 metres, and still the largest thing ever flown.

name: Command Module
fact: The only part of Apollo that came home.

name: Lunar Module
fact: A spacecraft that only ever flew in vacuum, so it did not have to look like anything.

name: Spacesuit
fact: A vehicle shaped like a person, and the hands are the hard part.

name: Guidance Computer
fact: Woven memory, and it flew to the Moon on 72 kilobytes.

name: Docking Port
fact: Two spacecraft becoming one, at a closing speed of a few centimetres a second.

name: Airlock
fact: A room you can empty of air without emptying the one next door.

name: Life Support
fact: Making oxygen, removing carbon dioxide, and the second is the urgent one.

name: Robotic Arm
fact: Joints in series, and the error at the end is every joint's error added up.

name: Float Chamber
fact: A small tank with a float, so the fuel level stays put whatever the pump is doing.

name: Bridge (Instrument)
fact: The part that carries the string's vibration down into the soundboard, and it is only held on by pressure.

name: Welt
fact: A strip stitched between upper and sole, so the shoe can be resoled without touching the upper.

name: Upper
fact: Everything above the sole, which is where the fit lives.

name: Turnout Coat
fact: Three layers: one that will not burn, one that keeps water out, one that holds air.

name: Breathing Apparatus
fact: Carrying your own air, and the cylinder is the clock.

name: Radioisotope Generator
fact: No moving parts, no sunlight needed, and it runs for decades because the fuel decays on its own schedule.

name: Thermocouple
fact: Two different metals joined, producing a voltage that depends only on the temperature difference.

name: Friction Disc
fact: The wearing part of a clutch, and it is meant to be the thing that goes.

name: Pressure Plate
fact: A spring that clamps the clutch shut, and the pedal's whole job is to defeat it.

name: Diaphragm Spring
fact: A cone of spring steel with fingers cut in it, so pressing the middle releases the rim.

name: Release Bearing
fact: The bearing that lets a spinning clutch be pushed by a hand that is not spinning.

name: Needle Plate
fact: The steel plate the needle passes through, and the hole size is the whole setting.

name: Driver Pin
fact: The top pin, pushed by a spring, and the one that blocks the lock.

name: Key Pin
fact: The bottom pin, and its length is one cut on the key.

name: Escape Wheel
fact: The last wheel in the train, and the one the pendulum is allowed to release a tooth at a time.

name: Hairspring
fact: A spiral thinner than a hair, and it is what makes a watch keep time.

name: Sheave
fact: The wheel inside a pulley block, and its groove must fit the rope exactly.

name: Jib
fact: The arm, and everything about a crane's stability is a moment about its base.

name: Outrigger
fact: Legs that put the crane's base wider than its wheels.

name: Presser Foot
fact: It holds the cloth down so the feed dog can move it, and lifting it is how you steer.

name: Crumple Zone
fact: Structure designed to fail, so the deceleration happens over half a metre instead of instantly.

name: Anti-roll Bar
fact: A torsion spring between the two wheels of an axle, doing nothing until the car leans.

name: Control Arm
fact: The link that decides the path a wheel takes as it moves up and down.

name: Brake Lever
fact: A lever whose ratio decides whether a hand can stop a bicycle.

name: O-ring
fact: A rubber circle squashed into a groove, and the pressure it seals against helps it seal.

name: Thermometer
fact: Something that changes measurably with temperature, and a scale somebody agreed on.

name: Still
fact: A pot, a head and a worm — heat here, cool there, catch what comes over.

name: Reflux
fact: Vapour that condenses and falls back, distilling the mixture again on its way.

name: Mihrab
fact: A niche that does nothing except point.

name: Iwan
fact: A vaulted hall open on one whole side, and four of them round a court is the Persian plan.

name: Caravanserai
fact: A courtyard with one gate, spaced a day's march from the next one.

name: Thruster
fact: A small engine that points a spacecraft rather than moving it anywhere.

name: Magnetometer
fact: Measuring a field that is invisible, and mapping what made it.

name: Defibrillator
fact: It does not start a heart. It stops one, and hopes the pacemaker restarts it.

name: Microcontroller
fact: A whole computer on one chip, in things that nobody thinks of as computers.

name: Gear Train
fact: Gears in series, and the ratios multiply.

name: Connecting Rod
fact: The link between a piston going up and down and a crank going round.

name: Host Plant
fact: The plant something else is living on, with or without its consent.

name: Tomb
fact: A structure whose whole purpose is that somebody stays where they were put.

name: Prism
fact: Glass with non-parallel faces, so the bending does not cancel and colours come apart.

name: Spectrometer
fact: Splitting light into its wavelengths, which is how a chemical announces itself across space.

name: Hypoxia
fact: Not enough oxygen reaching the tissue, and the brain notices last.

name: Asphyxia
fact: Oxygen cannot get in, and in an oxygen-poor atmosphere there is no warning at all.

name: Exsanguination
fact: Losing enough blood that the circulation stops working, well before it runs out.

name: Laceration
fact: A tear rather than a cut, and the ragged edge is why it heals differently.

name: Blunt Trauma
fact: The skin is intact and the damage is underneath, which is what makes it hard to see.

name: Crush Syndrome
fact: The danger is often the release, not the pressure.

name: Fracture
fact: Bone fails in tension long before it fails in compression, which is why it breaks on the far side.

name: Thermal Burn
fact: Depth is set by temperature and time together, and steam is worse than air at the same reading.

name: Chemical Burn
fact: It goes on burning after contact stops, which is the difference from heat.

name: Frostbite
fact: Ice crystals in the tissue, and the circulation shuts the extremity down to save the core.

name: Heat Stroke
fact: Thermoregulation has failed, which is a different thing from being hot.

name: Drowning
fact: Mostly it is quiet, and mostly very little water enters the lungs.

name: Electrocution
fact: Current does the damage, not voltage, and the path decides whether it matters.

name: Poisoning
fact: Every substance is a poison at some dose, which is the only useful general statement about it.

name: Allergic Reaction
fact: The immune system responding hard to something that was not a threat.

name: Silicosis
fact: Crystalline silica dust the lung cannot remove, and the scarring is permanent.

name: Asbestosis
fact: Fibres too fine to cough out and too durable to break down.

name: Narcosis
fact: Gas dissolving into nerve membranes under pressure, and the diver feels fine about it.

name: Methaemoglobinaemia
fact: Haemoglobin still there, still circulating, and no longer able to carry oxygen.

name: Radiation Sickness
fact: The cells that divide fastest go first, which is why the gut and the marrow fail before anything else.

name: Irritant
fact: Reversible inflammation, which is the whole difference from a corrosive.

name: Sensitiser
fact: Harmless the first time, and that is the danger.

name: Neurotoxin
fact: Interfering with signalling, which is fast and often does not need much.

name: Hepatotoxin
fact: The liver is damaged because it is the organ doing the processing.

name: Nephrotoxin
fact: The kidney concentrates what it is clearing, which is exactly the problem.

name: Route of Exposure
fact: How it gets in decides almost everything about what it does.

name: Latency
fact: The gap between the exposure and the disease, and it can be forty years.

name: Corrosive
fact: A substance that destroys tissue where it lands, rather than by being absorbed.

name: Segment
fact: The repeating unit an arthropod body is built from — each with its own pair of appendages in the ancestral plan, and fused into groups in every living lineage.

name: Thorax
fact: The middle of the three body regions of an insect, and the one that carries every leg and every wing.

name: Abdomen
fact: The hindmost body region, where digestion, breathing and reproduction happen and no leg is attached.

name: Mandible
fact: An insect's jaw: a single hard block that swings sideways rather than up and down.

name: Coxa
fact: The first of the six segments of an insect leg — the hip, joined to the underside of the thorax.

name: Trochanter
fact: A small triangular sclerite between coxa and femur, and the only true hinge in the upper leg.

name: Tibia
fact: The long lower segment of an insect leg, usually the thinnest and often carrying spurs.

name: Tarsus
fact: The foot: a short chain of small segments ending in claws.

name: Chelicera
fact: The mouthpart that gives the chelicerates their name — a fang, not a jaw.

name: Pedipalp
fact: The second pair of arachnid appendages: a feeler in a spider, a claw in a scorpion.

name: Ommatidium
fact: One facet of a compound eye — a complete little eye with its own lens.

name: Elytron
fact: A beetle's front wing, hardened into a case over the flying wing beneath.

name: Proboscis
fact: A drinking straw made from mouthparts, coiled under the head when it is not in use.

name: Ovipositor
fact: The egg-laying tube at the end of the abdomen, in some insects longer than the rest of the animal.

name: Sting
fact: A modified ovipositor. Only females have one, because only females ever had the organ it is made from.

name: Pupa
fact: The still stage where a larva is taken apart and an adult is built from the pieces.

name: Chrysalis
fact: A butterfly's pupa — bare, hardened and hanging, with no silk around it.

name: Instar
fact: The stage between two moults. An insect grows in steps, not continuously.

name: Pheromone
fact: A message written in a molecule, addressed to the rest of your own species.

name: Colony
fact: A society of insects where most members never reproduce.

name: Hive
fact: A bee colony's house, and the comb inside it.

name: Honeycomb
fact: Hexagonal wax cells, and the most efficient way to tile a plane with the least material.

name: Propolis
fact: Bee glue: tree resin worked with wax and used to seal every crack in the hive.

name: Queen Bee
fact: The one female in a colony that lays, and she is made rather than born.

name: Worker Bee
fact: A female bee that does not lay, and works through a fixed sequence of jobs as she ages.

name: Argyria
fact: Skin turned permanent blue-grey by silver, developed in it the same way a photograph is.

name: Diarrhoea
fact: The gut losing the argument about water, and still the second commonest cause of death in small children.

name: Hyperactivity
fact: Activity out of proportion to the setting — measurable, and much harder to attribute than it looks.

name: Seta
fact: A hollow cuticular bristle in a flexible socket, with one sensory cell wired to its base.

name: Prosoma
fact: Head and thorax fused under one shield, carrying every leg, the brain and the venom glands.

name: Opisthosoma
fact: The rear half of an arachnid: heart, gut, gonads, book lungs, silk glands — and never a leg.

name: Book Lung
fact: Air-filled leaves stacked like the pages of a book. Mygalomorphs have four, other spiders two.

name: Fang
fact: The chelicera's last joint, folding into a groove, with the venom duct opening near its tip.

name: Silk Gland
fact: A web spider carries four to seven, and each one spins a different silk for a different job.

name: Spider Silk
fact: It leaves the spigot liquid and sets because it is pulled — drawn, not extruded.

name: Dragline
fact: The line a spider pays out behind it wherever it goes, tacked down at intervals.

name: Orb Web
fact: Dry radii the spider walks on, and a sticky spiral it takes care never to touch.

name: Mygalomorph
fact: Jaws that stab downward, so the spider rears to bite — and four book lungs instead of two.

name: Tarantula
fact: Kicks barbed hairs off its own abdomen at whatever comes close. Captive females reach 20 years.

name: Harvestman
fact: No waist, no silk, no venom — and it eats solid food, which no spider can.

name: Pseudoscorpion
fact: A scorpion's pincers with nothing behind them: the venom is in the claw, and there is no tail.

name: Nymph
fact: The immature of an insect that has no pupa — already eyed and winged in outline, just smaller.

name: Proleg
fact: Not a leg: an unjointed sac on the abdomen that grips with a ring of tiny hooks.

name: Caterpillar
fact: Six true legs at the front, and behind them rows of prolegs that are not legs at all.

name: Haltere
fact: A hindwing shrunk to a club — basal plate, shaft and head — beating to sense rotation.

name: Fly
fact: Two wings, not four. The hind pair are halteres, which is what the name Diptera counts.

name: Maggot
fact: Legless, and in the higher flies headless too — it works with a pair of black mouth hooks.

name: Mesosoma
fact: In a wasp, bee or ant, the thorax with the first abdominal segment annexed onto the back of it.

name: Metasoma
fact: What is left of the abdomen once the thorax has taken segment I: everything from II back.

name: Petiolus
fact: The stalk between the two halves. Count its nodes and you have narrowed the ant right down.

name: Gaster
fact: The bulb at the back of an ant — the metasoma behind the waist, not the whole abdomen.

name: Metapleural Gland
fact: A gland no other insect family has: it coats an ant, and its nest, in antibiotic.

name: Queen Ant
fact: Not a ruler — the colony's only ovary. One was held in captivity for close to 29 years.

name: Nuptial Flight
fact: The one flight of a queen's life. She lands, breaks her wings off, and never flies again.

name: Stridulation
fact: A file of teeth drawn across a hard scraper. Each tooth is a click; enough clicks are a note.

name: Tympanal Organ
fact: An insect ear: cuticle thinned to a drum, an air sac behind it, a stretch receptor attached.

name: Cricket
fact: Sings by scraping one forewing across the other, and hears it with an ear on each front leg.

name: Louse
fact: An insect that gave up wings entirely, with eyes down to two facets or to none at all.

name: Nephron
fact: The kidney's working unit. About a million per kidney, and you can lose three quarters of them before a blood test notices.

name: Glomerulus
fact: A knot of capillaries that filters blood by pressure alone, with no pump of its own.

name: Urea
fact: What the body turns ammonia into so it can be carried in blood without poisoning it. The first organic compound ever made from inorganic parts.

name: Ureter
fact: The tube from kidney to bladder, and it does not simply drain — it squeezes.

name: Bladder
fact: A muscular bag whose defining trick is holding pressure steady while the volume climbs.

name: Urine
fact: 0.6% of what the kidney filtered. The rest was taken back.

name: Atrium
fact: The heart's receiving chamber. It does almost nothing, and losing it costs you about a fifth of your output.

name: Ventricle
fact: The pumping chamber, and the left one is three times the wall thickness of the right for a reason.

name: Aorta
fact: The body's main artery, and a spring as much as a pipe.

name: Platelet
fact: Not a cell — a fragment torn off a much larger one, with no nucleus and about ten days to live.

name: Lymph
fact: The fluid that leaked out of your capillaries and needs a second circulation to get home.

name: Larynx
fact: A valve that guards the airway, and makes sound as a side effect of doing it.

name: Pleura
fact: Two wet membranes that let the lung slide against the chest wall without ever being attached to it.

name: Breath
fact: About half a litre, twelve to twenty times a minute, and the muscle does the work only on the way in.

name: Duodenum
fact: The first twenty-five centimetres of intestine, where nearly all the chemistry actually happens.

name: Villus
fact: A finger of gut lining, and the reason a tube a few centimetres wide has the absorbing area of a room.

name: Myelin
fact: Fatty insulation wrapped round an axon, which makes the signal jump instead of crawl.

name: Adrenaline
fact: A hormone and a neurotransmitter at once, and the whole fight-or-flight response in one molecule.

name: Pituitary
fact: A pea under the brain that runs most of the other glands, and takes its orders from just above it.

name: Tendon
fact: Rope that ties muscle to bone, and stores energy as well as transmitting it.

name: Sarcomere
fact: The unit muscle is built from, and the reason contraction is a ratchet rather than a squeeze.

name: Clot
fact: A plug of platelets caught in a protein net. In the right place it saves you and in the wrong one it is a stroke.

name: Fibrin
fact: The mesh a clot is actually made of, assembled on the spot from something already dissolved in the blood.

name: Mouth
fact: Where digestion starts, and the only part of it you have any say over.

name: Pharynx
fact: The one passage that food and air both use, which is the design flaw everything else compensates for.

name: Epiglottis
fact: The flap that closes the airway when you swallow, and the reason the crossing is survivable.

name: Reflex
fact: An action decided in the spinal cord, with the brain told afterwards.

name: Rod Cell
fact: The eye's night receptor. Sensitive enough to answer a single photon, and it tells you nothing about colour.

name: Cone Cell
fact: Three kinds, three overlapping sensitivities, and every colour you have ever seen is the ratio between them.

name: Pupil
fact: Not a thing but a hole — and it looks black because almost no light that goes in comes back out.

name: Vitreous Humour
fact: The clear gel that holds the eye's shape, made once before birth and never replaced.

name: Melanin
fact: The pigment that absorbs ultraviolet, and the reason a tan is a record of damage rather than protection banked in advance.

name: Sweat Gland
fact: Two to four million of them, and they are most of why humans can run down faster animals.

name: Follicle
fact: The pit a hair grows out of, with a muscle and an oil gland attached to it.

name: Sebaceous Gland
fact: The oil gland on the side of a hair follicle, and it destroys itself to deliver.

name: Serum
fact: Plasma with the clotting proteins taken out — which is what is left in the tube after blood has clotted.

name: Blood Type
fact: Sugars on the surface of a red cell, and the reason transfusion killed people for centuries before anyone knew why.

name: Rhesus Factor
fact: The plus or minus after your blood group, and it matters most between a mother and a second child.

name: Albumin
fact: The commonest protein in blood, and its job is to hold water in the vessels.

name: Erythropoietin
fact: The kidney's message to the marrow: make more red cells. This is what altitude training is actually doing.

name: Egg Cell
fact: The largest cell in the human body, and every one you will ever have was made before you were born.

name: Ovulation
fact: One egg released, roughly once a month, out of a starting stock of a million or so.

name: Umbilical Cord
fact: Two arteries and one vein in a rope of jelly, and the artery is the one carrying used blood.

name: Eardrum
fact: A membrane the thickness of a sheet of paper, moving less than the width of an atom at the threshold of hearing.

name: Ossicle
fact: The three smallest bones in the body, and they exist to solve an impedance problem.

name: Semicircular Canal
fact: Three fluid loops at right angles, which is exactly enough to sense rotation in any direction.

name: Sweat
fact: 99% water, and the only reason it cools you is that evaporating takes heat away with it.

name: Lactation
fact: Milk made on demand, and the demand is the signal — supply follows removal rather than the other way round.

name: Shivering
fact: Muscles working against each other on purpose, because the waste heat is the point.

name: Basal Metabolic Rate
fact: What it costs to be alive doing nothing, and it is most of what you spend.

name: Blood Plasma
fact: Over half of blood by volume, and it is 92% water — the cells are the minority passenger.

name: Capillary Bed
fact: The only place in the circulation where anything is actually delivered. Everything else is plumbing.

name: Slow Twitch
fact: Muscle fibre built for endurance: full of mitochondria, red with myoglobin, and almost impossible to fatigue.

name: Fast Twitch
fact: The other kind: three times the speed, a fraction of the endurance, and it does not wait for oxygen.

name: Oxygen Debt
fact: Why you keep breathing hard after you stop. The body is paying for work already done.

name: Hypertrophy
fact: Muscle grows by making each fibre thicker, not by making more of them.

name: Fatigue
fact: Not one thing. The muscle, the fuel and the brain all give out, and usually the brain is first.

name: Receptor
fact: A lock on a cell. Almost every drug there is works by fitting one, or by stopping something else fitting it.

name: Agonist
fact: A key that fits the lock and turns it — the drug that does what the body's own molecule does.

name: Antagonist
fact: A key that fits and does not turn, and blocks the lock while it sits there.

name: First Pass Metabolism
fact: Everything swallowed goes through the liver before the rest of the body sees any of it.

name: Drug Half-Life
fact: How long until half of it is gone, and it is the reason dosing is every so many hours rather than once.

name: Tolerance
fact: The same dose doing less, because the body has adjusted to it being there.

name: Glial Cell
fact: The other half of the brain. They do not fire, and for a century that made them look like packing.

name: Medulla
fact: The bit of brainstem that runs breathing and heart rate, and never asks you.

name: Resting Potential
fact: A cell sits at about -70 millivolts, and holding it there is most of what a neuron spends energy on.

name: Proprioception
fact: The sense of where your body is without looking, and losing it is far more disabling than losing sight.

name: Keratinocyte
fact: The cell that makes up most of your skin, and its whole career is dying in the right way.

name: Goosebump
fact: A muscle pulling a hair upright, which is useful if you have fur and vestigial if you do not.

name: Scar
fact: Repair, not replacement. Collagen laid down fast and in the wrong direction, and it never gets past about 80% of the original strength.

name: Menstruation
fact: The lining shed because it was built for an implantation that did not happen — and very few mammals do this.

name: Ketone
fact: What the liver makes from fat when sugar runs out, and one of the few things the brain will burn besides glucose.

name: Cardiac Output
fact: About five litres a minute at rest, and it can pass twenty-five in someone trained.

name: Stroke Volume
fact: How much leaves the heart per beat — and the thing endurance training actually changes.

name: Lactate
fact: Not the cause of the burn, and not a waste product — it is fuel the body makes when oxygen runs short, and burns later.

name: Grey Matter
fact: Cell bodies. The thinking parts are on the outside of the brain and the inside of the spinal cord.

name: Ion Channel
fact: A pore that opens and shuts, and every nerve signal in you is these doing it in sequence.

name: Sclerite
fact: One hardened plate of the exoskeleton, bounded by soft membrane. The body wall is a mosaic of them.

name: Tergite
fact: The plate roofing one body segment. The side folds of the thoracic ones are where wings came from.

name: Sternite
fact: The plate under a segment. The first abdominal one is reduced or gone in most insects.

name: Pleurite
fact: The side wall of a thoracic segment, and the only place a leg or a wing is allowed to hinge.

name: Pronotum
fact: The shield over the first thoracic segment — a plain plate in most insects, a saddle in a grasshopper.

name: Tegmen
fact: A forewing hardened into a leathery cover. It gives up most of its lift to protect the wing beneath.

name: Clypeus
fact: The plate between the face and the upper lip. The mandibles bracket it but never touch it.

name: Labrum
fact: The upper lip: a single unpaired flap hinged to the face, closing the mouth cavity from the front.

name: Maxilla
fact: The second pair of jaws, carrying a palp that tastes the food before the mandibles get to it.

name: Labium
fact: The lower lip, and it is a pair of jaws fused on the midline — the second maxillae, joined into one.

name: Hypopharynx
fact: A tongue standing between the jaws. The salivary duct opens behind it, outside the mouth.

name: Tentorium
fact: The skeleton inside an insect’s head, folded in from the outside and braced corner to corner.

name: Ocellus
fact: A single-lens eye that forms no image. Three in a triangle, reading only how bright it is.

name: Apodeme
fact: An insect’s tendon is an ingrowth of its own skin — and it is shed and regrown at every moult.

name: Epicuticle
fact: The outermost skin of an insect, thinner than a wavelength of light, and carrying no chitin at all.

name: Cercus
fact: A pair of feelers at the tail end, wired to moving air. The escape turn starts before contact.

name: Orthopteran
fact: Straight-winged: leathery forewings, a saddle over the neck, hind legs built to jump. 22,500 species.

name: Katydid
fact: A bush-cricket that fiddles one way round only: the file is on the left tegmen, the scraper on the right.

name: Caste
fact: Not inherited. The same egg becomes a queen or a worker depending on how the larva was fed.

name: Worker Ant
fact: A sterile female, wingless for life. Everything the colony does apart from laying, she does.

name: Soldier Ant
fact: A worker grown head-first — jaws so enlarged that in some species it can no longer feed itself.

name: Alate
fact: The winged form. Ants and termites both make one, and both shed the wings after a single flight.

name: Queen Termite
fact: Her abdomen swells until she cannot walk, and she lays thousands of eggs a day for decades.

name: Soldier Termite
fact: Blind, sterile and built around its head. Some have given up jaws entirely and spray glue instead.

name: Trophallaxis
fact: Mouth-to-mouth feeding. A colony shares one stomach, and everything dissolved in it.

name: Termite Mound
fact: Soil, saliva and dung built into a chimney. The colony lives under it rather than in it.

name: Swarm
fact: How a bee colony reproduces: the old queen leaves with the workers, and a daughter keeps the house.

name: Bolus
fact: A swallow. The mouthful once it has been chewed and wetted enough to go down in one piece.

name: Chyme
fact: What the stomach hands on: a soup at about pH 2, released a few millilitres at a time.

name: Pepsin
fact: The stomach's protein-cutting enzyme, and it only works in acid — which is a safety feature.

name: Amylase
fact: The enzyme that starts on starch, and it is in your mouth — digestion begins before you swallow.

name: Trypsin
fact: The intestine's protein cutter, and the one that switches on all the others.

name: Lipase
fact: The fat splitter, and it cannot work until bile has broken the fat into droplets.

name: Hepatocyte
fact: The liver cell, and it does several hundred different jobs — which is why nothing has ever replaced a liver mechanically.

name: Portal Vein
fact: The one vein that goes to an organ instead of back to the heart, and everything you eat travels it.

name: Absorption
fact: The moment something stops being in your gut and starts being in you. Everything before this is still outside.

name: Osteoblast
fact: The cell that builds bone, and it walls itself in doing it.

name: Ossification
fact: Bone forming — and most of yours was cartilage first.

name: Periosteum
fact: The living sleeve around a bone. It is where the pain is, and where a fracture heals from.

name: Synovial Fluid
fact: Joint oil, and it gives a lower friction than anything engineering has managed.

name: Negative Feedback
fact: The output shutting off its own cause. Nearly everything the body holds steady is held by this.

name: Prolactin
fact: The milk hormone, and it is held switched off by the brain rather than switched on.

name: Aldosterone
fact: The salt hormone. It tells the kidney to keep sodium, and water follows sodium.

name: Parathyroid
fact: Four glands the size of grains of rice, and they hold blood calcium steadier than almost anything else in the body.

name: Differentiation
fact: One genome, two hundred kinds of cell. Nothing is added — things are switched off.

name: Gastrulation
fact: The fold that turns a ball of cells into something with an inside — and the most important event in your life.

name: Neural Tube
fact: The brain and spinal cord begin as a flat sheet that rolls up and zips shut.

name: Myelination
fact: Insulation laid down over twenty-five years, front of the brain last — which is a fact about adolescence.

name: Synaptic Plasticity
fact: Connections that strengthen with use. This is what learning physically is.

name: Bile Duct
fact: The pipe from liver and gallbladder to the gut, and it shares its last few millimetres with the pancreas.

name: Osteoclast
fact: The cell that dissolves bone, and you need it as much as the one that builds.

name: Endocrine Gland
fact: A gland with no duct. It puts its product into the blood and lets the circulation do the addressing.

name: Germ Layer
fact: Three sheets laid down in the first fortnight, and every tissue you have comes from one of them.

name: Pons
fact: A bridge across the brainstem, and it is where the paralysis of dreaming is switched on.

name: Pantothenic acid
fact: Named from the Greek for 'from everywhere', because it is in nearly every food — which is why deficiency in humans is very rare.

name: Linoleic acid
fact: The more essential of the two essential fatty acids, because the body uses it as the base from which it makes the others.

name: Alpha-linolenic acid
fact: 'Linolenic' comes from linon, the Greek for flax — the plant is in the name of the molecule.

name: Head capsule
fact: Six segments fused into one sclerotised box — the sutures still visible on it are internal strengthening, not the boundaries between the segments, which have gone.

name: Contraception
fact: The combined pill does not block anything: it keeps the hormone level high enough that the signal to release an egg is never sent.

name: Hearing aid
fact: Not an amplifier. A plain sound amplifier cannot legally be sold as one — the work is compression, because the damaged ear's usable range is narrower at both ends.

name: Resin composite
fact: Two materials that are each bad at what the other is good at: the fibre is stiff and brittle, the polymer ductile and weak, and the pair is stiff, strong and tough.

name: MDF
fact: Wood taken apart to individual fibres and reassembled, so it has no grain left — which is why a routed edge holds where plywood's would splinter.

name: Radiation
fact: Whether it is dangerous is decided by the energy of one quantum, not by how much of it there is: above about 10 eV a single one can break a bond.

name: Lycopene
fact: Named after Lycopersicon, a former tomato genus. Eleven conjugated double bonds make it that red.

name: Gallic acid
fact: Named for the oak galls it was prepared from, not for gallium — it contains none.

name: Oleic acid
fact: The most common fatty acid in nature, and the thing people mean when they call olive oil monounsaturated.

name: Genistein
fact: Named for the dyer's broom it was first pulled out of in 1899, though soy is where it is abundant.

name: Quercetin
fact: Named in 1857 after quercetum, an oak forest, though capers, onions and kale are where you meet it.

name: Rosmarinic acid
fact: Named for rosemary and shared across the mint family — sage, basil, perilla and mint all carry it.

name: Ellagic acid
fact: Galle spelled backwards, to keep it apart from gallic acid — which is literally what it is two of.

name: Malvidin
fact: Makes red wine red. It decays to syringic acid, which is how a 6,100-year-old winery was identified.

name: Sesamin
fact: A lignan of sesame oil, and of the bark of Fagara trees that have nothing else to do with sesame.

name: Betaine
fact: Named for the sugar beet it came out of, Beta vulgaris — not, despite everything, for the Greek letter.

name: Sulforaphane
fact: Does not exist in an intact cabbage. Chopping lets myrosinase reach glucoraphanin, and the reaction makes it.

name: Zeaxanthin
fact: Zea mays plus xanthos, Greek for yellow. One of two carotenoids the retina holds.

name: Phytic acid
fact: How a seed banks its phosphorus. It grips calcium, iron and zinc too, and the gut cannot get them back.

name: Resveratrol
fact: A phytoalexin: the plant does not keep it ready, it makes it when injured or attacked.

name: Ergosterol
fact: What a fungus uses where an animal uses cholesterol. Named after ergot, where it was first found.

name: Casein
fact: Latin caseus, cheese. Four fifths of cow's-milk protein, and the part that curdles; whey is the rest.

name: Radon
fact: A colourless, odourless radioactive gas that seeps out of uranium-bearing rock — by the EPA's count the second most frequent cause of lung cancer after smoking.

name: Tennessine
fact: Named for Tennessee, where Oak Ridge's labs helped make it — the most recently discovered element, caught as atoms lasting only tens to hundreds of milliseconds.

discovered.note: Dubna and Oak Ridge fire calcium-48 at a berkelium-249 target and catch the decays of element 117.

name: Oganesson
fact: Named for Yuri Oganessian, who led the discovery of the heaviest elements; its only known isotope lasts 0.7 milliseconds.

discovered.note: First synthesised at Dubna by a Russian–American team, by firing calcium-48 at californium-249.

name: Inertia
fact: Things keep doing what they are doing, at rest or in motion, until a force changes their velocity.

name: Torque
fact: A force's turning power: the force applied perpendicular to a lever, times its distance from the fulcrum.

name: Wavelength
fact: The distance over which a wave's shape repeats, from crest to crest.

name: Kinetic Energy
fact: The energy a thing has because it is moving.

name: Potential Energy
fact: Energy a system has because of where its parts are relative to each other.

name: Absolute Zero
fact: The theoretically coldest temperature — 0 kelvin, which is −273.15 °C.

name: Doppler Effect
fact: The pitch of a passing siren drops because its waves bunch up ahead of it and stretch out behind.

name: Diffraction
fact: Waves bend around obstacles and spread out through openings.

name: Ohm's Law
fact: Current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it, and resistance is the constant that connects them.

name: Maxwell's Equations
fact: The equations that tied electricity, magnetism and light into one theory.

name: Ideal Gas Law
fact: Pressure, volume and temperature of a gas, tied together in one equation.

name: Conservation of Energy
fact: The total energy of an isolated system stays constant; it only changes form.

name: Software
fact: Programs, plus the design documents and specifications behind them, that tell a computer what to do.

name: Email
fact: Digital messages sent over a computer network, held on a server until the other end collects them.

name: Cryptography
fact: The practice of secure communication in the presence of adversaries.

name: Beach
fact: Loose sand, gravel or shingle left where waves and currents deposit and rework it.

name: Jet Stream
fact: A fast, narrow river of air near the tropopause, flowing west to east around the world.

name: Ice Sheet
fact: A continental glacier — by definition more than 50,000 km², and only two exist.

name: Humidity
fact: The concentration of water vapour in the air, which depends on temperature and pressure.

name: Bog
fact: A wetland that accumulates peat, where the surface water is acidic and low in nutrients.

name: Ester
fact: What an acid and an alcohol make when they join — and often the smell of fruit and flowers.

name: Thiol
fact: The sulfur analogue of an alcohol — and the reason skunks smell the way they do.

name: Chloride
fact: Chlorine with one extra electron.

name: Knot
fact: An intentional complication in cordage — practical, decorative, or both.

name: Scroll
fact: A roll of papyrus, parchment or paper with writing on it — the first form of editable record-keeping.

name: Central Heating
fact: One main source of heat, shared out to many rooms.

name: Tonsil
fact: Lymphoid organs at the back of the throat, largest in young children relative to the throat.

name: Kelvin
fact: The SI unit of temperature, counted up from absolute zero — a rise of one kelvin is exactly a rise of one degree Celsius.

name: Litre
fact: A cube ten centimetres on a side — and, almost exactly, the volume of a kilogram of water.

name: Hour
fact: A twenty-fourth of a day, now defined as exactly 3,600 seconds.

name: Gum
fact: Plant polysaccharides that thicken a solution enormously even in tiny amounts — the thickeners, gels and glues behind a great deal of food and industry.

name: Juice
fact: The liquid of a fruit or vegetable, pressed out and drunk.

name: Polymerase
fact: The enzyme that builds long chains — DNA and RNA are assembled by one reading a template strand.

name: Canal
fact: An artificial river: an engineered channel for drainage, irrigation or carrying boats.

name: Squash
fact: Pumpkin, gourd or squash, depending on the species and who is talking — all fruits of the genus Cucurbita.

name: Fluid
fact: Anything that flows when pushed sideways — liquids and gases both.

name: Armor
fact: A covering that takes the blow so the body does not.

name: Addition
fact: Combining two quantities into one — repeated addition of 1 is the same as counting.

name: Subtraction
fact: Addition run backwards: the number that, added to the second, gives the first.

name: Multiplication
fact: Repeated addition: three groups of four.

name: Arithmetic
fact: The elementary branch of mathematics: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

name: Exponentiation
fact: Repeated multiplication: a base multiplied by itself, n times.

name: Square Root
fact: The number that, multiplied by itself, gives the number you started with.

name: Logarithm
fact: The inverse of exponentiation; Napier introduced it in 1614 to turn multiplying into adding.

name: Integer
fact: Zero, the counting numbers, and their negations.

name: Negative Number
fact: A number less than zero — a debt, thought of as an asset below nothing.

name: Rational Number
fact: Any number that can be written as one integer over another.

name: Real Number
fact: The numbers of the continuous line, including the irrational ones — the numbers calculus needs.

name: Complex Number
fact: A real part plus an imaginary one — the numbers that make every polynomial equation solvable.

name: Point
fact: "That which has no part" — position with no size.

name: Line
fact: Infinitely long and with no width: the idealisation of a taut string.

name: Angle
fact: Two rays from a common point; how far one is turned from the other.

name: Polygon
fact: A closed chain of straight edges: triangle, square, pentagon and on.

name: Perimeter
fact: The length of a closed boundary — the fence needed around a yard.

name: Parallel
fact: Lines in one plane that never meet, however far they run.

name: Tangent
fact: A line that just touches a curve at one point.

name: Trigonometry
fact: The relations between the angles and side lengths of triangles, from the Greek for "triangle" and "measure".

name: Sine
fact: Opposite over hypotenuse — and, on the unit circle, a height.

name: Sphere
fact: All the points at one distance from a centre, in three dimensions.

name: Volume
fact: How much three-dimensional space something takes up.

name: Derivative
fact: The instantaneous rate of change of a function — the slope of its tangent.

name: Integral
fact: Area under a curve — and the inverse of differentiation.

name: Matrix
fact: A rectangle of numbers in rows and columns, built to hold a whole system of linear equations.

name: Sequence
fact: A list in which order matters and repeats are allowed.

name: Series
fact: An addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.

name: Conjecture
fact: A proposition put forward without proof — some are still open after centuries.

name: Mathematics
fact: The study of numbers, shapes, sets, functions and the structures between them.

name: Percentage
fact: A number expressed as a fraction of 100 — "by the hundred".

name: Goods
fact: What a factory makes from raw material: things that are scarce because producing them costs effort.

name: Service
fact: Value that is an act, not an object: someone is willing to pay for it being done.

name: Price
fact: The amount at which buyers and sellers agree a thing changes hands.

name: Supply and Demand
fact: The model of how a market settles on a price.

name: Inflation
fact: The average price of goods and services rising, measured in money.

name: Deflation
fact: Inflation's opposite: the general price level falling.

name: Profit
fact: What is left of the revenue once every cost of the inputs has been paid.

name: Business
fact: Making a living by producing, or buying and selling, goods and services.

name: Company
fact: A legal entity that is an association of legal persons with a shared objective.

name: Corporation
fact: A company the state authorises to act as one entity — and whose owners are not personally liable.

name: Wage
fact: The price of labour.

name: Employment
fact: A relationship between two parties for the provision of paid labour.

name: Unemployment
fact: Available for work, but not in paid employment.

name: Loan
fact: Money handed over on an agreement to pay it back.

name: Mortgage
fact: A loan secured on a property — "death pledge" in Law French.

name: Insurance
fact: A fee paid now for compensation if a specified loss comes later.

name: Investment
fact: Committing resources to something expected to gain value over time.

name: Stock Exchange
fact: A market where shares in corporations are bought and sold — Amsterdam's is often called the oldest modern one.

name: Accounting
fact: Recording and reporting financial transactions; double-entry bookkeeping comes from medieval Venice.

name: Gross Domestic Product
fact: The total market value of a country's final goods and services in a year.

name: Economic Growth
fact: More, and better, goods and services produced by a society.

name: Economics
fact: The social science of production, distribution and consumption.

name: Monopoly
fact: A single seller, and so no competition and no substitute.

name: Subsidy
fact: Public money that keeps a job, a farm or a housing programme going.

name: Sales Tax
fact: A tax paid to a governing body on the sale of certain goods and services.

name: Property Tax
fact: A tax on the value of a property, set as a percentage — or a "millage".

name: Income Tax
fact: A tax on the income or profits people and entities earn.

name: International Trade
fact: Exchange of capital, goods and services across borders.

name: Exchange Rate
fact: The rate at which one currency is exchanged for another.

name: Pension
fact: A fund paid into during a working career, paid out in retirement.

name: Bankruptcy
fact: A legal process through which those who cannot repay debts may seek relief.

name: Black Market
fact: A clandestine market with some aspect of illegality.

name: Protectionism
fact: Restricting imports with tariffs and quotas.

name: Competition
fact: Firms contending for limited goods by varying price, product, promotion and place.

name: Commerce
fact: The organised system for the large-scale exchange of goods and services.

name: Productivity
fact: Output per unit of input: how efficiently goods or services get made.

name: Morality
fact: The standards by which communities and individuals evaluate actions, character and social arrangements.

name: Truth
fact: Conformity to reality or fact — a property of sentences, propositions or beliefs.

name: Idea
fact: In philosophy, a mental image of some object — and what beliefs are made of.

name: Concept
fact: A unit of cognition that sorts things into kinds by their shared features.

name: Argument
fact: Premises directed towards a conclusion, to give reasons.

name: Fallacy
fact: Faulty reasoning that looks well-reasoned if no one notices.

name: Inference
fact: A step in reasoning from premises to their logical consequences.

name: Deductive Reasoning
fact: If the premises are true, the conclusion cannot be false.

name: Inductive Reasoning
fact: From a sample to a conclusion about the whole — supported by probability, never by certainty.

name: Hypothesis
fact: A proposed explanation for a phenomenon, waiting to be tested.

name: Fact
fact: A true datum about an occurrence in the real world.

name: Skepticism
fact: Doubt towards knowledge claims that are seen as mere belief or dogma.

name: Empiricism
fact: The view that true knowledge comes from sensory experience and evidence.

name: Rationalism
fact: Reason as the chief source and test of knowledge.

name: Free Will
fact: The capacity to choose between courses of action — the basis of moral responsibility.

name: Determinism
fact: All events within the universe can occur only in one possible way.

name: Existentialism
fact: The struggle to lead an authentic life despite the apparent absurdity of existence.

name: Nihilism
fact: The rejection of any objectively meaningful purpose, moral value or truth.

name: Utilitarianism
fact: Act so as to maximise happiness and well-being for everyone affected.

name: Deontology
fact: Rightness lies in the action's fit with rules and duties, not its consequences.

name: Relativism
fact: Valuations are relative to the perspective of an observer or the context.

name: Humanism
fact: Human agency as the starting point for moral and philosophical inquiry.

name: Metaphysics
fact: The branch of philosophy on the basic nature of reality.

name: Aesthetics
fact: The branch of philosophy that studies beauty and taste.

name: Wisdom
fact: Wit and virtue together: applying experience to complex questions of life.

name: Virtue
fact: A trait of excellence — moral, social or intellectual.

name: Conscience
fact: The inner process that links emotion and reasoning to one's own moral philosophy.

name: Thought Experiment
fact: An imaginary scenario meant to elucidate or test an argument or theory.

name: Deity
fact: A supernatural being with authority over some aspect of the universe or life.

name: Theology
fact: The study of religious belief from a religious perspective.

name: Sacrifice
fact: An act or offering made to a deity.

name: Saint
fact: In Christian belief, a person recognised as exceptionally holy or close to God.

name: Relic
fact: The physical remains or personal effects of a saint, kept for veneration.

name: Monastery
fact: The buildings of a community of monks or nuns — or of a hermit living alone.

name: Heresy
fact: A belief strongly at variance with a religious organisation's accepted beliefs.

name: Pantheism
fact: Reality and divinity are the same thing: the universe is the divine.

name: Deism
fact: A creator who made the universe — known by reason and observation, not revelation.

name: Salvation
fact: The deliverance of the soul from ignorance or perpetual harm.

name: Hell
fact: A place or state in the afterlife where souls are punished.

name: Resurrection
fact: Coming back to life after death.

name: Apocalypse
fact: An unveiling — the Greek for "revelation, disclosure".

name: Creation Myth
fact: A symbolic narrative of how the world began and how people first came to live in it.

name: Taboo
fact: A social group's ban on something it finds repulsive, offensive, sacred or restricted.

name: Magic
fact: Beliefs, rituals or actions meant to manipulate natural or supernatural forces.

name: Superstition
fact: A belief or practice others consider irrational or supernatural — luck, fate, amulets.

name: Astrology
fact: Divination from the apparent positions of celestial objects — pseudoscience since the 18th century.

name: Divination
fact: An attempt to gain insight into a question by a magic ritual or practice.

name: Folklore
fact: The expressive culture a group shares — learned outside any school curriculum.

name: Funeral
fact: A ceremony for the final disposition of a corpse — burial, entombment or cremation.

name: Cremation
fact: Final disposition of a corpse by burning.

name: Fasting
fact: Refraining from eating — as a religious ritual or a hunger strike.

name: Totem
fact: A spirit being, sacred object or symbol that serves as a clan's emblem — from the Ojibwe doodem.

name: Curse
fact: An expressed wish that adversity or misfortune will befall someone, a place or an object.

name: Witchcraft
fact: The use of magic by a witch — traditionally to inflict harm or misfortune.

name: Monster
fact: An imaginary creature of folklore, myth and horror, grotesque enough to cause terror.

name: Mysticism
fact: The experience of becoming one with God, the Absolute, or all that exists.

name: Secularism
fact: Conducting human affairs on naturalistic considerations, uninvolved with religion.

name: Education
fact: The transmission of knowledge and skills and the development of character.

name: Teaching
fact: What a teacher does so that a learner takes up knowledge and know-how.

name: Student
fact: A person enrolled in a school — or anyone with a special interest in a subject.

name: University
fact: From the Latin for "a whole": an institution of tertiary education and research that awards degrees.

name: Curriculum
fact: A planned sequence of instruction.

name: Exam
fact: An educational assessment meant to measure knowledge, skill or aptitude.

name: Academic Degree
fact: A qualification awarded on completing a course of study in higher education.

name: Skill
fact: The learned or innate ability to act with determined results, within limited time or energy.

name: Pedagogy
fact: The study of how knowledge and skills are imparted in an educational context.

name: Information
fact: Something with the power to inform; any non-random observable pattern conveys some.

name: Data
fact: Values that convey information: quantities, qualities, facts, statistics, symbols.

name: Communication
fact: Commonly defined as the transmission of information.

name: Conversation
fact: Interactive communication between two or more people.

name: Nonverbal Communication
fact: Messages sent through signals that do not involve spoken or written words.

name: Body Language
fact: Physical behaviour, not words, used to convey information — mostly without awareness.

name: Culture
fact: The behaviour, institutions, norms, beliefs, arts and customs found in human societies.

name: Anthropology
fact: The scientific study of humanity, across biology and sociology, present and past.

name: Cultural Anthropology
fact: The branch of anthropology on cultural variation among humans.

name: Ethnography
fact: The systematic study of individual cultures, by watching how groups behave and how they interpret it.

name: Ethnicity
fact: A group whose members identify with each other on perceived shared attributes.

name: Nomad
fact: A community without fixed habitation that regularly moves to and from areas.

name: Cultural Heritage
fact: The tangible and intangible legacy of a group, inherited from past generations.

name: Popular Culture
fact: The practices, beliefs, art and objects dominant in a society at a given time.

name: Oral Tradition
fact: Knowledge, art and beliefs passed on by speech or song from one generation to the next.

name: Greeting
fact: An act of communication that makes one's presence known and suggests a relationship or status.

name: Body Modification
fact: The deliberate altering of the human anatomy or appearance.

name: Tattoo
fact: Ink or pigment inserted into the dermis to form a design.

name: Birthday
fact: The anniversary of a birth, celebrated with gifts, cards or a party.

name: Holiday
fact: A day or period set aside for festivals or recreation.

name: Carnival
fact: Public celebration before Lent — parades, street parties, indulgence.

name: Christmas
fact: A religious and cultural celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ, observed on 25 December.

name: Easter
fact: The culmination of the Passion of Jesus, after Lent's forty days of fasting and prayer.

name: Halloween
fact: "Saints' eve": the start of Allhallowtide, the time for remembering the dead.

name: Diwali
fact: The Hindu festival of lights — light over darkness, knowledge over ignorance.

name: New Year's Eve
fact: The evening of the last day of the year, 31 December in the Gregorian calendar.

name: Marriage
fact: A culturally and often legally recognised union between spouses.

name: Wedding
fact: A ceremony in which two people are united in marriage.

name: Humanities
fact: Academic disciplines that study human society and culture.

name: Social Science
fact: The branch of science devoted to societies and the relationships among their members.

name: Sociology
fact: The scientific study of human society, social behaviour and everyday culture.

name: Linguistics
fact: The scientific study of language.

name: Museum
fact: An institution that displays and preserves culturally or scientifically significant objects — originally a place for the Muses.

name: Civilization
fact: Dense settlements, hierarchy, a division of labour and a ruling elite.

name: Archive
fact: An accumulation of historical records, or the building that holds them.

name: Historical Method
fact: The techniques historians use to research and write histories of the past.

name: Stone Age
fact: About 3.4 million years in which stone was the main edge-making material.

name: Paleolithic
fact: The age of knapped stone tools, alongside wood and bone.

name: Mesolithic
fact: The last hunter-gatherer period between the Ice Age and farming.

name: Neolithic Revolution
fact: Humankind's first historically verifiable transition to agriculture.

name: Ancient History
fact: From the beginning of writing through late antiquity.

name: Pharaoh
fact: The monarch of ancient Egypt — the word once meant the king's administration.

name: Serfdom
fact: A condition of debt bondage to the lord of the manor whose land the serf worked.

name: Nobility
fact: A social class ranked immediately below royalty, in societies with an aristocracy.

name: Chivalry
fact: An informal code of conduct that developed in France between 1170 and 1220.

name: Age of Discovery
fact: The 15th to 17th centuries, when European seafarers explored, colonized and conquered across the globe.

name: Colonization
fact: The act or process of sending people to live in and govern another country.

name: Columbian Exchange
fact: The transfer of plants, animals and diseases between the Old World and the New after 1492.

name: Atlantic Slave Trade
fact: Operated by slave ships from Europe and the New World; most captives came from Central and West Africa.

name: Age of Enlightenment
fact: Reason, natural rights and empirical knowledge, spread through print.

name: Scientific Revolution
fact: The boundary between ancient thought and modern science.

name: French Revolution
fact: From the Estates General of 1789 to the coup of 18 Brumaire in 1799.

name: American Revolution
fact: A colonial rebellion that became a revolution and created the United States.

name: Great Depression
fact: A severe global economic downturn, 1929 to 1939.

name: Moon Landing
fact: Luna 2 touched the Moon first, in 1959; Apollo 11 landed a crew in 1969.

name: Information Age
fact: The shift from traditional industries to an economy built on information technology.

name: Green Revolution
fact: High-yielding cereals and chemical fertilisers that raised crop yields sharply.

name: Abolitionism
fact: The political movement to end slavery and liberate the enslaved.

name: Civil Rights Movement
fact: The US movement, 1954 to 1968, against legalised racial segregation and discrimination.

name: Inquisition
fact: A Catholic judicial procedure in which church judges investigated and tried cases.

name: Roman Empire
fact: The state that dominated the Mediterranean — its first emperor, Augustus, from 27 BC.

name: Ancient Egypt
fact: A cradle of civilization along the lower Nile, at its peak in the New Kingdom.

name: Ancient Greece
fact: From the Greek Dark Ages to the end of classical antiquity.

name: Ancient Rome
fact: The Roman civilisation from the 8th century BC to the collapse of the West in the 5th century AD.

name: Mesopotamia
fact: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates, site of the earliest Neolithic Revolution.

name: Hanseatic League
fact: A medieval network of merchant guilds and market towns in northern Europe.

name: Holy Roman Empire
fact: A decentralised polity of central Europe that lasted until 1806.

name: Little Ice Age
fact: A regional cooling, strongest in the North Atlantic — not a true ice age.

name: Spanish Flu
fact: The 1918–1920 H1N1 pandemic, with an estimated 17 to 50 million deaths.

name: Human History
fact: The record of humankind from prehistory to the present.

name: Artist
fact: A person who creates art or practises the arts.

name: Genre
fact: A style or form of art or communication with socially agreed conventions.

name: Novel
fact: An extended work of narrative fiction, usually in prose and published as a book.

name: Fable
fact: A short story whose animals or objects speak, to illustrate a moral lesson.

name: Fairy Tale
fact: A short story from the folklore genre.

name: Fantasy
fact: Speculative fiction with supernatural or magical elements, imaginary realms and creatures.

name: Science Fiction
fact: Speculative fiction that imagines advanced changes in technology, science or biology.

name: Horror Fiction
fact: A genre meant to disturb, frighten or scare an audience.

name: Short Story
fact: Narrative fiction in prose, short enough to read in a single sitting.

name: Biography
fact: A detailed account of a person's life.

name: Autobiography
fact: A self-written account of one's own life.

name: Diary
fact: A record with discrete entries arranged by date.

name: Dictionary
fact: A listing of the words of a language, often arranged alphabetically.

name: Encyclopedia
fact: A reference work giving summaries of knowledge, arranged in articles.

name: Essay
fact: A piece of writing that gives the author's own argument.

name: Epic Poetry
fact: A lengthy narrative poem about the deeds of extraordinary characters.

name: Haiku
fact: A short-form poem that originated in Japan.

name: Rhyme
fact: Repetition of similar sounds in the final stressed syllables of words.

name: Sonnet
fact: A fixed poetic form of fourteen lines with a set rhyming scheme, from 13th-century Sicily.

name: Ode
fact: A lyric poem from Ancient Greece that praises an event or individual.

name: Writer
fact: A person who uses written words to communicate ideas, inspire feelings or entertain.

name: Literature
fact: Any collection of written work — more narrowly, writing considered an art form.

name: Prose
fact: Language in its natural flow of speech, without regular rhythm — not verse.

name: Narration
fact: Written or spoken commentary that conveys a story to an audience.

name: Drama
fact: The mode of fiction represented in performance: a play, opera, mime or ballet.

name: Tragedy
fact: A genre of drama based on human suffering and terrible events befalling its characters.

name: Choir
fact: A musical ensemble of singers, often tied to a church.

name: Concert
fact: A live performance of music in front of an audience.

name: Musician
fact: Someone who composes, conducts or performs music.

name: Music Theory
fact: The study of theoretical frameworks for understanding music.

name: Singing
fact: The art of creating music with the voice — the oldest form of musical expression.

name: Ballad
fact: A form of verse, often a narrative set to music.

name: Hymn
fact: A song of adoration or prayer, addressed to a deity.

name: Lullaby
fact: A soothing song for children — sometimes a way to pass down tradition.

name: National Anthem
fact: A patriotic composition evoking the history and traditions of a nation.

name: Folk Music
fact: Music transmitted orally, with unknown composers, changing between generations.

name: Sonata
fact: A piece of three or four movements for one or more instruments.

name: Concerto
fact: An instrumental composition for one or more soloists accompanied by an orchestra.

name: Aria
fact: A self-contained piece for one voice, normally part of a larger work such as an opera.

name: Blues
fact: A music genre that began among African Americans in the Deep South around the 1860s.

name: Ballet
fact: A performance dance that began in the Italian Renaissance and developed in France and Russia.

name: Waltz
fact: A ballroom and folk dance in triple time, from 18th-century German-speaking Europe.

name: Circus
fact: A company of performers: clowns, acrobats, trained animals and more.

name: Puppetry
fact: Theatre with puppets animated by a human puppeteer.

name: Acting
fact: Telling a story by enacting it as a character.

name: Cubism
fact: An early-20th-century Paris movement: subjects analysed, broken up and reassembled.

name: Impressionism
fact: Visible brush strokes and accurate light in its changing qualities.

name: Surrealism
fact: Letting the unconscious mind express itself in illogical, dreamlike scenes.

name: Dada
fact: An international art movement that grew out of World War I.

name: Pop Art
fact: A mid-1950s movement of the UK and US that used mass-reproduction techniques.

name: Modernism
fact: An early-20th-century movement of experimentation, abstraction and subjective experience.

name: Romanticism
fact: Subjectivity, imagination and nature, against the Enlightenment and industrialisation.

name: Abstract Art
fact: Art that departs from the depiction of visible reality.

name: Calligraphy
fact: Fine handwriting as a visual art — "beautiful writing".

name: Collage
fact: Art assembled from different forms into a new whole — from the French for "to glue".

name: Comics
fact: A medium that expresses ideas with images, often combined with text.

name: Manga
fact: Comics or graphic novels originating from Japan.

name: Graffiti
fact: Writing or drawings on a wall, usually without permission and in public view.

name: Mural
fact: Artwork painted or applied directly to a wall or ceiling.

name: Mosaic
fact: Small pieces of coloured stone, glass or ceramic set in plaster to form an image.

name: Origami
fact: The art and technique of folding paper.

name: Portrait
fact: A representation of a person in which the face is predominant.

name: Printmaking
fact: Making artworks by transferring ink from a matrix to paper or another surface.

name: Watercolor
fact: Painting with pigments suspended in a water-based solution, usually on paper.

name: Illustration
fact: A decoration, interpretation or visual explanation of a text, concept or process.

name: Typography
fact: The art and technique of arranging type so written language is legible.

name: Graphic Design
fact: Creating visual communications that transmit specific messages to social groups.

name: Animation
fact: Pictures played in sequence to create the illusion of moving images.

name: Anime
fact: Animation produced in Japan.

name: Taxidermy
fact: The art of preserving an animal's body by mounting or stuffing it for display or study.

name: Violence
fact: The use of physical force to cause harm to other living beings.

name: Wealth
fact: Abundant financial assets or possessions that can be converted into a form used for transactions.

name: Poverty
fact: A state in which a person lacks the money and essentials for a basic standard of living.

name: Politics
fact: The activity of settling affairs in an organized society.

name: Political Science
fact: The scientific study of politics, governance and power.

name: Liberty
fact: Being free within society from restrictions imposed by authority.

name: Citizenship
fact: Membership in the political community of a sovereign state.

name: Civil Liberties
fact: Fundamental rights and freedoms that governments pledge not to restrict without due process.

name: Election
fact: A group decision-making process by which a population votes to choose officeholders.

name: Voting
fact: Making collective decisions by submitting and then adding up individual choices.

name: Political Party
fact: An organization that coordinates candidates to compete in elections and take part in governance.

name: Opinion Poll
fact: A survey of public opinion from a particular sample.

name: Diplomacy
fact: Communication by representatives of states to influence events in the international system.

name: International Relations
fact: The academic study of activities among states and other international actors.

name: International Law
fact: The rules and norms that states feel an obligation to obey in their mutual relations.

name: Globalization
fact: Increasing interdependence and integration among the economies, markets and cultures of different countries.

name: Imperialism
fact: Maintaining and extending power over foreign nations.

name: Coup d'État
fact: An illegal and overt attempt to unseat an incumbent leadership.

name: Riot
fact: A form of civil disorder marked by public violence against authority or property.

name: Protest
fact: A public act of objection, disapproval or dissent.

name: Activism
fact: Efforts to promote, impede or direct social, political, economic or environmental reform.

name: Social Movement
fact: A loosely organized effort by many people to achieve a social or political goal.

name: Autocracy
fact: A form of government in which absolute power is held by one person.

name: Dictatorship
fact: A form of government led by someone who holds absolute or near-absolute power.

name: Absolute Monarchy
fact: A monarchy in which the sovereign is the sole source of political power.

name: Constitutional Monarchy
fact: A monarchy in which the monarch rules in accordance with a constitution.

name: Oligarchy
fact: A form of government in which power rests with a small number of people.

name: Theocracy
fact: A form of government in which deities are the supreme ruling authority.

name: Sovereign State
fact: A state with the highest authority over a territory.

name: Federation
fact: A union of partially self-governing provinces or states under a federal government.

name: Confederation
fact: A formal alliance of sovereign states united for common action.

name: Welfare State
fact: A government that protects the economic and social well-being of its citizens.

name: Legislature
fact: A deliberative assembly with the legal authority to make law.

name: Parliament
fact: A law-making body that represents the electorate and oversees the government.

name: Judiciary
fact: The system of courts that adjudicates legal disputes and applies the law.

name: Separation of Powers
fact: Keeping legislation, adjudication and execution institutionally distinct.

name: Public Policy
fact: The laws, regulations and actions a government uses to address social issues.

name: Ideology
fact: A set of ideals, values or beliefs held by a person or group.

name: Anarchism
fact: A political philosophy that seeks to abolish institutions of authority, coercion and hierarchy.

name: Authoritarianism
fact: A system that rejects political plurality and relies on strong central power.

name: Totalitarianism
fact: A system that completely controls the public and the private sphere of society.

name: Capitalism
fact: An economic system based on private ownership of the means of production for profit.

name: Communism
fact: An ideology seeking a classless society built on common ownership.

name: Marxism
fact: A political philosophy that analyses class relations and social conflict through historical materialism.

name: Socialism
fact: An ideology of social ownership of the means of production.

name: Conservatism
fact: A philosophy that seeks to preserve traditional institutions, customs and values.

name: Liberalism
fact: A philosophy built on individual rights, liberty and consent of the governed.

name: Libertarianism
fact: A philosophy that holds liberty and personal sovereignty as primary values.

name: Fascism
fact: A far-right, authoritarian, ultranationalist ideology of early 20th-century Europe.

name: Nationalism
fact: The idea that the nation should be congruent with the state.

name: Patriotism
fact: Love, devotion and attachment to one's country.

name: Populism
fact: Politics that emphasise the common people against a perceived elite.

name: Social Democracy
fact: A reformist, democratic approach to achieving social equality.

name: Multiculturalism
fact: The coexistence of multiple cultures in one society.

name: Social Equality
fact: A state in which everyone in society has equal rights, liberties and status.

name: Human Rights
fact: Moral principles that set standards of human behavior, belonging to everyone by being human.

name: Suffrage
fact: The right to vote in public political elections and referendums.

name: Racism
fact: The belief that human groups can be ranked by inherited traits, or prejudice against other ethnic groups.

name: Prejudice
fact: A preconceived, usually unfavourable, evaluation of someone based on their perceived group.

name: Discrimination
fact: Making unjustified distinctions between people based on the group they belong to.

name: Genocide
fact: The intentional partial or total destruction of a human group.

name: Crime
fact: An unlawful act punishable by a state or other authority.

name: Theft
fact: Taking another person's property without permission, intending to deprive the owner.

name: Murder
fact: The unlawful killing of another human without justification.

name: Fraud
fact: Intentional deception to deprive a victim of a legal right or to gain unfairly.

name: Robbery
fact: Taking or attempting to take anything of value by force, threat or fear.

name: Piracy
fact: Robbery or criminal violence by attackers on a ship or boat.

name: Smuggling
fact: The illegal and often covert transport of goods or people across a border.

name: Kidnapping
fact: The illegal relocation and confinement of a person against their will.

name: Torture
fact: The deliberate infliction of severe pain or suffering on a person.

name: Assassination
fact: The willful killing of a prominent person by sudden or secret attack, usually for political reasons.

name: Terrorism
fact: The use of violence against non-combatants to achieve political or ideological aims.

name: Corruption
fact: Dishonesty or crime by someone in authority to gain illicit benefits or abuse power.

name: Organized Crime
fact: Centralized enterprises that engage in and profit from illegal activities.

name: Court
fact: An institution with the authority to adjudicate legal disputes and administer justice.

name: Judge
fact: A public official who presides over court proceedings.

name: Jury
fact: A sworn body of people convened by a court to hear evidence and render a verdict.

name: Lawyer
fact: A person qualified to advise on the law and represent others in legal matters.

name: Police
fact: A body empowered by a state to enforce the law and protect public order.

name: Trial
fact: Parties to a dispute presenting evidence in a tribunal with authority to adjudicate.

name: Witness
fact: Someone who provides testimonial evidence of what they know or claim to know.

name: Appeal
fact: Review of a case or decision by a higher authority.

name: Statute
fact: A law or formal written enactment of a legislature.

name: Precedent
fact: A judicial decision that serves as authority for courts deciding similar later cases.

name: Common Law
fact: Law developed through judicial decisions rather than statutes.

name: Criminal Law
fact: The body of law that relates to crime.

name: Intellectual Property
fact: Intangible creations of the human intellect, and the rights to control their use.

name: Copyright
fact: The exclusive legal right to copy, distribute, adapt and perform a creative work.

name: Patent
fact: The legal right to exclude others from making, using or selling an invention for a limited time.

name: Inheritance
fact: Receiving property, titles, debts and rights upon the death of an individual.

name: Will and Testament
fact: A legal document stating how a person's property is to be distributed after death.

name: Capital Punishment
fact: The state-sanctioned killing of a person as punishment for misconduct.

name: Rule of Law
fact: The principle that the law is clear and open, and binds institutions as well as individuals.

name: Jurisprudence
fact: The philosophy of law.

name: Lawsuit
fact: A civil proceeding by a plaintiff against a defendant in a court of law.

name: News
fact: Information about current events.

name: Journalism
fact: Producing and distributing reports on the "news of the day".

name: Mass Media
fact: Forms of media that reach large audiences via mass communication.

name: Propaganda
fact: Mass communication used to influence an audience and further an agenda.

name: Censorship
fact: The suppression of speech, public communication or other information.

name: Public Relations
fact: Managing and disseminating information to the public to influence their perception.

name: Publishing
fact: Making information, literature, music and other content available to the public.

name: Magazine
fact: A periodical publication on a regular schedule with subject-oriented text and visuals.

name: Social Media
fact: Technologies for creating, sharing and aggregating content among virtual communities.

name: Academic Journal
fact: A periodical in which scholarship on an academic discipline is published.

name: Cartoon
fact: A drawn, unrealistic or semi-realistic image, often for satire, humor or animation.

name: Internet Meme
fact: A cultural item that spreads across the internet, now mainly through social media.

name: Personality
fact: The pattern of behaviour, thought and feeling that makes one person distinct from another.

name: Personality Psychology
fact: The branch of psychology that studies personality and how individuals differ.

name: Evolutionary Psychology
fact: An approach that explains the mind and behaviour as adaptations shaped by evolution.

name: Human Nature
fact: The characteristic ways of thinking, feeling and acting that humans share.

name: Human Behavior
fact: How people respond, mentally, physically and socially, to the world around them.

name: Cognition
fact: The mental processes that acquire, store, retrieve and use knowledge.

name: Cognitive Development
fact: How a child's thinking, perception, language and problem-solving grow.

name: Creativity
fact: The ability to produce new and valuable ideas or works.

name: Imagination
fact: Forming pictures and ideas in the mind without input from the senses.

name: Introspection
fact: Looking inward at one's own thoughts and feelings.

name: Hypnosis
fact: A state of focused attention and heightened response to suggestion.

name: Feeling
fact: A subjective experience, close to but not the same as emotion.

name: Mood
fact: A lasting emotional state, less specific and less intense than an emotion.

name: Bias
fact: A leaning for or against something that is unfair or inaccurate.

name: Stereotype
fact: A generalised belief about everyone in a particular group.

name: Sadness
fact: Emotional pain linked to loss, disappointment and sorrow.

name: Shame
fact: The painful feeling of having fallen short of social and personal standards.

name: Guilt
fact: The feeling of having broken one's own moral standards and being responsible for it.

name: Embarrassment
fact: Discomfort felt when a socially awkward act is seen by others.

name: Shyness
fact: Social inhibition and apprehension in new situations.

name: Anxiety
fact: Dread about something that may happen in the future.

name: Boredom
fact: Uninterest in one's surroundings, often from lack of anything to do.

name: Courage
