name: Scientific Theory
fact: An explanation of an aspect of the natural world that has been repeatedly tested and has corroborating evidence.

name: Scientific Law
fact: A statement, based on repeated experiments or observations, that describes or predicts natural phenomena.

name: Scientific Modelling
fact: The making of models of objects and processes to make part of the world easier to understand or simulate.

name: Research
fact: Creative and systematic work undertaken to increase the stock of knowledge.

name: Laboratory
fact: A facility with controlled conditions for scientific or technological research, experiments and measurement.

name: Accuracy & Precision
fact: Accuracy is how close a measurement is to the true value; precision is how close measurements are to each other.

name: Metrology
fact: The scientific study of measurement, which establishes a common understanding of units.

name: Unit of Measurement
fact: A definite magnitude of a quantity, adopted by convention or law as a standard for measuring that quantity.

name: Metric System
fact: A decimal system of measurement built on base units and unit prefixes such as kilo and milli.

name: SI Units
fact: The modern form of the metric system and the world's most widely used system of measurement.

name: Second
fact: The base unit of time, derived from the division of the day.

name: Minute
fact: A unit of time, sixty of which make an hour.

name: Week
fact: A unit of time equal to seven days.

name: Inch
fact: A unit of length in the British Imperial and United States customary systems.

name: Cubit
fact: An ancient unit of length: the distance from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger.

name: Mile
fact: A British imperial and United States customary unit of length.

name: Nautical Mile
fact: A unit of length used in air, marine and space navigation.

name: Acre
fact: A unit of land area in the British imperial and United States customary systems.

name: Hectare
fact: A metric unit of area used mainly for land.

name: Gallon
fact: A unit of volume in British imperial and United States customary units.

name: Calorie
fact: A unit of energy that originated from the caloric theory of heat.

name: Electronvolt
fact: A unit of energy: that gained by one electron accelerating through a potential difference of one volt.

name: Joule
fact: The SI unit of energy.

name: Watt
fact: The SI unit of power, the rate of energy transfer.

name: Newton
fact: The SI unit of force.

name: Kilogram
fact: The SI base unit of mass, equal to one thousand grams.

name: Ampere
fact: The SI unit of electric current.

name: Volt
fact: The SI unit of electric potential, potential difference and electromotive force.

name: Ohm
fact: The SI unit of electrical resistance, named after the German physicist Georg Ohm.

name: Hertz
fact: The SI unit of frequency: one cycle per second.

name: Decibel
fact: A relative unit expressing the ratio of two powers on a logarithmic scale; a tenth of a bel.

name: Celsius
fact: The unit of temperature on the Celsius scale, once called centigrade.

name: Fahrenheit
fact: A temperature scale proposed by Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit.

name: Radian
fact: The SI unit of angle, defined by an arc equal in length to the radius.

name: Astronomy
fact: The natural science that studies celestial objects and the phenomena of the cosmos.

name: Astronomical Object
fact: A naturally occurring physical entity, association or structure that exists within the universe.

name: Astrophysics
fact: The science that applies physics and chemistry to astronomical objects and the universe.

name: Extraterrestrial Life
fact: Life that originates from another world rather than on Earth; none has yet been detected.

name: Observatory
fact: A location used for observing terrestrial, marine or celestial events.

name: Luminosity
fact: An absolute measure of radiated electromagnetic energy per unit time.

name: Apparent Magnitude
fact: A measure of the brightness of an astronomical object.

name: Interplanetary Medium
fact: The mass and energy that fills the Solar System, through which the planets and other bodies move.

name: Canopus
fact: The brightest star in the constellation Carina and second-brightest in the night sky.

name: Galactic Center
fact: The barycenter of the Milky Way, around a supermassive black hole.

name: Sagittarius A*
fact: The supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way.

name: Large Magellanic Cloud
fact: A dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

name: Small Magellanic Cloud
fact: A dwarf irregular galaxy near the Milky Way.

name: Triangulum Galaxy
fact: A spiral galaxy in the constellation Triangulum.

name: Centaurus A
fact: A galaxy in the constellation Centaurus.

name: Messier 87
fact: A supergiant elliptical galaxy in the constellation Virgo.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy
fact: A face-on spiral galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major.

name: Carina Nebula
fact: A large, complex nebula in the constellation Carina.

name: Eagle Nebula
fact: A young open cluster of stars in the constellation Serpens.

name: Horsehead Nebula
fact: A small dark nebula in the constellation Orion.

name: Cygnus X-1
fact: The first X-ray source widely accepted to be a black hole.

name: Hyades
fact: The nearest open star cluster.

name: Omega Centauri
fact: The largest known globular cluster in the Milky Way.

name: Celestial Mechanics
fact: The branch of astronomy dealing with the motions and gravitational interactions of objects in space.

name: Barycenter
fact: The centre of mass around which two or more bodies orbit.

name: Kepler's Laws
fact: Three laws describing the orbits of planets around the Sun.

name: Lagrange Point
fact: Points of equilibrium for a small object under the gravity of two massive orbiting bodies.

name: Orbital Mechanics
fact: The application of ballistics and celestial mechanics to rockets, satellites and other spacecraft.

name: Geostationary Orbit
fact: A circular orbit above the equator that keeps a satellite over one spot on Earth.

name: Low Earth Orbit
fact: An orbit close to Earth, used by many satellites and crewed spacecraft.

name: Gravity Assist
fact: A spaceflight flyby that uses a planet's gravity and motion to alter a spacecraft's path and speed.

name: Gravitational Acceleration
fact: The acceleration of an object in free fall in a vacuum.

name: Celestial Sphere
fact: An abstract sphere of arbitrarily large radius, concentric to Earth, on which all objects in the sky can be projected.

name: Astronomical Coordinate Systems
fact: Systems for specifying the positions of celestial objects relative to a reference frame.

name: Equinox
fact: The moment when the Sun appears directly above the equator.

name: Solstice
fact: The time when the Sun reaches its most northerly or southerly path; it happens twice a year.

name: Astrometry
fact: The branch of astronomy that makes precise measurements of the positions and movements of stars.

name: Albedo
fact: The fraction of sunlight that a body diffusely reflects.

name: Cosmic Distance Ladder
fact: The succession of methods by which astronomers measure the distances to celestial objects.

name: Outer Space
fact: The expanse that exists beyond Earth's atmosphere and between celestial bodies.

name: Stellar Black Hole
fact: A black hole formed by the gravitational collapse of a star.

name: Cosmic Ray
fact: High-energy particles, mostly protons or atomic nuclei, that move through space at nearly the speed of light.

name: Interstellar Medium
fact: The matter and radiation that exists in the space between the star systems in a galaxy.

name: Dark Nebula
fact: An interstellar cloud so dense that it obscures the light of objects behind it.

name: Great Attractor
fact: A region of enhanced gravitational attraction in the local universe.

name: Galaxy Classification
fact: A system for dividing galaxies into groups by their visual appearance, shape and structure.

name: Irregular Galaxy
fact: A galaxy that does not have a distinct regular shape, unlike a spiral or an elliptical galaxy.

name: Dwarf Galaxy
fact: A small galaxy of up to several billion stars.

name: Blazar
fact: An active galactic nucleus with a relativistic jet directed very nearly towards an observer.

name: Physical Cosmology
fact: The branch of physics that models the universe from the laws of physics.

name: Chronology of the Universe
fact: The history and future of the universe according to physical cosmology.

name: Fate of the Universe
fact: A topic in physical cosmology: the possible scenarios for how the universe will end.

name: Solar System Formation
fact: How the Sun and planets formed from the collapse of a giant molecular cloud.

name: Cosmological Constant
fact: A coefficient Einstein added to his field equations of general relativity, later revived to express the energy density of space.

name: Terrestrial Planet
fact: A planet composed primarily of silicate, rocks or metals.

name: Giant Planet
fact: A planet much larger than Earth, sometimes called a Jovian planet.

name: Natural Satellite
fact: An astronomical body that orbits a planet, dwarf planet or small Solar System body: a moon.

name: Minor Planet
fact: An astronomical object in direct orbit around the Sun that is classified as neither a planet nor a comet.

name: Meteor Shower
fact: A celestial event in which meteors seem to radiate from one point in the night sky.

name: Impact Event
fact: A collision between astronomical objects causing measurable effects.

name: Ring System
fact: A disc or torus of solid chunks of ice, rock and dust orbiting an astronomical object.

name: Variable Star
fact: A star whose brightness as seen from Earth changes systematically with time.

name: Gamma-ray Burst
fact: An extremely energetic event in a distant galaxy, the brightest class of explosion in the universe.

name: Nova
fact: A transient event that causes the sudden appearance of a bright, apparently new star that slowly fades.

name: Star System
fact: A small number of stars that orbit each other, bound by gravitational attraction.

name: Planetary System
fact: A set of non-stellar bodies gravitationally bound to and orbiting a star or star system.

name: Star Cluster
fact: A group of stars that share an origin and are held together by gravity.

name: Stellar Evolution
fact: The process by which a star changes over the course of time.

name: Starburst Galaxy
fact: A galaxy forming stars at an exceptionally high rate.

name: Wolf–Rayet Star
fact: A rare kind of star whose spectrum shows broad emission lines of ionised helium, nitrogen or carbon.

name: Stellar Kinematics
fact: The study or measurement of the motions of stars through space.

name: Stellar Magnetic Field
fact: A magnetic field generated by the motion of conductive plasma inside a star.

name: Stellar Structure
fact: Models describing the internal structure of a star and predicting its luminosity, colour and evolution.

name: Metallicity
fact: The abundance of elements heavier than hydrogen and helium in an astronomical object.

name: Hertzsprung–Russell Diagram
fact: A scatter plot of stars showing the relation between their luminosities and their classifications or temperatures.

name: Inorganic Chemistry
fact: The branch of chemistry that studies inorganic and organometallic compounds, mainly those not based on carbon.

name: Physical Chemistry
fact: The study of chemical systems in terms of the principles of physics, such as motion, energy, force and time.

name: Electrochemistry
fact: The branch of physical chemistry concerned with the relationship between electrical potential difference and chemical change.

name: Environmental Chemistry
fact: The scientific study of the chemical and biochemical phenomena that occur in natural places.

name: Medicinal Chemistry
fact: The discipline at the intersection of chemistry and pharmacy that designs and develops drugs.

name: Nuclear Chemistry
fact: The sub-field of chemistry dealing with radioactivity, nuclear processes and transformations in atomic nuclei.

name: Nuclide
fact: A class of atoms defined by its numbers of protons and neutrons and its nuclear energy state.

name: Organometallic Chemistry
fact: The study of compounds with at least one chemical bond between a carbon atom of an organic molecule and a metal.

name: Phase Diagram
fact: A chart showing the conditions of pressure and temperature at which distinct phases occur and coexist at equilibrium.

name: Photochemistry
fact: The branch of chemistry concerned with the chemical effects of light.

name: Polymer Chemistry
fact: The sub-discipline of chemistry that focuses on the structures, synthesis and properties of polymers and macromolecules.

name: Quantum Chemistry
fact: A branch of physical chemistry that applies quantum mechanics to predict the properties of molecules and materials.

name: Materials Science
fact: An interdisciplinary field relating the structure of materials to their properties, to design materials for specific uses.

name: Alchemy
fact: An ancient branch of natural philosophy, once practised in China, India, the Muslim world and Europe.

name: Chemical Substance
fact: A unique form of matter with constant chemical composition and characteristic properties.

name: Amount of Substance
fact: A count of elementary entities, measured as a ratio to the Avogadro constant; the mole measures it.

name: Chemical Synthesis
fact: The artificial execution of chemical reactions to obtain one or more products.

name: Conservation of Mass
fact: The law that the mass of a closed system stays constant over time: mass is rearranged, not created or destroyed.

name: Acid–Base Reaction
fact: A chemical reaction between an acid and a base.

name: Chemical Equation
fact: The symbolic representation of a chemical reaction, with reactants on the left and products on the right.

name: Chemical Equilibrium
fact: The state in which reactants and products are present in concentrations with no further tendency to change with time.

name: Chemical Formula
fact: A notation for the composition and structure of a chemical compound, using element symbols for its atoms.

name: Chemical Kinetics
fact: The branch of physical chemistry concerned with the rates of chemical reactions.

name: Reaction Mechanism
fact: The step-by-step sequence of elementary reactions by which an overall chemical reaction occurs.

name: Substitution Reaction
fact: A reaction in which one functional group in a compound is replaced by another.

name: Intermolecular Force
fact: The force that mediates interaction between molecules, weak relative to the forces that hold a molecule together.

name: Valence Bond Theory
fact: A basic theory of chemical bonding in which atomic orbitals combine to give individual chemical bonds.

name: Chromatography
fact: A laboratory technique for separating a mixture into its components.

name: Analytical Chemistry
fact: The branch of chemistry that identifies the chemical composition of materials and quantifies the components of mixtures.

name: Spectroscopy
fact: The study that measures and interprets electromagnetic spectra as they interact with matter.

name: Absorption Spectroscopy
fact: Techniques that measure the absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a sample as a function of frequency or wavelength.

name: Mass Spectrometry
fact: An analytical technique that measures the mass-to-charge ratio of ions.

name: Atomic Number
fact: The number of protons in the nucleus of every atom of an element.

name: Atomic Mass
fact: The mass of a single atom, mostly from its protons and neutrons.

name: Synthetic Element
fact: A chemical element that does not occur naturally on Earth and was made by human manipulation of particles.

name: Inorganic Compound
fact: A compound that lacks carbon–hydrogen bonds; that is, not an organic compound.

name: Organic Compound
fact: A compound of carbon; defined as the subject matter of organic chemistry.

name: Water Vapor
fact: The gaseous phase of water, produced by evaporation, boiling or the sublimation of ice.

name: Carbonate
fact: A salt of carbonic acid, containing the carbonate ion.

name: Calcium Carbonate
fact: The compound found in chalk, limestone, eggshells and shells.

name: Silicate
fact: Any of a family of anions made of silicon and oxygen.

name: Haloalkane
fact: An alkane in which one or more hydrogens are replaced by halogens.

name: Organophosphorus Chemistry
fact: The study of the synthesis and properties of organic compounds containing phosphorus.

name: Organosilicon Chemistry
fact: The study of organometallic compounds containing carbon–silicon bonds.

name: Organosulfur Chemistry
fact: The study of the properties and synthesis of organic compounds that contain sulfur.

name: Amide
fact: A compound whose functional group links amino acids into proteins as peptide bonds.

name: Amine
fact: An organic compound with carbon–nitrogen bonds, formed from ammonia.

name: Alcohol
fact: An organic compound with at least one hydroxyl group bound to a saturated carbon atom.

name: Aldehyde
fact: An organic compound containing a formyl functional group.

name: Carboxylic Acid
fact: A polar organic acid that contains a carboxyl group.

name: Alkane
fact: An acyclic saturated hydrocarbon: hydrogen and carbon atoms joined by single bonds.

name: Alkene
fact: A hydrocarbon containing one or more carbon–carbon double bonds.

name: Alkyne
fact: An unsaturated hydrocarbon with at least one carbon–carbon triple bond.

name: Aromatic Compound
fact: An organic compound with a chemistry typified by benzene.

name: Aerosol
fact: A suspension of fine solid particles or liquid droplets in a gas.

name: Dispersion
fact: A system in which particles of one material are dispersed in a continuous phase of another material.

name: Gel
fact: A semi-solid, from soft and weak to hard and tough, that shows no flow when in a steady state.

name: Syngas
fact: A mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide in various ratios.

name: Atomic Orbital
fact: A function describing the location and wave-like behaviour of an electron in an atom.

name: History of Atomic Theory
fact: The scientific theory that matter is composed of particles called atoms, and how the idea changed.

name: Binding Energy
fact: The smallest amount of energy required to remove a particle from a system or to disassemble it into parts.

name: Bohr Model
fact: An obsolete model of the atom with early quantum concepts, built on Rutherford's discovery of the nucleus.

name: Electron Configuration
fact: The distribution of an atom's electrons among its orbitals.

name: Electron Shell
fact: An orbit that electrons follow around an atom's nucleus.

name: Energy Level
fact: A discrete value of energy that a bound quantum mechanical system can take.

name: Rutherford Scattering
fact: Experiments showing that every atom has a nucleus holding all its positive charge and most of its mass.

name: Molecular Orbital
fact: A mathematical function describing the location and wave-like behaviour of an electron in a molecule.

name: Molecular Orbital Theory
fact: A method for describing the electronic structure of molecules using quantum mechanics.

name: Phase Transition
fact: The transition of a medium between states, such as solid, liquid and gas.

name: Phase of Matter
fact: A region of material that is chemically uniform, physically distinct and often mechanically separable.

name: Critical Point
fact: The end point of a phase equilibrium curve, such as the liquid–vapor critical point.

name: Triple Point
fact: The temperature and pressure at which the gas, liquid and solid phases of a substance coexist in equilibrium.

name: Crystallography
fact: The branch of science that studies molecular and crystalline structure.

name: Crystallization
fact: A process that leads to solids with a uniform pattern of atoms or molecules: a crystal.

name: Amorphous Solid
fact: A solid that lacks the long-range order characteristic of a crystal.

name: Vapor
fact: A substance in the gas phase below its critical temperature, which can be condensed by pressure alone.

name: Theoretical Physics
fact: A branch of physics that uses mathematical models to explain and predict natural phenomena.

name: Classical Mechanics
fact: The theory describing the effect of forces on the motion of macroscopic objects, without quantum effects.

name: Motion
fact: The change in position of an object or fluid with respect to a reference frame over time.

name: Mechanics
fact: The area of physics concerned with the relationships between force, matter and motion.

name: Kinematics
fact: The study of the geometry of the motion of objects, independent of the forces that set them in motion.

name: Statics
fact: The branch of classical mechanics that analyses force and torque on a system in equilibrium.

name: Newton's Laws of Motion
fact: Three physical laws relating the motion of an object to the forces acting on it.

name: Equations of Motion
fact: Equations that describe the behaviour of a physical system in terms of its motion as a function of time.

name: Moment of Inertia
fact: A measure of how difficult it is to change the rotation rate of a rigid body about an axis.

name: Impulse
fact: The change in momentum of an object, typically from a force acting over a short time.

name: Angular Momentum
fact: The rotational analogue of linear momentum, a conserved quantity.

name: Centripetal Force
fact: The force that makes a body follow a curved path.

name: Frame of Reference
fact: An abstract coordinate system whose origin, orientation and scale are specified in physical space.

name: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
fact: Gravity as a force: every particle attracts every other with a force growing with their masses and shrinking with distance squared.

name: Oscillation
fact: The repetitive or periodic variation of some measure about a central value, such as a swinging pendulum.

name: Harmonic Oscillator
fact: A system that, when displaced from equilibrium, feels a restoring force proportional to the displacement.

name: Simple Harmonic Motion
fact: Periodic motion under a restoring force proportional to the displacement from equilibrium.

name: Hamiltonian Mechanics
fact: A reformulation of Lagrangian mechanics that uses momenta in place of velocities.

name: Lagrangian Mechanics
fact: An alternate formulation of classical mechanics, founded on the principle of virtual work.

name: Ballistics
fact: The field of mechanics concerned with the launching, flight and impact of projectiles.

name: Relativistic Mechanics
fact: Mechanics that is compatible with special and general relativity.

name: Continuum Mechanics
fact: The mechanics of materials modelled as a continuous medium rather than as discrete particles.

name: Fluid Mechanics
fact: The branch of physics concerned with the mechanics of fluids and the forces on them.

name: Fluid Dynamics
fact: The subdiscipline of fluid mechanics that describes the flow of liquids and gases.

name: Aerodynamics
fact: The study of the motion of air, particularly around a solid object such as a wing.

name: Bernoulli's Principle
fact: A concept in fluid dynamics relating pressure, speed and height: faster flow means lower pressure.

name: Drag
fact: A force acting opposite to the direction of motion of an object moving through a fluid.

name: Flight
fact: The motion of an object through an atmosphere or the vacuum of space, without contacting any planetary surface.

name: Navier–Stokes Equations
fact: The equations describing the motion of viscous fluids.

name: Reynolds Number
fact: A number that predicts flow patterns from the ratio of inertial to viscous forces.

name: Turbulence
fact: Fluid motion with chaotic changes in pressure and flow velocity, in contrast to laminar flow.

name: Solid Mechanics
fact: The branch of continuum mechanics that studies the motion and deformation of solid materials under forces.

name: Deformation
fact: The change in size or shape of an object under force, elastic or plastic.

name: Elastic Modulus
fact: A quantity describing a substance's resistance to being deformed elastically when stress is applied.

name: Elasticity
fact: The ability of a body to resist a distorting influence and return to its original size and shape.

name: Hooke's Law
fact: The law that the force to stretch or compress a spring grows linearly with the distance.

name: Plasticity
fact: The ability of a solid to undergo permanent deformation in response to applied forces.

name: Stiffness
fact: The extent to which an object resists deformation under an applied force.

name: Strength of Materials
fact: The calculation of stresses and strains in structural members such as beams, columns and shafts.

name: Stress
fact: A physical quantity describing the forces present during deformation.

name: Statistical Mechanics
fact: A framework that applies statistics and probability to large assemblies of microscopic entities.

name: Laws of Thermodynamics
fact: A set of scientific laws defining physical quantities such as temperature, energy and entropy in thermodynamic systems.

name: Heat Capacity
fact: The amount of heat that must be supplied to an object to produce a unit change in its temperature.

name: Heat Transfer
fact: The generation, use, conversion and exchange of thermal energy between physical systems.

name: Enthalpy
fact: The sum of a thermodynamic system's internal energy and the product of its pressure and volume.

name: Black-Body Radiation
fact: The thermal electromagnetic radiation emitted by a body in thermodynamic equilibrium with its environment.

name: Internal Energy
fact: The energy of a thermodynamic system, excluding the kinetic energy of its motion.

name: Thermodynamic Cycle
fact: Linked sequences of thermodynamic processes that return a system to its initial state.

name: Free Energy
fact: A state function of a system whose change is the maximum work it can perform at constant temperature.

name: Explosion
fact: A rapid expansion in volume with an extreme outward release of energy, usually with high temperatures and gas pressures.

name: Acoustics
fact: The branch of mechanics that studies mechanical waves in gases, liquids and solids: vibration, sound and ultrasound.

name: Speed of Sound
fact: The distance travelled per unit of time by a sound wave through an elastic medium.

name: Ultrasound
fact: Sound with frequencies above the upper limit of human hearing.

name: Amplitude
fact: A measure of the change of a periodic variable in a single period.

name: Wave Interference
fact: The combining of two coherent waves by adding their displacements, giving greater or lower amplitude.

name: Noise
fact: Sound, chiefly unwanted, that is unpleasant, loud or disruptive.

name: Superposition Principle
fact: For linear systems, the net response to several stimuli is the sum of the responses to each alone.

name: Wave Equation
fact: A second-order linear partial differential equation describing waves such as sound, water and light.

name: Optics
fact: The branch of physics that studies the behaviour and detection of electromagnetic radiation, including visible light.

name: Focal Length
fact: A measure of how strongly an optical system converges or diverges light.

name: Polarization
fact: A property of transverse waves specifying the geometrical orientation of the oscillations.

name: Refractive Index
fact: The ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in a medium.

name: Transparency
fact: The property of allowing light to pass through a material without appreciable scattering.

name: Color Theory
fact: A body of knowledge describing colour mixing, contrast, harmony, schemes and symbolism.

name: Primary Color
fact: Colorants or coloured lights that can be mixed in varying amounts to produce a gamut of colours.

name: RGB Color Model
fact: An additive colour model in which red, green and blue light are added to reproduce a broad array of colours.

name: CMYK Color Model
fact: A subtractive colour model used in printing, with cyan, magenta, yellow and a black key plate.

name: Gloss
fact: An optical property of how well a surface reflects light in a mirror-like direction.

name: Ionizing Radiation
fact: Radiation with enough energy to knock electrons off atoms and molecules.

name: Gauge Theory
fact: A field theory whose equations stay unchanged under local transformations.

name: Quantum Gravity
fact: The search for a theory joining gravity with quantum mechanics.

name: Atomic Physics
fact: The branch of physics that studies atoms as electrons around a nucleus.

name: Condensed Matter Physics
fact: The physics of solids, liquids and other dense phases of matter.

name: Solid-State Physics
fact: The study of rigid matter, the largest branch of condensed matter physics.

name: Degenerate Matter
fact: Matter so dense that the Pauli exclusion principle holds a star up.

name: Bose–Einstein Condensate
fact: A state of matter in which cooled bosons share the lowest quantum state.

name: Magnetism
fact: The force by which magnetic fields make objects attract or repel.

name: Ferromagnetism
fact: The strong magnetism of iron and a few other materials, which can become permanent magnets.

name: Dipole
fact: A pair of separated opposite charges, or a tiny magnet.

name: Metamaterial
fact: A material whose properties come from its designed structure, not its chemistry.

name: Oil Drop Experiment
fact: Millikan and Fletcher's experiment that measured the charge of the electron.

name: Photoelectric Effect
fact: Light knocking electrons out of a material.

name: Electrostatics
fact: The physics of electric charges at rest.

name: Coulomb's Law
fact: The law giving the force between two charges at rest, falling with the square of distance.

name: Electric Field
fact: The field around a charge that pushes or pulls other charges.

name: Electric Potential
fact: The electric potential energy per unit of charge at each point in space.

name: Electromagnetic Radiation
fact: Self-propagating waves of the electromagnetic field, from radio waves to gamma rays.

name: Electromagnetic Spectrum
fact: The full range of electromagnetic radiation, sorted by frequency.

name: Radio Wave
fact: Electromagnetic waves with the longest wavelengths of all.

name: Microwave
fact: Electromagnetic waves shorter than radio waves but longer than infrared.

name: Infrared
fact: Electromagnetic radiation just beyond red light, felt as heat and invisible to the eye.

name: Visible Spectrum
fact: The band of electromagnetic radiation the human eye can see.

name: Fluorescence
fact: Light given off by a substance while it absorbs other light, such as ultraviolet.

name: Electromagnetic Field
fact: The combined electric and magnetic field acting on charges.

name: Electromotive Force
fact: The energy a source gives each unit of charge in a circuit, measured in volts.

name: Lorentz Force
fact: The force electric and magnetic fields exert on a moving charge.

name: Eddy Current
fact: Loops of current induced in a conductor by a changing magnetic field.

name: Magnetostatics
fact: The study of magnetic fields made by steady currents.

name: Alternating Current
fact: Electric current that keeps reversing direction.

name: Direct Current
fact: Electric charge flowing in one direction only.

name: Electrical Impedance
fact: A circuit's opposition to alternating current, combining resistance and reactance.

name: Resistance and Conductance
fact: How strongly an object resists current, and its reciprocal, how easily current passes.

name: Capacitance
fact: The ability of an object to store electric charge.

name: Gain
fact: How much a circuit, often an amplifier, increases the power or size of a signal.

name: Inductance
fact: A conductor's tendency to oppose changes in the current flowing through it.

name: Kirchhoff's Circuit Laws
fact: Two laws on current and voltage in circuits, from Gustav Kirchhoff.

name: Quantum Chromodynamics
fact: The theory of the strong force between quarks, carried by gluons.

name: Quantum Electrodynamics
fact: The quantum theory of how light and matter interact.

name: Quantum Entanglement
fact: Particles sharing one quantum state, even when far apart.

name: Quantum Field Theory
fact: The framework that joins field theory, special relativity and quantum mechanics.

name: Quantum Tunnelling
fact: A particle passing through a barrier it classically lacks the energy to cross.

name: Schrödinger Equation
fact: The equation governing how a quantum system's wave function changes.

name: Wave Function
fact: The mathematical description of a quantum system's state.

name: Wave–Particle Duality
fact: Photons and electrons show wave or particle behaviour depending on the experiment.

name: General Relativity
fact: Einstein's geometric theory of gravitation.

name: Special Relativity
fact: Einstein's theory of the relationship between space and time.

name: Principle of Relativity
fact: The idea that the laws of physics stay the same for every observer moving steadily.

name: Equivalence Principle
fact: The principle that gravitational and inertial mass are equivalent.

name: Gravitational Singularity
fact: A point where gravity is predicted to be so intense that spacetime breaks down.

name: Lorentz Transformation
fact: The transformations relating spacetime coordinates between frames moving at constant velocity.

name: Michelson–Morley Experiment
fact: The experiment that failed to detect the aether, the supposed carrier of light.

name: Speed of Light
fact: The speed of electromagnetic waves, greatest in a vacuum.

name: Nuclear Physics
fact: The physics of atomic nuclei and their interactions.

name: Nucleosynthesis
fact: The process that builds new atomic nuclei from protons, neutrons and older nuclei.

name: Beta Particle
fact: A fast electron or positron thrown out by a decaying nucleus.

name: Particle Physics
fact: The study of the fundamental particles and forces of matter and radiation.

name: Beyond the Standard Model
fact: Theories trying to explain what the Standard Model cannot.

name: String Theory
fact: A theory in which particles are tiny vibrating strings.

name: Supersymmetry
fact: A proposed symmetry pairing every particle with a partner of different spin.

name: Particle
fact: A separate part of a larger system, from electrons to grains of powder.

name: Particle Accelerator
fact: A machine that uses electromagnetic fields to speed particles into beams.

name: Tevatron
fact: A circular particle accelerator at Fermilab in Illinois.

name: Particle Detector
fact: A device that detects, tracks and identifies ionizing particles.

name: Cloud Chamber
fact: A sealed chamber of supersaturated vapor that shows the tracks of ionizing radiation.

name: Scattering
fact: Moving particles or radiation deflected from a straight path.

name: Subatomic Particle
fact: A particle smaller than an atom.

name: Gauge Boson
fact: A force-carrying elementary particle exchanged between fermions.

name: Antiparticle
fact: The partner of a particle with the same mass and opposite charges.

name: Earth Science
fact: The sciences that study the planet Earth and its spheres.

name: Natural Environment
fact: Everything living and non-living that occurs naturally.

name: Natural Resource
fact: Resources drawn from nature and used with few changes.

name: Natural Disaster
fact: The harm done to a society by a natural hazard such as a flood or earthquake.

name: Wildfire
fact: An unplanned, uncontrolled fire in an area of combustible vegetation.

name: Internal Structure of Earth
fact: The layers of Earth, from the rigid lithosphere down to the solid inner core.

name: Geology
fact: The science of the Earth, its rocks and how they change over time.

name: Lithosphere
fact: The rigid outermost rocky shell of a planet.

name: Stratigraphy
fact: The study of rock layers and layering.

name: Thrust Fault
fact: A break in the crust where older rock is pushed over younger rock.

name: Mineralogy
fact: The scientific study of minerals, their chemistry, structure and formation.

name: Pyroxene
fact: A group of rock-forming silicate minerals found in many igneous and metamorphic rocks.

name: Talc
fact: A soft clay mineral of hydrated magnesium silicate, ground into baby powder.

name: Jade
fact: Two different decorative rocks, nephrite and jadeite, both called jade.

name: Petrology
fact: The branch of geology that studies rocks and how they form.

name: Geodesy
fact: The science of measuring Earth's shape, gravity and orientation.

name: Geophysics
fact: The physics of Earth: its shape and its gravitational, magnetic and electromagnetic fields.

name: Earth's Inner Core
fact: The solid ball at the centre of the Earth, its innermost layer.

name: Earth's Magnetic Field
fact: The magnetic field reaching from Earth's interior into space, meeting the solar wind.

name: Seismology
fact: The scientific study of earthquakes and the elastic waves they send through the Earth.

name: Geomorphology
fact: The study of how landforms originate and evolve.

name: Landform
fact: A natural or human-made feature of a planet's solid surface.

name: Land
fact: The solid surface of Earth not covered by the ocean or other water.

name: Mountain Pass
fact: A navigable route through a mountain range or over a ridge.

name: Mountain Range
fact: A series of mountains arranged in a line and connected by high ground.

name: Hill
fact: A landform rising above the surrounding terrain, lower than a mountain.

name: Sedimentary Basin
fact: A sunken region of the crust where thick sediments pile up into rock.

name: Alluvial Fan
fact: A fan of sediment spreading out where a canyon meets open ground.

name: Rapids
fact: Steep stretches of river where the water speeds up and turns turbulent.

name: Glacial Landform
fact: A landform shaped by glaciers and ice sheets.

name: Bay
fact: A recessed coastal body of water joined to a larger one.

name: Hotspot
fact: A volcanic spot fed by unusually hot mantle beneath.

name: Artificial Island
fact: An island built by people instead of formed by nature.

name: Land Reclamation
fact: Making new land from sea, riverbeds or lake beds.

name: Polder
fact: Low-lying land enclosed by dikes.

name: History of Earth
fact: Earth's development from its formation to the present day.

name: Geological History of Earth
fact: Earth's major geological events placed on the geologic time scale.

name: Geochronology
fact: The science of dating rocks, fossils and sediments.

name: Late Ordovician Extinction
fact: The first of the big five mass extinctions.

name: Late Devonian Extinction
fact: One of the big five mass extinctions, at the Frasnian–Famennian boundary.

name: Triassic–Jurassic Extinction
fact: The mass extinction that ended the Triassic.

name: Precambrian
fact: Earth's early history, before the Cambrian.

name: Phanerozoic
fact: The current geologic eon, from the Cambrian to today.

name: Paleozoic
fact: The first era of the Phanerozoic, before the Mesozoic.

name: Cambrian
fact: The first period of the Paleozoic Era.

name: Permian
fact: The last period of the Paleozoic Era.

name: Mesozoic
fact: The era of the dinosaurs: Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous.

name: Triassic
fact: The first and shortest period of the Mesozoic Era.

name: Jurassic
fact: The Mesozoic period between the Triassic and Cretaceous.

name: Cretaceous
fact: The third and last period of the Mesozoic Era, and its longest.

name: Cenozoic
fact: Earth's current geological era, the age of mammals.

name: Paleogene
fact: The first period of the Cenozoic Era.

name: Neogene
fact: The second period of the Cenozoic Era.

name: Quaternary
fact: The current period of the Cenozoic Era, the age of ice ages.

name: Holocene
fact: The current geological epoch, since the last ice age.

name: Shrubland
fact: A plant community dominated by shrubs.

name: Jungle
fact: Land covered with dense forest and tangled vegetation, usually in the tropics.

name: Temperate Forest
fact: A temperate-climate habitat of broadleaf and mixed forest.

name: Marsh
fact: A wetland dominated by herbaceous plants, not woody ones.

name: Pedosphere
fact: The soil layer of the Earth's crust, where the spheres meet.

name: Soil Fertility
fact: The ability of soil to sustain plant growth and good yields.

name: Soil Science
fact: The study of soil as a natural resource.

name: Air Mass
fact: A large volume of air defined by its temperature and humidity.

name: Atmospheric Pressure
fact: The pressure of the air in Earth's atmosphere.

name: Atmospheric Science
fact: The study of Earth's atmosphere and its physical processes.

name: Ozone Depletion
fact: The thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer, worst over the poles in spring.

name: Mirage
fact: An optical illusion in which refraction bends light into a displaced image.

name: Climatology
fact: The scientific study of Earth's climate.

name: Climate Change
fact: The long-term warming of the planet and its wider effects on the climate.

name: Climate Variability
fact: Climate variations beyond single weather events, and those lasting decades or more.

name: El Niño–Southern Oscillation
fact: Pacific Ocean temperature swings between warm El Niño and cool La Niña.

name: Köppen Climate Classification
fact: A system sorting Earth's climates into five main groups.

name: Weather Forecasting
fact: Using science and technology to predict the atmosphere for a place and time.

name: Low-Pressure Area
fact: A region where air pressure is lower than its surroundings.

name: High-Pressure Area
fact: A region where air pressure is higher than its surroundings, also called an anticyclone.

name: Precipitation
fact: Water that condenses in the air and falls from clouds as rain, snow or hail.

name: Summer
fact: The hottest and brightest temperate season, between spring and autumn.

name: Autumn
fact: The temperate season between summer and winter, also called fall.

name: Winter
fact: The coldest, darkest season, when the hemisphere tilts away from the Sun.

name: Dry Season
fact: The yearly period of low rainfall, especially in the tropics.

name: Wet Season
fact: The time of year when most of a region's rain falls.

name: Atmospheric Circulation
fact: The large-scale movement of air that spreads heat around the Earth.

name: Cyclone
fact: A large air mass spiralling inward around a centre of low pressure.

name: Hadley Cell
fact: The tropical air circulation that rises at the equator and sinks in the subtropics.

name: Polar Vortex
fact: A large region of cold, rotating air encircling a pole.

name: Walker Circulation
fact: A model of tropical air flow in a closed loop across the Pacific.

name: Dust Storm
fact: Strong wind lifting loose sand and dirt from a dry surface.

name: Hydrosphere
fact: All the water on, under and above the surface of a planet.

name: Cryosphere
fact: The parts of Earth where water is frozen solid.

name: Ice Shelf
fact: A large platform of glacial ice floating on the ocean.

name: Oceanography
fact: The scientific study of the ocean.

name: Sea Level
fact: The average level of the sea, from which heights are measured.

name: Seabed
fact: The bottom of the ocean.

name: Hydrology
fact: The scientific study of how water moves, is distributed and managed.

name: Body of Water
fact: A significant accumulation of water on Earth's surface.

name: Hydrography
fact: The measurement and description of oceans, seas, lakes and rivers, chiefly for safe navigation.

name: Limnology
fact: The study of inland waters such as lakes.

name: Dry Lake
fact: A basin that once held a lake, left dry when evaporation outpaced recharge.

name: Drainage Basin
fact: An area of land whose surface water all drains to one point.

name: Abiogenesis
fact: The natural process by which life arises from non-living matter.

name: Marine Life
fact: All the organisms that live in the salt water of seas and oceans.

name: Model Organism
fact: A species studied in depth to learn how other organisms work.

name: Biology
fact: The scientific study of life and living organisms.

name: Microbiology
fact: The scientific study of microorganisms.

name: Mycology
fact: The branch of biology that studies fungi.

name: Biomechanics
fact: The mechanics of living things, from whole bodies down to proteins.

name: Neuroscience
fact: The scientific study of the nervous system.

name: Sense
fact: A biological system for gathering information about the surroundings.

name: Paleontology
fact: The scientific study of past life, mainly through fossils.

name: History of Life
fact: How living and extinct organisms evolved, from the first life to today.

name: Human Genome
fact: The complete set of human DNA sequences.

name: Hybrid
fact: The offspring of two different varieties, species or genera.

name: Phylogenetics
fact: The study of the evolutionary history and relationships of organisms.

name: Anatomy
fact: The study of the structure of organisms and their parts.

name: Dissection
fact: Cutting apart a dead body to study its structure.

name: Ganglion
fact: A cluster of nerve cell bodies in the peripheral nervous system.

name: Sensory Nervous System
fact: The part of the nervous system that processes sensory information.

name: Auditory System
fact: The sensory system for hearing, ears included.

name: Taste
fact: The sense that detects chemicals in the mouth, mostly on the tongue.

name: Olfactory System
fact: The sensory system for the sense of smell.

name: Sense of Smell
fact: The special sense through which smells are perceived.

name: Odor
fact: A smell caused by volatile chemical compounds in the air.

name: Somatosensory System
fact: The sensory system of touch, body position and balance.

name: Visual System
fact: The body system that detects and interprets light to build an image.

name: Visual Perception
fact: The ability to detect light and form an image from it.

name: Color Vision
fact: The ability to tell apart light of different frequencies.

name: Fingerprint
fact: The impression left by the friction ridges of a finger.

name: Fur
fact: The soft, thick hair that covers most mammals.

name: Whiskers
fact: Sensitive hairs that mammals use to feel their surroundings.

name: Pelvis
fact: The lower part of the trunk and the bones inside it.

name: Spinal Column
fact: The backbone, defining feature of the vertebrates.

name: Plant Anatomy
fact: The study of the internal structure of plants.

name: Plant Morphology
fact: The study of the form and external structure of plants.

name: Shrub
fact: A small to medium woody plant with several stems.

name: Vascular Tissue
fact: The xylem and phloem that carry water and food through a plant.

name: Hypha
fact: The long, branching thread that a fungus grows from.

name: Biochemistry
fact: The study of chemical processes within living organisms.

name: Chemical Biology
fact: Using chemistry and small molecules to study living systems.

name: Molecular Biology
fact: The study of the molecules behind biological activity, chiefly nucleic acids and proteins.

name: Biomolecule
fact: A molecule made by a living organism and essential to its processes.

name: Alkaloid
fact: Natural organic compounds that contain nitrogen.

name: Biological Pigment
fact: A coloured substance made by a living organism.

name: Carotenoid
fact: The yellow, orange and red pigments of carrots, tomatoes and flamingos.

name: Plant Hormone
fact: Signal molecules that control a plant's growth and development.

name: Lipid
fact: Fats, waxes and related compounds that store energy and form cell membranes.

name: Physiology
fact: The scientific study of how living systems function.

name: Blood Sugar Level
fact: The amount of glucose in the blood, tightly regulated by the body.

name: Excretion
fact: The removal of metabolic waste from an organism.

name: Defecation
fact: The elimination of solid waste from the digestive tract.

name: Urination
fact: The release of urine from the bladder.

name: Biological Sex
fact: Whether an organism produces large or small gametes.

name: Female
fact: The sex that produces the larger gamete, the egg cell.

name: Male
fact: The sex that produces the smaller gamete, sperm.

name: Fertilisation
fact: The fusion of gametes into a zygote that develops into a new organism.

name: Microbial Cyst
fact: A dormant resting stage of a microorganism.

name: Menopause
fact: The time when menstrual periods stop for good.

name: Plant Reproduction
fact: How plants reproduce, sexually by gametes or by cloning themselves.

name: Developmental Biology
fact: The study of how animals and plants grow and develop.

name: Human Development
fact: The growth of a human from fertilisation to maturity.

name: Imago
fact: The adult, final stage of an insect's metamorphosis.

name: Longevity
fact: How long the longest-lived members of a population live.

name: Ontogeny
fact: The development of an organism from fertilised egg to adult.

name: Botany
fact: The science that studies plants.

name: Carnivorous Plant
fact: A plant that traps and eats animals for nutrients.

name: Cell Biology
fact: The branch of biology that studies the cell.

name: Cell Signaling
fact: How a cell communicates with itself, other cells and its environment.

name: Programmed Cell Death
fact: A cell's death caused by events inside the cell itself.

name: Organelle
fact: A specialised subunit of a cell with its own function.

name: Mitochondria
fact: The organelle that makes the cell's chemical energy.

name: Plant Cell
fact: The cells of green plants.

name: Plastid
fact: A membrane-bound organelle in plant and algal cells.

name: Ecology
fact: The science of how organisms interact with their environments.

name: Biodiversity
fact: The variability of life on Earth.

name: Biosphere
fact: The worldwide sum of all ecosystems, Earth's zone of life.

name: Endangered Species
fact: A species at very high risk of extinction.

name: Invasive Species
fact: An introduced species that harms its new environment.

name: Sustainability
fact: The ability to continue the same over a long period.

name: Wildlife Conservation
fact: Protecting wild species and their habitats.

name: Eel
fact: Long, snake-shaped ray-finned fish that change greatly from larva to adult.

name: Flying Fish
fact: Saltwater fish that glide through the air above the waves.

name: Milkfish
fact: A widespread Indo-Pacific fish, the only living member of its family.

name: Oarfish
fact: Very long, rarely seen ocean fish of the open sea.

name: Mullet
fact: Coastal fish eaten around the Mediterranean since Roman times.

name: Stickleback
fact: Small spiny fish of fresh, brackish and sea water in the north.

name: Stingray
fact: Flat cartilaginous fish with stinging tails.

name: Skate
fact: Flat cartilaginous fish of the ray family Rajidae.

name: Sawfish
fact: Giant rays with a long toothed snout like a saw.

name: Electric Ray
fact: Rays that stun prey with an electric discharge.

name: Barracuda
fact: A large predatory saltwater fish of tropical oceans.

name: Cichlid
fact: A huge, diverse family of freshwater fish.

name: Tilapia
fact: Cichlid fish of great economic importance, widely farmed.

name: Guppy
fact: A small, colourful livebearing aquarium fish.

name: Plaice
fact: A flatfish; the European plaice is the commercially important one.

name: Turbot
fact: A large flatfish of the Northeast Atlantic, Baltic and Mediterranean.

name: Alaska Pollock
fact: A schooling North Pacific fish of the cod family.

name: Cod
fact: The demersal fish of the genus Gadus.

name: Haddock
fact: A saltwater fish of the cod family.

name: Mahi-mahi
fact: A surface-dwelling fish of warm open seas, also called dolphinfish.

name: Grouper
fact: Marine fish once counted among the seabasses, now a family of their own.

name: European Seabass
fact: A mostly ocean-going fish of European and North African coasts.

name: Betta
fact: The betta, a freshwater fish of Southeast Asia.

name: Perch
fact: A freshwater fish of the genus Perca.

name: Remora
fact: The suckerfish that clings to sharks and other large animals.

name: Ocean Sunfish
fact: One of the largest ray-finned fish in the world.

name: Wrasse
fact: A large family of marine fish, many of them brightly coloured.

name: Lungfish
fact: Freshwater fish that can breathe air.

name: Arapaima
fact: A very large Amazon fish, also called the pirarucu.

name: Ghost Shark
fact: Cartilaginous fish known as ghost sharks.

name: Sturgeon
fact: Ancient fish of the family Acipenseridae, descended from earlier fish.

name: Anchovy
fact: Small, common forage fish of the family Engraulidae.

name: Herring
fact: Forage fish that move in large schools near coasts.

name: Sardine
fact: Small, oily forage fish of the herring group.

name: Sprat
fact: Small forage fish of the genus Sprattus.

name: Carp
fact: Freshwater fish of the very large family Cyprinidae.

name: Smelt
fact: Small fish of the family Osmeridae, found in oceans, rivers and lakes.

name: Trout
fact: Carnivorous freshwater fish of the salmon family.

name: Catfish
fact: Fish named for barbels that look like a cat's whiskers.

name: Bichir
fact: Archaic freshwater fish of tropical Africa and the Nile.

name: Coral Reef Fish
fact: Marine fish that live among coral reefs.

name: Deep-sea Fish
fact: Fish that live in the darkness below the sunlit waters.

name: Cartilaginous Fish
fact: The jawed fish whose skeletons are mostly cartilage.

name: Bony Fish
fact: The bony fish, whose skeletons are mostly bone.

name: Ray-finned Fish
fact: The ray-finned fish, nearly all the fish alive today.

name: Jawless Fish
fact: The jawless fish, such as lampreys and hagfishes.

name: Salamander
fact: Lizard-like amphibians with a tail in both larva and adult.

name: Newt
fact: A semiaquatic salamander whose young phase is called an eft.

name: True Toad
fact: Any member of the toad family Bufonidae.

name: Crocodilians
fact: The order of semiaquatic predatory reptiles, closest living relatives of birds.

name: Alligator
fact: A large crocodilian; the American and Chinese alligators survive.

name: Caiman
fact: A Central and South American relative of the alligator.

name: Chameleon
fact: Old World lizards famed for shifting colour.

name: Gecko
fact: Small, mostly carnivorous lizards of warm climates.

name: Green Iguana
fact: A large, tree-living, mostly plant-eating lizard.

name: Horned Lizard
fact: North American lizards with horns and flat, rounded bodies.

name: Skink
fact: One of the most diverse families of lizards.

name: Copperhead
fact: A venomous pit viper of the eastern United States.

name: Cottonmouth
fact: A semiaquatic venomous pit viper of the southeastern United States.

name: Boa Family
fact: The boas, a family of nonvenomous snakes that includes some of the world's largest.

name: Coral Snake
fact: Elapid snakes in two groups, Old World and New World.

name: Garter Snake
fact: Small to medium snakes of North and Central America.

name: Sea Snake
fact: Elapid snakes that live in the sea.

name: Mamba
fact: Fast-moving, highly venomous snakes of the genus Dendroaspis.

name: Cobra Genus
fact: The genus of true cobras, venomous snakes of Africa and Asia.

name: Snapping Turtle
fact: A large freshwater turtle of eastern North America.

name: Alligator Snapping Turtle
fact: The largest freshwater turtle in North America.

name: Painted Turtle
fact: North America's most widespread native turtle.

name: Red-eared Slider
fact: A popular pet turtle and the most invasive chelonian.

name: Sea Turtle
fact: Marine reptiles of the order Testudines.

name: Tortoise
fact: Land-dwelling turtles of the family Testudinidae.

name: Galápagos Tortoise
fact: A very large tortoise of the Galápagos.

name: Plesiosaur
fact: Extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles with long necks and paddle limbs.

name: Synapsids
fact: The group that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.

name: Dimetrodon
fact: An extinct synapsid of the Permian with a large sail on its back.

name: Seabird
fact: Birds adapted to life in the marine environment.

name: Ratites and Tinamous
fact: The infraclass of birds that includes ostriches, emus, kiwis and tinamous.

name: Accipiter
fact: A genus of birds of prey that includes many sparrowhawks.

name: Falcon
fact: Birds of prey of the genus Falco, including the hobbies and kestrels.

name: Old World Vulture
fact: Vultures of Europe, Asia and Africa, in the same family as eagles and hawks.

name: Osprey
fact: A fish-eating bird of prey found almost worldwide.

name: Secretarybird
fact: A large, mostly ground-living African bird of prey.

name: Nightjar
fact: Night-flying birds with long wings, short legs and very short bills.

name: Auk
fact: The family of seabirds that includes puffins, murres and guillemots.

name: Gull
fact: Seabirds informally called seagulls.

name: Sandpiper
fact: Shorebirds that pick small invertebrates from mud or soil.

name: Tern
fact: Seabirds of the gull and tern family found near water worldwide.

name: Dodo
fact: The extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.

name: Passenger Pigeon
fact: An extinct North American pigeon named for its migrations.

name: Rock Dove
fact: The common city pigeon, wild form of the domestic pigeon.

name: Hornbill
fact: Tropical birds with a long, down-curved bill, often topped by a horny casque.

name: Hoopoe
fact: Colourful birds with a crown of feathers they can raise or lower.

name: Kingfisher
fact: Small to medium, brightly coloured birds of the family Alcedinidae.

name: Cuckoo
fact: The family of birds that includes cuckoos and roadrunners.

name: Grouse
fact: Game birds of the order Galliformes, in the pheasant family.

name: Guinea Fowl
fact: African birds among the oldest of the gallinaceous birds.

name: Peafowl
fact: The birds of which the male is the peacock.

name: Common Pheasant
fact: The ring-necked game bird of the pheasant family.

name: Common Quail
fact: A small, migratory, ground-nesting game bird.

name: Domestic Turkey
fact: A large fowl, the same species as the wild turkey.

name: Loon
fact: Aquatic birds of North America and northern Eurasia, also called divers.

name: Bustard
fact: Large ground birds of dry grassland and steppe.

name: Songbird
fact: A perching bird of the suborder Passeri.

name: Bird-of-paradise
fact: Birds of New Guinea and nearby lands, of the family Paradisaeidae.

name: Crows and Ravens
fact: The genus of crows, ravens and rooks.

name: Eurasian Magpie
fact: A crow-family bird resident across northern Eurasia.

name: Honeyeater
fact: A large, diverse family of small to medium birds, mostly Australasian.

name: Lyrebird
fact: A ground-dwelling Australian bird that mimics natural and artificial sounds.

name: Shrike
fact: Passerine birds also called butcherbirds.

name: Bulbul
fact: Medium-sized songbirds of Africa and Asia.

name: Finch
fact: Small birds with stout conical bills for eating seeds and nuts.

name: Red-winged Blackbird
fact: A blackbird of North and Central America.

name: Lark
fact: Passerine birds of the family Alaudidae.

name: Mockingbird
fact: New World birds known for mimicking other birds' songs.

name: New World Warbler
fact: Small, often colourful birds restricted to the New World.

name: European Robin
fact: The small, red-breasted robin of the British Isles and Europe.

name: Common Nightingale
fact: A small bird known for its powerful and beautiful song.

name: House Sparrow
fact: A small sparrow found in most parts of the world.

name: Common Starling
fact: A medium-sized passerine of the starling family.

name: Common Myna
fact: An Asian bird that has adapted very well to cities.

name: Sunbird
fact: Small, slender Old World nectar-feeding birds.

name: Swallow
fact: Songbirds highly adapted to feeding in flight.

name: Tit
fact: Small passerine birds, the tits, chickadees and titmice.

name: Thrush
fact: The worldwide passerine family Turdidae.

name: American Robin
fact: A migratory thrush named for its resemblance to the European robin.

name: Wren
fact: Small brown passerine birds of the family Troglodytidae.

name: Darter
fact: Tropical waterbirds also called anhingas or snakebirds.

name: Frigatebird
fact: Seabirds of tropical and subtropical oceans.

name: Shoebill
fact: A large wading bird named for its shoe-shaped bill.

name: Stork
fact: Large, long-legged wading birds with long, stout bills.

name: Honeyguide
fact: Birds also known as indicator birds.

name: Budgerigar
fact: The budgie, a small, long-tailed Australian parrot.

name: Cockatoo
fact: Parrots of the family Cacatuidae, native to Australasia.

name: Moa
fact: Extinct flightless birds of New Zealand.

name: Eurasian Eagle-owl
fact: A large owl of much of Eurasia.

name: Barn Owl
fact: The genus of barn owls.

name: Tinamou
fact: Ground birds of Central and South America.

name: Trogon
fact: The trogons and quetzals, one family of colourful tropical birds.

name: Resplendent Quetzal
fact: A bird of Central American cloud forests, in the trogon family.

name: Megabat
fact: The fruit bats, also called flying foxes.

name: Microbat
fact: The echolocating bats, generally smaller than megabats.

name: Flying Fox
fact: The genus of large fruit bats, the flying foxes.

name: Scallop
fact: Marine bivalve molluscs of the family Pectinidae.

name: Jumping Spider
fact: Spiders of the largest spider family, with the best vision among arthropods.

name: Decapod
fact: A crustacean of the order Decapoda: crabs, lobsters, crayfish, shrimp and prawns.

name: Malacostraca
fact: The class of crustaceans that includes crabs, lobsters, shrimp and krill.

name: Ostracod
fact: Small crustaceans sometimes called seed shrimp.

name: Hexapods
fact: The largest clade of arthropods, including the insects.

name: Winged Insects
fact: The subclass of insects that includes all winged insects.

name: Stick Insects
fact: The order of stick insects.

name: Weevil
fact: Small, plant-eating beetles known for very long snouts.

name: Fruit Fly
fact: The fruit fly, a species of the family Drosophilidae.

name: Botfly
fact: Flies whose larvae are internal parasites of mammals.

name: Crane Fly
fact: A fly of the superfamily Tipuloidea, whose larva is the leatherjacket.

name: Blowfly
fact: The blowflies, bluebottles and greenbottles.

name: Horsefly
fact: The horse flies and deer flies, large and agile in flight.

name: Leafhopper
fact: Minute insects that suck sap from grass, shrubs and trees.

name: Scale Insect
fact: Small, very varied insects of the order Hemiptera.

name: Whitefly
fact: Hemipterans that feed on the undersides of plant leaves.

name: Hymenoptera
fact: The insect order of sawflies, wasps, bees and ants.

name: Fire Ant
fact: Stinging ants of the genus Solenopsis.

name: Carpenter Ant
fact: The most species-rich genus of ants, found nearly worldwide.

name: Bumblebee
fact: Any bee of the genus Bombus.

name: Africanized Bee
fact: The hybrid honey bee nicknamed the killer bee.

name: Hornet
fact: The largest of the eusocial wasps, genus Vespa.

name: Geometer Moth
fact: Moths whose larvae, the inchworms, seem to measure the earth.

name: Large White Butterfly
fact: The large white, or cabbage butterfly.

name: Swallowtail Butterfly
fact: Large, colourful butterflies of the family Papilionidae.

name: Odonata
fact: The order of predatory flying insects: dragonflies and damselflies.

name: Damselfly
fact: Slimmer, usually smaller relatives of dragonflies.

name: Mole Cricket
fact: Burrowing crickets with shovel-like forelimbs.

name: Chelicerates
fact: The arthropod subphylum of spiders, scorpions, mites and horseshoe crabs.

name: Sea Scorpion
fact: Extinct marine arthropods, informally the sea scorpions.

name: Horseshoe Crab
fact: The horseshoe crabs, arthropods related to arachnids.

name: C. elegans
fact: A transparent soil nematode, the type species of its genus.

name: Bristle Worm
fact: Marine bristle worms with bristled protrusions on each segment.

name: Bilateria
fact: Animals with bilateral symmetry, a head end and a tail end.

name: Animal Coloration
fact: The look of an animal resulting from light reflected or emitted by its surface.

name: Animal Locomotion

name: Octahedron

name: Dodecahedron

name: Icosahedron

name: Platonic solid

name: Tesseract

name: Cardioid

name: Cycloid

name: Catenary

name: Brachistochrone curve

name: Lemniscate

name: Elliptic curve

name: Cantor set

name: Julia set
fact: The Julia set and the Fatou set are two complementary sets in complex dynamics, defined from a function.

name: Koch snowflake
fact: The Koch snowflake is a fractal curve and one of the earliest fractals to have been described.

name: Mandelbrot set

name: Sierpiński triangle
fact: The Sierpiński triangle is a fractal with the overall shape of an equilateral triangle, subdivided recursively into smaller equilateral triangles.

name: Circumference
fact: The circumference is the perimeter of a circle or ellipse, its arc length straightened out to a line segment.

name: Radius

name: Perpendicular
fact: Two geometric objects are perpendicular if they intersect at right angles.

name: Unit circle

name: Law of cosines

name: Squaring the circle

name: Parallel postulate

name: Straightedge and compass construction

name: Hyperbolic geometry
fact: Hyperbolic geometry is a non-Euclidean geometry.

name: Projective geometry
fact: Projective geometry is the study of geometric properties that are invariant under projective transformations.

name: Spherical geometry

name: Stereographic projection
fact: A stereographic projection is a perspective projection of the sphere, through a point on the sphere, onto a plane.

name: Histogram

name: Bar chart
fact: A bar chart presents categorical data with rectangular bars whose heights or lengths are proportional to the values.

name: Pie chart
fact: A pie chart is a circular statistical graphic divided into slices to illustrate numerical proportion.

name: Scatter plot

name: Monty Hall problem

name: Banach–Tarski paradox

name: Cantor's diagonal argument
fact: Cantor's diagonal argument proves that some infinite sets cannot be put into one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers.

name: Zorn's lemma

name: Square root of 2
fact: The square root of two is the positive real number that, multiplied by itself, equals two.

name: Euler's constant
fact: Euler's constant is the limiting difference between the harmonic series and the natural logarithm.

name: Sexagesimal

name: Tally marks

name: Hindu–Arabic numeral system

name: Maya numerals
fact: The Mayan numeral system represented numbers and calendar dates in the Maya civilization.

name: Continued fraction

name: Division by zero
fact: Division where the divisor is zero is a problematic special case in mathematics.

name: Multiplication table
fact: A multiplication table is a mathematical table used to define a multiplication operation for an algebraic system.

name: Long division
fact: Long division is a standard algorithm for dividing multi-digit numbers by hand, in a series of easier steps.

name: Modus ponens
fact: Modus ponens is a deductive argument form and rule of inference in propositional logic.

name: Quaternion
fact: The quaternions are a number system like the complex numbers, but with four real-number components instead of two.

name: Random walk
fact: A random walk is a path made of a succession of random steps on some mathematical space.

name: Monte Carlo method
fact: Monte Carlo methods use repeated random sampling to obtain numerical results.

name: Linear regression
fact: Linear regression estimates the relationship between a response and one or more explanatory variables.

name: Principal component analysis
fact: Principal component analysis is a linear dimensionality reduction technique used in exploratory data analysis.

name: Peano axioms
fact: The Peano axioms are axioms for the natural numbers, presented by the Italian mathematician Giuseppe Peano.

name: Lambda calculus
fact: The lambda calculus is a formal system for expressing computation through function abstraction and application.

name: Fields Medal

name: Millennium Prize Problems
fact: The Millennium Prize Problems are seven well-known complex mathematical problems, each with a prize of one million dollars.

name: Chemist

name: Chemical engineer

name: Safety data sheet
fact: A safety data sheet is a document that lists information on occupational safety and health for the use of substances and products.

name: Food chemistry
fact: Food chemistry is the study of chemical processes and interactions of all biological and non-biological components of foods.

name: Surface science
fact: Surface science is the study of physical and chemical phenomena at the interface of two phases.

name: Theoretical chemistry
fact: Theoretical chemistry is the branch of chemistry which develops the theoretical generalizations of modern chemistry.

name: Computational chemistry
fact: Computational chemistry uses computer simulations to assist in solving chemical problems and to calculate the structures and properties of molecules.

name: Solid-state chemistry
fact: Solid-state chemistry, also called materials chemistry, is the study of the synthesis, structure and properties of solid phase materials.

name: Octet rule

name: Single bond

name: Double bond

name: Triple bond
fact: A triple bond is a chemical bond between two atoms involving six bonding electrons, stronger than single or double bonds.

name: Polyatomic ion
fact: A polyatomic ion is a covalent bonded set of two or more atoms that behaves as a single unit and usually has a net charge.

name: Valence electron
fact: Valence electrons are electrons in the outermost shell of an atom that can take part in forming a chemical bond.

name: Concentration
fact: Concentration is the abundance of a constituent divided by the total volume of a mixture.

name: Aqueous solution
fact: An aqueous solution is a solution in which the solvent is water.

name: Solid solution
fact: A solid solution is a homogeneous mixture of two compounds in solid state with a single crystal structure, a term commonly used for metals.

name: Solubility
fact: Solubility is the ability of a substance, the solute, to form a solution with another substance, the solvent.

name: Miscibility

name: Solvation

name: Tincture

name: Chemical nomenclature

name: Mass number

name: Relative atomic mass

name: Heavy metals

name: Post-transition metal

name: Atomic radius

name: Electronegativity
fact: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract shared electrons when forming a chemical bond.

name: Ionization energy
fact: Ionization energy is the minimum energy required to remove the most loosely bound electron of an isolated gaseous atom, positive ion or molecule.

name: Electron affinity
fact: Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron attaches to a neutral atom or molecule in the gaseous state to form an anion.

name: Reagent
fact: A reagent is a substance or compound added to a system to cause a chemical reaction, or test if one occurs.

name: Stoichiometry
fact: Stoichiometry is the relationship between the quantities of reactants and products before, during and after chemical reactions.

name: Law of definite proportions
fact: The law of definite proportions states that a chemical compound contains its constituent elements in a fixed ratio, whatever its source.

name: Avogadro constant
fact: The Avogadro constant is a ratio between an amount of substance and the number of particles that it contains.

name: Empirical formula
fact: The empirical formula of a compound is the simplest whole number ratio of the atoms present in it.

name: Structural isomer
fact: A structural isomer is a compound with the same number and type of atoms as another, but with a different connectivity between them.

name: Lewis structure
fact: Lewis structures are diagrams that show the bonding between atoms of a molecule and any lone pairs of electrons.

name: Skeletal formula
fact: The skeletal formula is a minimalist structural formula representing a molecule's atoms, bonds and some details of its geometry.

name: Ball-and-stick model
fact: The ball-and-stick model shows the three-dimensional position of atoms as spheres, connected by rods which represent the bonds.

name: Space-filling model
fact: A space-filling model is a three-dimensional molecular model where the atoms are represented by spheres whose radii are proportional to the radii of the atoms.

name: Ribbon diagram
fact: Ribbon diagrams are schematic representations of protein structure and one of the most common methods of protein depiction used today.

name: Diatomic molecule
fact: Diatomic molecules are molecules composed of only two atoms, of the same or different chemical elements.

name: Macromolecule
fact: A macromolecule is a molecule of high relative molecular mass, made of the multiple repetition of units from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

name: Volatile organic compound
fact: Volatile organic compounds are organic compounds with a high vapor pressure at room temperature.

name: Cyclic compound
fact: A cyclic compound, or ring compound, is a chemical compound which includes a ring.

name: Heterocyclic compound
fact: A heterocyclic compound is a hydrocarbon-based cyclic compound that contains at least one heteroatom as member of its rings.

name: Molar mass
fact: The molar mass of a chemical substance is the ratio between the mass and the amount of substance of any sample of it.

name: Activated carbon
fact: Activated carbon, also called activated charcoal, is a form of carbon commonly used to filter contaminants from water and air.

name: Allotropes of carbon
fact: Carbon forms many allotropes, structurally different forms of the same element; well-known forms include diamond and graphite.

name: Buckminsterfullerene
fact: Buckminsterfullerene is a fullerene with a cage-like fused-ring structure of twenty hexagons and twelve pentagons, resembling a football.

name: Liquid helium
fact: Liquid helium is a physical state of helium at very low temperatures, which may show superfluidity.

name: Liquid oxygen
fact: Liquid oxygen is a clear, pale cyan liquid form of dioxygen, used as the oxidizer in the first liquid-fueled rocket.

name: Singlet oxygen
fact: Singlet oxygen is a gaseous chemical with two oxygen atoms in a quantum state where all electrons are spin-paired.

name: Triplet oxygen
fact: Triplet oxygen is the ground state of molecular oxygen, whose molecules contain two unpaired electrons.

name: Allotropes of sulfur
fact: Sulfur exists as many allotropes; in number of allotropes it is second only to carbon.

name: Superheavy element
fact: Superheavy elements, also known as transactinides, are the chemical elements beyond the actinides in the periodic table.

name: Transuranium element
fact: The transuranium elements are the chemical elements with atomic number greater than that of uranium, all radioactively unstable.

name: Acid anhydride
fact: An acid anhydride is a compound of two acyl groups bonded to a common oxygen atom, commonly formed by removing water from a pair of acids.

name: Amphoterism
fact: An amphoteric compound is a molecule or ion that can react both as an acid and as a base.

name: Alkali
fact: An alkali is a base that dissolves in water, a hydroxide of an alkali metal or alkaline earth metal.

name: Weak base
fact: A weak base does not accept all the available ions, and forms an equilibrium between the base and its conjugate acid.

name: Hydronium
fact: Hydronium is the cation, the type of oxonium ion produced by protonation of water.

name: Protonation
fact: Protonation is the adding of a proton to an atom, molecule or ion, forming a conjugate acid.

name: Deprotonation
fact: Deprotonation is the removal of a proton from an acid in an acid–base reaction, forming the conjugate base of that acid.

name: Lewis acids and bases
fact: A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair from a Lewis base to form a Lewis adduct.

name: Nucleophile
fact: A nucleophile is a chemical species that forms bonds by donating an electron pair.

name: Acid strength
fact: Acid strength is the tendency of an acid to dissociate into a proton and an anion.

name: Acid dissociation constant
fact: An acid dissociation constant is a quantitative measure of the strength of an acid in solution.

name: Mineral acid
fact: A mineral acid is an acid derived from one or more inorganic compounds, as opposed to organic acids.

name: Organic acid
fact: An organic acid is an organic compound with acidic properties; the most common are the carboxylic acids.

name: Sulfonic acid
fact: Sulfonic acid is a member of the class of organosulfur compounds with a sulfonyl hydroxide group.

name: Intermetallic
fact: An intermetallic is a metallic alloy that forms a solid-state compound with a crystal structure between two or more metallic elements.

name: Network solid
fact: A network solid is a chemical compound in which the atoms are bonded by covalent bonds in a continuous network throughout the material.

name: Cementite
fact: Cementite, or iron carbide, is a compound of iron and carbon.

name: Carbide
fact: A carbide usually describes a compound composed of carbon and a metal.

name: Hydrate
fact: A hydrate is a substance that contains water or its constituent elements.

name: Ice crystal
fact: Ice crystals are solid water in symmetrical shapes including hexagonal columns, hexagonal plates and dendritic crystals.

name: Monomer
fact: A monomer is a molecule that can react with other monomer molecules to form a larger polymer chain.

name: Functional group
fact: A functional group is any substituent in a molecule that causes the molecule's characteristic chemical reactions.

name: Carbonyl group
fact: A carbonyl group is a functional group composed of a carbon atom double-bonded to an oxygen atom.

name: Aromaticity
fact: Aromaticity describes how a conjugated ring of unsaturated bonds exhibits a stabilization stronger than would be expected from conjugation alone.

name: Cycloalkane
fact: The cycloalkanes are the monocyclic saturated hydrocarbons, made only of hydrogen and carbon atoms arranged in a single ring.

name: Phenol formaldehyde resin
fact: Phenol formaldehyde resins are synthetic polymers used as the basis for Bakelite, the first commercial synthetic resins.

name: Polyphenol
fact: Polyphenols are a large family of naturally occurring phenols, abundant in plants and structurally diverse.

name: Flavonoid
fact: Flavonoids are a class of polyphenolic secondary metabolites found in plants.

name: Terpene
fact: Terpenes are a large and diverse class of natural products, crucial biosynthetic building blocks in many organisms, particularly plants.

name: Anthocyanidin
fact: Anthocyanidins are common plant pigments, based on the flavylium cation.

name: Ammonium
fact: Ammonium is a modified form of ammonia that has an extra hydrogen atom, a positively charged molecular ion.

name: Zwitterion
fact: A zwitterion, also called an inner salt, is a molecule with an equal number of positively and negatively charged functional groups.

name: Halide
fact: A halide is a binary chemical compound of a halogen atom and an element or radical that is less electronegative.

name: Bromide
fact: A bromide ion is the negatively charged form of bromine; most bromides are colorless.

name: Fluoride
fact: Fluoride is an inorganic, monatomic anion of fluorine, whose salts are typically white or colorless.

name: Calcium fluoride
fact: Calcium fluoride is the inorganic compound of calcium and fluorine, a white solid practically insoluble in water.

name: Nitride
fact: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen, inorganic or organic, ionic or covalent.

name: Tincture of iodine
fact: Tincture of iodine is an antiseptic tincture containing iodine, ethanol and water.

name: Acetate
