fact: An acetate is a salt formed by the combination of acetic acid with a base.

name: Copper(II) acetate
fact: Copper acetate, also called cupric acetate, is a chemical compound of copper and acetate.

name: Iron oxide
fact: An iron oxide is a chemical compound composed of iron and oxygen.

name: Peroxide
fact: Peroxides are a group of molecules in which oxygen atoms are joined to each other through single covalent bonds.

name: Oxyanion
fact: An oxyanion is an ion formed from a chemical element combined with oxygen, formed by a large majority of the chemical elements.

name: Perchlorate
fact: A perchlorate is a chemical compound used mainly in making rocket fuel and fireworks.

name: Hydroxide
fact: Hydroxide is a diatomic anion of an oxygen and hydrogen atom held together by a single covalent bond, carrying a negative electric charge.

name: Chrome yellow
fact: Chrome yellow is a bright, warm yellow pigment used in paints, industry, chemistry, art and fashion.

name: Sulfide
fact: Sulfide is an inorganic anion of sulfur, or a compound containing it.

name: Lime sulfur
fact: Lime sulfur is mainly a mixture of calcium polysulfides and thiosulfate, formed by reacting calcium hydroxide with elemental sulfur.

name: Qualitative inorganic analysis
fact: Classical qualitative inorganic analysis seeks to find the elemental composition of inorganic compounds by detecting ions in an aqueous solution.

name: Elemental analysis
fact: Elemental analysis is a process where a sample is analyzed for its elemental and sometimes isotopic composition.

name: Combustion analysis
fact: Combustion analysis determines the elemental composition of a pure organic compound by combusting the sample.

name: Cheminformatics
fact: Cheminformatics uses physical chemistry theory with computer and information science techniques on problems in chemistry.

name: Flame test
fact: A flame test is a relatively quick test for the presence of some elements in a sample.

name: Gravimetric analysis
fact: Gravimetric analysis is a set of methods in analytical chemistry for determining an analyte based on its mass.

name: Titration
fact: Titration is a common laboratory method of quantitative chemical analysis to determine the concentration of an analyte.

name: Calorimetry
fact: Calorimetry is the science of measuring changes in state variables of a body to derive the heat transfer associated with changes of its state.

name: Electrophoresis
fact: Electrophoresis is the motion of charged particles or dissolved charged molecules relative to a fluid under a uniform electric field.

name: Atomic absorption spectroscopy
fact: Atomic absorption spectroscopy is an elemental analysis method for determining the concentration of metals in a sample.

name: Infrared spectroscopy
fact: Infrared spectroscopy measures the interaction of infrared radiation with matter by absorption, emission or reflection.

name: Raman spectroscopy
fact: Raman spectroscopy is a spectroscopic technique typically used to determine vibrational modes of molecules.

name: Ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy
fact: Ultraviolet–visible spectrophotometry is absorption or reflectance spectroscopy in the ultraviolet and visible regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.

name: X-ray spectroscopy
fact: X-ray spectroscopy is a general term for several spectroscopic techniques for characterizing materials by using x-ray radiation.

name: Isomerization
fact: Isomerization is the process in which a molecule is transformed into an isomer with a different chemical structure.

name: Chain reaction
fact: A chain reaction is a sequence of reactions where a reactive product causes additional reactions to take place.

name: Elementary reaction
fact: An elementary reaction is a chemical reaction in which species react directly to form products in a single step.

name: Reaction intermediate
fact: A reaction intermediate is a molecular entity arising within the sequence of a stepwise chemical reaction.

name: Organic reaction
fact: Organic reactions are chemical reactions involving organic compounds.

name: Elastic collision
fact: An elastic collision is one in which the total kinetic energy of the two bodies remains the same before and after the collision.

name: Inelastic collision
fact: An inelastic collision is one in which kinetic energy is not conserved, due to internal friction.

name: Central force
fact: A central force on an object is directed towards or away from a point called the center of force.

name: Conservative force
fact: A conservative force is one whose total work in moving a particle between two points is independent of the path taken.

name: Fictitious force
fact: A fictitious force, also called an inertial force or pseudo-force, appears to act on an object when its motion is described from a non-inertial frame of reference.

name: Centrifugal force
fact: A centrifugal force is a kind of fictitious force that appears to act on all objects when viewed in a rotating frame of reference.

name: Normal force
fact: The normal force is the component of a contact force that is perpendicular to the surface that an object contacts.

name: Resultant force
fact: A resultant force is the single force and associated torque obtained by combining a system of forces and torques acting on a rigid body.

name: Restoring force
fact: The restoring force acts to bring a body to its equilibrium position, and is always directed back toward it.

name: Inertial frame of reference
fact: An inertial frame of reference is a frame in which objects exhibit inertia: they remain at rest or in uniform motion relative to the frame.

name: Non-inertial reference frame
fact: A non-inertial reference frame, also known as an accelerated reference frame, undergoes acceleration with respect to an inertial frame.

name: Free body diagram
fact: A free body diagram is a graphical illustration used to visualize the applied forces, moments and resulting reactions on a free body.

name: Net force
fact: The net force is the sum of all the forces acting on an object.

name: Rolling resistance
fact: Rolling resistance is the force resisting the motion when a body such as a ball, tire or wheel rolls on a surface.

name: Galilean transformation
fact: A Galilean transformation converts between the coordinates of two reference frames which differ only by constant relative motion.

name: Relative velocity
fact: The relative velocity of an object with respect to an observer is its velocity measured in the rest frame of the observer.

name: Center of mass
fact: The center of mass, sometimes called the barycenter or balance point, is the unique point where the weighted relative position of the distributed mass sums to zero.

name: Mechanical advantage
fact: Mechanical advantage is a measure of the force amplification achieved by using a tool, mechanical device or machine system.

name: Damping
fact: Damping is the loss of energy of an oscillating system by dissipation, reducing or preventing its oscillation.

name: Normal mode
fact: A normal mode is a pattern of motion in which all parts of the system move sinusoidally with the same frequency and a fixed phase relation.

name: Mechanical resonance
fact: Mechanical resonance is the tendency of a system to respond at greater amplitude when its oscillations match its natural frequency of vibration.

name: Perpetual motion
fact: Perpetual motion is the motion of bodies that continues forever in an unperturbed system.

name: Potential well
fact: A potential well is the region surrounding a local minimum of potential energy.

name: Projectile
fact: A projectile is launched by an external force and then moves freely under the influence of gravity and air resistance.

name: Radiation pressure
fact: Radiation pressure, also known as light pressure, is mechanical pressure exerted upon a surface by the exchange of momentum with the electromagnetic field.

name: Mechanical equilibrium
fact: A particle is in mechanical equilibrium if the net force on it is zero.

name: Vibration
fact: Vibration is an oscillation of matter about an equilibrium point.

name: Bouncing ball
fact: The physics of a bouncing ball concerns its motion before, during and after impact against the surface of another body.

name: Linear motion
fact: Linear motion, also called rectilinear motion, is one-dimensional motion along a straight line.

name: Projectile motion
fact: Projectile motion describes an object launched into the air that moves under the influence of gravity alone.

name: Steady state
fact: A system is in a steady state if the variables that define its behavior are unchanging in time.

name: Trajectory
fact: A trajectory is the path an object takes through its motion over time.

name: Cavendish experiment
fact: The Cavendish experiment was the first to measure the force of gravity between masses in the laboratory.

name: Free fall
fact: Free fall is any motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.

name: Gravitational field
fact: A gravitational field is a vector field used to explain the influences that a body extends into the space around itself.

name: Gravitational potential
fact: The gravitational potential associates with each point in space the work per unit mass needed to move an object there from a fixed reference point.

name: Tidal force
fact: The tidal force is the difference in gravitational attraction between different points in a gravitational field.

name: Angular acceleration
fact: Angular acceleration is the time derivative of angular velocity.

name: Angular velocity
fact: Angular velocity identifies the plane, direction and angular speed of rotation of a particle rotating in a circle.

name: Circular motion
fact: Circular motion is the motion of an object along a circular path, like a stone tied to a string or a point on a rotating wheel.

name: Precession
fact: Precession is a change in the orientation of the rotational axis of a rotating body.

name: Boundary layer
fact: A boundary layer is the thin layer of fluid in the immediate vicinity of a bounding surface, formed by the fluid flowing along the surface.

name: Boyle's law
fact: Boyle's law is an empirical gas law that describes the relationship between pressure and volume of a confined gas.

name: Archimedes' principle
fact: Archimedes' principle states that the upward buoyant force on a body immersed in a fluid equals the weight of the fluid that the body displaces.

name: Coandă effect
fact: The Coandă effect is the tendency of a fluid jet to stay attached to a surface of any form.

name: Compressibility
fact: Compressibility is a measure of the relative volume change of a fluid or solid as a response to a pressure change.

name: Newtonian fluid
fact: A Newtonian fluid is one in which the viscous stresses arising from its flow are linearly correlated to the local strain rate.

name: Non-Newtonian fluid
fact: A non-Newtonian fluid does not follow Newton's law of viscosity; it has variable viscosity dependent on stress.

name: Flow visualization
fact: Flow visualization makes flow patterns visible, in order to get qualitative or quantitative information on them.

name: Mass flow rate
fact: Mass flow rate is the rate at which mass of a fluid passes through a surface over time.

name: Hydrostatics
fact: Hydrostatics is the branch of fluid mechanics that studies fluids at hydrostatic equilibrium.

name: Communicating vessels
fact: Communicating vessels are connected containers of a homogeneous fluid: when the liquid settles, it balances out to the same level in all of them.

name: Hydrostatic equilibrium
fact: Hydrostatic equilibrium is the condition of a fluid at rest, when external forces such as gravity are balanced by a pressure-gradient force.

name: Pascal's law
fact: Pascal's law states that a pressure change at any point in a confined incompressible fluid is transmitted throughout the fluid.

name: Length contraction
fact: Length contraction is the phenomenon that a moving object's length is measured to be shorter than its proper length.

name: Ladder paradox
fact: The ladder paradox is a thought experiment in special relativity involving a ladder travelling horizontally at relativistic speed and undergoing length contraction.

name: Lorentz factor
fact: The Lorentz factor expresses how much the measurements of time, length and other physical properties change for an object while it moves.

name: Luminiferous aether
fact: Luminiferous aether was the formerly postulated medium for the propagation of light.

name: Minkowski spacetime
fact: Minkowski spacetime is the main mathematical description of spacetime in the absence of gravitation, a four-dimensional model.

name: Relativity of simultaneity
fact: The relativity of simultaneity is the concept that whether two separated events occur at the same time depends on the observer's reference frame.

name: Spacetime diagram
fact: A spacetime diagram is a graphical illustration of locations in space at various times, especially in special relativity.

name: Time dilation
fact: Time dilation is the difference in elapsed time as measured by two clocks, because of relative velocity or a difference in gravitational potential.

name: Twin paradox
fact: The twin paradox is a thought experiment in special relativity in which a twin who takes a space voyage returns home to find the twin who stayed has aged more.

name: Proper time
fact: Proper time along a timelike world line is the time as measured by a clock following that line.

name: Hawking radiation
fact: Hawking radiation is radiation released outside a black hole's event horizon due to quantum effects.

name: Gravitational time dilation
fact: Gravitational time dilation is a difference of elapsed time between two events, measured by observers at varying distances from a gravitating mass.

name: White hole
fact: A white hole is a hypothetical region of spacetime that cannot be entered from the outside, although energy, matter and light can escape from it.

name: No-hair theorem
fact: The no-hair theorem states that a stationary black hole can be completely characterized by only three independent externally observable classical parameters.

name: Faster-than-light
fact: Faster-than-light travel is the hypothetical propagation of matter or information faster than the speed of light in vacuum.

name: Plum pudding model
fact: The plum pudding model is an obsolete scientific model of the atom proposed by Sir J. J. Thomson after his discovery of the electron.

name: Rutherford model
fact: The Rutherford model is the idea that an atom contains a compact nucleus.

name: Positronium
fact: Positronium is a system of an electron and its anti-particle, a positron, bound together into an exotic atom.

name: Hydrogen line
fact: The hydrogen line is a spectral line created by a change in the energy state of solitary, electrically neutral hydrogen atoms.

name: Emission spectrum
fact: The emission spectrum of an element is the spectrum of radiation emitted when electrons move from a high energy state to a lower one.

name: Optical pumping
fact: Optical pumping is a process in which light is used to raise electrons from a lower energy level to a higher one.

name: Molecular physics
fact: Molecular physics is the study of the physical properties of molecules and molecular dynamics.

name: Franck–Hertz experiment
fact: The Franck–Hertz experiment was the first electrical measurement to clearly show the quantum nature of atoms.

name: Born rule
fact: The Born rule gives the probability that a measurement of a quantum system will yield a given result.

name: Correspondence principle
fact: A correspondence principle is any of several premises about the relationship between classical and quantum mechanics, a term coined by Niels Bohr.

name: Hidden-variable theory
fact: A hidden-variable theory is a deterministic model which seeks to explain the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics by introducing additional variables.

name: Measurement problem
fact: The measurement problem is the problem of definite outcomes: quantum systems have superpositions but measurements give only one definite result.

name: Quantum superposition
fact: Quantum superposition is a fundamental principle of quantum mechanics: combinations of solutions to the Schrödinger equation are also solutions.

name: Wave function collapse
fact: Wave function collapse occurs when a wave function in a superposition of several eigenstates reduces to a single eigenstate by interaction with the external world.

name: Quantum fluctuation
fact: A quantum fluctuation is the temporary random change in the amount of energy in a point in space, as prescribed by Heisenberg's uncertainty principle.

name: Quantum indeterminacy
fact: Quantum indeterminacy is the apparent necessary incompleteness in the description of a physical system in quantum physics.

name: Quantum information
fact: Quantum information is the information of the state of a quantum system.

name: Quantum state
fact: A quantum state is a mathematical entity that represents a physical system.

name: Bell test
fact: A Bell test is a real-world physics experiment designed to test quantum mechanics in relation to Einstein's concept of local realism.

name: Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen paradox
fact: The Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen paradox is a thought experiment arguing that the description of physical reality provided by quantum mechanics is incomplete.

name: Particle in a box
fact: The particle in a box model describes the movement of a free particle in a small space surrounded by impenetrable barriers.

name: Matter wave
fact: Matter waves are half of wave–particle duality: at all scales where measurements have been practical, matter exhibits wave-like behavior.

name: Electron diffraction
fact: Electron diffraction is a generic term for changes in the direction of electron beams due to elastic interactions with atoms.

name: Davisson–Germer experiment
fact: In the Davisson–Germer experiment, electrons scattered by the surface of a crystal of nickel metal displayed a diffraction pattern.

name: Quantum vacuum state
fact: The quantum vacuum state is the quantum state with the lowest possible energy, and generally contains no physical particles.

name: Crystal system
fact: In crystallography, a crystal system is a set of point groups, and a lattice system is a set of Bravais lattices.

name: Crystal structure
fact: A crystal structure is a description of the ordered arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a crystalline material.

name: Crystallographic defect
fact: A crystallographic defect is an interruption of the regular patterns of arrangement of atoms or molecules in crystalline solids.

name: Electronic band structure
fact: The electronic band structure of a solid describes the range of energy levels that electrons may have within it, and those they may not.

name: Quasiparticle
fact: A quasiparticle describes a collective behavior of a group of particles that can be treated as if they were a single particle.

name: Electron hole
fact: An electron hole is a quasiparticle denoting the lack of an electron at a position where one could exist in an atom or atomic lattice.

name: Fermi gas
fact: A Fermi gas is an idealized model, an ensemble of many non-interacting fermions.

name: Mott insulator
fact: Mott insulators are materials expected to conduct electricity according to conventional band theories, but are actually insulators.

name: Soft matter
fact: Soft matter is a type of matter that can be deformed or structurally altered by thermal or mechanical stress.

name: High-temperature superconductivity
fact: High-temperature superconductivity is superconductivity in materials with a critical temperature above the boiling point of liquid nitrogen.

name: Type-I superconductor
fact: The interior of a bulk superconductor cannot be penetrated by a weak magnetic field, a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect.

name: Magnetic dipole
fact: A magnetic dipole is a theoretical description of a sufficiently small magnet such as that of an atom or electron.

name: Magnetic flux
fact: The magnetic flux through a surface is the surface integral of the normal component of the magnetic field over that surface.

name: Magnetic moment
fact: The magnetic moment characterizes the strength and orientation of a magnet or other object that exerts a magnetic field.

name: Magnetic susceptibility
fact: Magnetic susceptibility is a measure of how much a material will become magnetized in an applied magnetic field.

name: Ising model
fact: The Ising model is a mathematical model of ferromagnetism in statistical mechanics.

name: Hysteresis
fact: Hysteresis is the dependence of the state of a system on its history.

name: Conservation law
fact: A conservation law states that a particular measurable property of an isolated physical system does not change as the system evolves over time.

name: Transport phenomena
fact: The study of transport phenomena concerns the exchange of mass, energy, charge, momentum and angular momentum between systems.

name: Background radiation
fact: Background radiation is a measure of the level of ionizing radiation present in the environment at a particular location.

name: Inverse-square law
fact: An inverse-square law states that the observed intensity of a physical quantity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from its source.

name: Instability
fact: In dynamical systems, instability means that some of the outputs or internal states increase with time, without bounds.

name: Metastability
fact: Metastability is an intermediate energetic state other than the state of least energy; a ball resting in a hollow on a slope is a simple example.

name: Classical physics
fact: Classical physics consists of physical theories that are non-quantum or both non-quantum and non-relativistic.

name: Modern physics
fact: Modern physics includes quantum mechanics, special relativity and general relativity.

name: Experimental physics
fact: Experimental physics is concerned with the observation of physical phenomena and experiments.

name: Computational physics
fact: Computational physics is the study and implementation of numerical analysis to solve problems in physics.

name: Atmospheric physics
fact: Atmospheric physics is the application of physics to the study of the atmosphere.

name: Biophysics
fact: Biophysics is an interdisciplinary science that applies methods traditionally used in physics to study biological phenomena.

name: Chemical physics
fact: Chemical physics is a branch of physics that studies chemical processes from a physical point of view.

name: Polymer physics
fact: Polymer physics is the field of physics that studies polymers, their fluctuations and mechanical properties.

name: Mathematical physics
fact: Mathematical physics is the development of mathematical methods for use in physics and their applications.

name: Action at a distance
fact: Action at a distance is the concept that an object's motion can be affected by another object without the two being in physical contact.

name: Principle of locality
fact: The principle of locality states that an object is influenced directly only by its immediate surroundings.

name: Arrow of time
fact: The arrow of time is the concept positing the one-way direction or asymmetry of time.

name: Curved spacetime
fact: Curved spacetime is the mathematical model in which, with general relativity, gravity naturally arises.

name: Physical property
fact: A physical property is any property of a physical system that is measurable.

name: Physicist
fact: A physicist is a scientist who specializes in physics, the interactions of matter and energy at all length and time scales.

name: Physics education
fact: Physics education refers to the education methods currently used to teach physics.

name: Exotic matter
fact: Exotic matter includes hypothetical particles and states of matter that have not yet been encountered.

name: Fifth force
fact: A fifth force is a hypothetical fundamental interaction beyond the four known interactions: gravitational, electromagnetic, strong nuclear and weak nuclear.

name: Quantum Hall effect
fact: The quantum Hall effect is a quantized version of the Hall effect, observed in two-dimensional electron systems at low temperatures and strong magnetic fields.

name: Faraday effect
fact: The Faraday effect is a magneto-optical phenomenon that causes a polarization rotation proportional to the magnetic field along the direction of the light.

name: Compton scattering
fact: Compton scattering is the quantum theory of scattering of a high-frequency photon through an interaction with a charged particle, usually an electron.

name: Cyclotron radiation
fact: Cyclotron radiation is electromagnetic radiation emitted by accelerating charged particles deflected by a magnetic field.

name: Photoluminescence
fact: Photoluminescence is light emission from matter after absorbing photons.

name: Scintillator
fact: A scintillator is a material that exhibits scintillation, a kind of luminescence, when excited by ionizing radiation.

name: Radiometry
fact: Radiometry is a set of techniques for measuring electromagnetic radiation, including visible light.

name: Irradiance
fact: Irradiance is the radiant flux received by a surface per unit area.

name: Electrical conductor
fact: An electrical conductor is an object or material that allows the flow of charge, electric current, in one or more directions.

name: Ground (electricity)
fact: In electrical engineering, ground may refer to a reference point in an electrical circuit from which voltages are measured.

name: Electric power
fact: Electric power is the rate of transfer of electrical energy within a circuit.

name: AC power
fact: In alternating current circuits, energy storage elements such as inductors and capacitors may result in periodic reversals of the direction of energy flow.

name: Electrical resistivity and conductivity
fact: Electrical resistivity and conductivity are intrinsic properties of materials that measure their ability to conduct electric current.

name: Electric flux
fact: Electric flux is the total electric field that crosses a given surface.

name: Magnetohydrodynamics
fact: Magnetohydrodynamics is a model of electrically conducting fluids that treats all types of charged particles together as a single continuous fluid.

name: Zeroth law of thermodynamics
fact: The zeroth law of thermodynamics provides an independent definition of temperature without reference to entropy.

name: First law of thermodynamics
fact: The first law of thermodynamics is the law of conservation of energy applied to thermodynamic processes.

name: Second law of thermodynamics
fact: The second law of thermodynamics says that heat always flows spontaneously from hotter to colder regions of matter.

name: Third law of thermodynamics
fact: The third law of thermodynamics says the entropy of a closed system approaches a constant value as its temperature approaches absolute zero.

name: Heat capacity ratio
fact: The heat capacity ratio is also known as the adiabatic index, the ratio of specific heats, or Laplace's coefficient.

name: Latent heat
fact: Latent heat is energy released or absorbed during a constant-temperature process such as melting or condensation.

name: Heat equation
fact: The heat equation models how the temperature of a body evolves through time.

name: Thermal insulation
fact: Thermal insulation is the reduction of heat transfer between objects in thermal contact.

name: Newton's law of cooling
fact: Newton's law of cooling says a body loses heat at a rate proportional to its temperature difference from its surroundings.

name: Brayton cycle
fact: The Brayton cycle, also known as the Joule cycle, describes heat engines that use air or another gas as the working fluid.

name: Carnot cycle
fact: A Carnot cycle is an ideal thermodynamic cycle proposed by the French physicist Sadi Carnot.

name: Ericsson cycle
fact: The Ericsson cycle is named after the inventor John Ericsson, who designed and built many unique heat engines.

name: Heat pump and refrigeration cycle
fact: Heat pump and refrigeration cycles are the models behind heat pump, air conditioning and refrigeration systems.

name: Otto cycle
fact: The Otto cycle is an idealized thermodynamic cycle that describes a typical spark ignition piston engine.

name: Rankine cycle
fact: The Rankine cycle describes how heat engines such as steam turbines extract mechanical work from a fluid moving between a heat source and a heat sink.

name: Stirling cycle
fact: The Stirling cycle describes the general class of Stirling devices, including the original Stirling engine.

name: Ideal gas
fact: An ideal gas is a theoretical gas of many randomly moving point particles that do not interact with each other.

name: Heat engine
fact: A heat engine is a system that transfers thermal energy to do mechanical or electrical work.

name: Carnot heat engine
fact: A Carnot heat engine is a theoretical heat engine that operates on the Carnot cycle.

name: Stirling engine
fact: A Stirling engine runs on the cyclic expansion and contraction of a gas exposed to different temperatures.

name: Energy conversion efficiency
fact: Energy conversion efficiency is the ratio between the useful output of an energy conversion machine and its input.

name: Kinetic theory of gases
fact: The kinetic theory of gases is a simple classical model of the thermodynamic behavior of gases.

name: Effusion
fact: Effusion is the process in which a gas escapes from a container through a very small hole.

name: Mean free path
fact: The mean free path is the average distance a moving particle travels before substantially changing its direction or energy.

name: Equation of state
fact: An equation of state relates state variables such as pressure, volume, temperature and internal energy.

name: Gibbs free energy
fact: Gibbs free energy is a thermodynamic potential used to calculate the maximum work a closed system can do at constant temperature and pressure.

name: Thermal radiation
fact: Thermal radiation is electromagnetic radiation emitted by the thermal motion of particles in matter.

name: Black body
fact: A black body is an idealized body that absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation.

name: Planck's law
fact: Planck's law describes the spectral density of electromagnetic radiation emitted by a black body in thermal equilibrium.

name: Stefan–Boltzmann law
fact: The Stefan–Boltzmann law describes the intensity of thermal radiation emitted by matter in terms of its temperature.

name: Ultraviolet catastrophe
fact: The ultraviolet catastrophe was the classical prediction that an ideal black body would emit unbounded energy at short wavelengths.

name: Equipartition theorem
fact: The equipartition theorem relates the temperature of a system to its average energies.

name: Adiabatic process
fact: An adiabatic process occurs without transferring heat between a thermodynamic system and its environment.

name: Isentropic process
fact: An isentropic process is an idealized thermodynamic process that is both adiabatic and reversible.

name: Joule–Thomson effect
fact: The Joule–Thomson effect describes the temperature change of a real gas or liquid as it expands through a valve or porous plug.

name: Isothermal process
fact: An isothermal process is a thermodynamic process in which the temperature of a system stays constant.

name: Endothermic process
fact: An endothermic process is a chemical or physical process that absorbs heat from its surroundings.

name: Exothermic process
fact: An exothermic process releases energy from the system to its surroundings, usually as heat.

name: Reversible process
fact: A reversible process is one whose direction can be reversed by infinitesimal changes in the surroundings.

name: Irreversible process
fact: An irreversible process is a thermodynamic process that is impossible to reverse or undo.

name: Chemical potential
fact: The chemical potential of a species is the energy absorbed or released when its particle number changes.

name: Thermodynamic system
fact: A thermodynamic system is a body of matter or radiation, separate from its surroundings, that can be studied using the laws of thermodynamics.

name: Closed system
fact: A closed system does not allow transfer of matter in or out of the system.

name: Brownian motion
fact: Brownian motion is the random motion of particles suspended in a liquid or a gas.

name: Photon gas
fact: A photon gas is a gas-like collection of photons that has pressure, temperature and entropy like a conventional gas.

name: Thermal energy
fact: The term thermal energy is often used ambiguously in physics and engineering.

name: Thermal equilibrium
fact: Two systems are in thermal equilibrium if there is no net flow of thermal energy between them.

name: Thermal expansion
fact: Thermal expansion is the tendency of matter to increase in size with increasing temperature.

name: Partial pressure
fact: The partial pressure of a gas in a mixture is the pressure it would have if it alone occupied the whole volume.

name: Pressure gradient
fact: The pressure gradient describes in which direction and how fast the pressure increases most rapidly around a location.

name: Standard temperature and pressure
fact: Standard temperature and pressure are standard sets of conditions for experimental measurements, used to compare different data.

name: Cold
fact: Cold is the presence of low temperature, especially in the atmosphere.

name: Thermodynamic temperature
fact: Thermodynamic temperature, also called absolute temperature, is measured from absolute zero.

name: Maxwell's demon
fact: Maxwell's demon is a thought experiment that appears to disprove the second law of thermodynamics.

name: Boltzmann's entropy formula
fact: Boltzmann's entropy formula relates the entropy of an ideal gas to the number of microstates corresponding to its macrostate.

name: Transverse wave
fact: A transverse wave oscillates perpendicularly to the direction of the wave's advance.

name: Longitudinal wave
fact: A longitudinal wave oscillates in the direction parallel to the direction in which the wave travels.

name: Mechanical wave
fact: A mechanical wave is an oscillation of matter that transfers energy through an elastic material medium.

name: Wavenumber
fact: The wavenumber, also known as repetency, is the spatial frequency of a wave.

name: Wave vector
fact: A wave vector is a vector used in describing a wave. It has a magnitude and direction.

name: Fraunhofer diffraction
fact: The Fraunhofer diffraction equation models the diffraction of plane waves incident on an object, viewed at a long distance.

name: Huygens–Fresnel principle
fact: The Huygens–Fresnel principle states that every point on a wavefront is itself the source of spherical wavelets.

name: Fermat's principle
fact: Fermat's principle, also known as the principle of least time, links ray optics and wave optics.

name: Bragg's law
fact: Bragg's law gives the angles for coherent scattering of waves from a large crystal lattice.

name: Harmonic
fact: A harmonic is a sinusoidal wave whose frequency is a whole-number multiple of the fundamental frequency.

name: Group velocity
fact: The group velocity of a wave is the velocity with which the overall envelope of its amplitudes propagates through space.

name: Shock wave
fact: A shock wave is a propagating disturbance that moves faster than the local speed of sound in the medium.

name: Waveform
fact: The waveform of a signal is the shape of its graph as a function of time.

name: Coherence
fact: Coherence expresses the potential for two waves to interfere.

name: Standing wave
fact: A standing wave oscillates in time but its peak amplitude profile does not move in space.

name: Sonic boom
fact: A sonic boom is the sound of shock waves created when an object travels through the air faster than sound.

name: Sound pressure
fact: Sound pressure is the pressure difference between the ambient atmospheric pressure and that of a sound wave.

name: Loudness
fact: Loudness is the subjective perception of sound pressure.

name: Beat
fact: A beat is an interference pattern between two sounds of slightly different frequencies, heard as a periodic variation in volume.

name: Acoustic resonance
fact: Acoustic resonance is when an acoustic system responds strongly to sound waves matching one of its natural frequencies.

name: Caustic
fact: A caustic is the envelope of light rays reflected or refracted by a curved surface or object.

name: Optical aberration
fact: Aberration is a property of optical systems that makes the image not a true reproduction of the object.

name: Chromatic aberration
fact: Chromatic aberration is a failure of a lens to focus all colors to the same point.

name: Spherical aberration
fact: Spherical aberration is a type of aberration found in optical systems with spherical surfaces.

name: Photonics
fact: Photonics is the branch of optics that generates, detects and manipulates light in the form of photons.

name: Circular polarization
fact: In circular polarization the field of the wave has a constant magnitude and rotates at a constant rate.

name: Curved mirror
fact: A curved mirror is a mirror with a curved reflecting surface, either convex or concave.

name: Total internal reflection
fact: In total internal reflection, waves reaching a boundary between two media are completely reflected back.

name: Photonic crystal
fact: A photonic crystal is an optical nanostructure in which the refractive index changes periodically.

name: Opacity
fact: Opacity is the measure of impenetrability to electromagnetic or other radiation, especially visible light.

name: Optical depth
fact: Optical depth is the natural logarithm of the ratio of incident to transmitted radiant power through a material.

name: Birefringence
fact: Birefringence, or double refraction, is when the refractive index of a material depends on the polarization and direction of light.

name: Virtual image
fact: In optics, the image of an object is the collection of focus points of light rays coming from the object.

name: Iridescence
fact: Iridescence is the phenomenon of surfaces that appear gradually to change colour as the angle of view changes.

name: Magnification
fact: Magnification is the process of enlarging the apparent size, not the physical size, of something.

name: Moiré pattern
fact: A moiré pattern is a large-scale interference pattern produced when one ruled pattern is overlaid on another similar pattern.

name: Illuminance
fact: Illuminance is the total luminous flux incident on a surface, per unit area.

name: Luminance
fact: Luminance is a photometric measure of the luminous intensity per unit area of light travelling in a given direction.

name: Luminous flux
fact: Luminous flux is the measure of the perceived power of light.

name: Luminous intensity
fact: Luminous intensity is a measure of the wavelength-weighted power a light source emits in a particular direction.

name: Contrast
fact: Contrast is the difference in luminance or color that makes an object distinguishable from its background.

name: Terahertz radiation
fact: Terahertz radiation, also called T-rays, consists of electromagnetic waves between a tenth of a terahertz and ten terahertz.

name: Reflection coefficient
fact: The reflection coefficient describes how much of a wave is reflected by an impedance discontinuity in the medium.

name: Bulk modulus
fact: The bulk modulus of a substance is a measure of its resistance to bulk compression.

name: Poisson's ratio
fact: Poisson's ratio measures the deformation of a material in directions perpendicular to the direction of loading.

name: Brittleness
fact: A material is brittle if it fractures under stress with little elastic or plastic deformation.

name: Ductility
fact: Ductility is the ability of a material to sustain significant plastic deformation before fracture under tension.

name: Rigid body
fact: A rigid body is a solid body in which deformation is zero or negligible under an applied force.

name: Shear modulus
fact: The shear modulus, or modulus of rigidity, is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain.

name: Compression
fact: Compression is the application of balanced inward pushing forces that reduce the size of a material or structure.

name: Tension
fact: Tension is the pulling or stretching force transmitted along an object such as a string, rope or chain.

name: Shear stress
fact: Shear stress is the component of stress coplanar with a material cross section.

name: Toughness
fact: Toughness is the ability of a material to absorb energy and deform plastically without fracturing.

name: Soil mechanics
fact: Soil mechanics is a branch of soil physics and applied mechanics that describes the behavior of soils.

name: Angle of repose
fact: The angle of repose of a granular material is the steepest angle at which it can be piled without slumping.

name: Rheology
fact: Rheology is the study of the flow of matter, primarily in a fluid state, and of soft solids.

name: Vorticity
fact: Vorticity describes the local spinning motion of a continuum near some point.

name: Laminar flow
fact: In laminar flow fluid particles follow smooth paths in layers, with little or no mixing.

name: Mach number
fact: The Mach number is the ratio of flow velocity past a boundary to the local speed of sound.

name: Magnus effect
fact: The Magnus effect occurs when a spinning object moves through a fluid.

name: Pipe flow
fact: Pipe flow is a type of fluid flow within a closed conduit such as a pipe, duct or tube.

name: Compressible flow
fact: Compressible flow is the branch of fluid mechanics that deals with flows with significant changes in fluid density.

name: Incompressible flow
fact: Incompressible flow is a flow in which the material density does not vary over time.

name: Flow velocity
fact: Flow velocity is a vector field used to mathematically describe the motion of a continuum.

name: Computational fluid dynamics
fact: Computational fluid dynamics uses numerical analysis and data structures to analyze and solve problems that involve flows.

name: Angular frequency
fact: Angular frequency, also called angular speed, is a scalar measure of the angle rate, the rate of change of the phase of a sinusoidal waveform.

name: Density of states
fact: The density of states of a system describes the number of allowed states per unit energy range.

name: Detailed balance
fact: The principle of detailed balance says that in equilibrium the flux of energy transfer must be equal in both directions.

name: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution
fact: The Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution is a probability distribution named after James Clerk Maxwell and Ludwig Boltzmann.

name: Canonical ensemble
fact: A canonical ensemble represents the possible states of a mechanical system in thermal equilibrium with a heat bath at a fixed temperature.

name: Microcanonical ensemble
fact: The microcanonical ensemble represents the possible states of a mechanical system whose total energy is exactly specified.

name: Grand canonical ensemble
fact: The grand canonical ensemble represents the possible states of a system of particles in thermodynamic equilibrium with a reservoir.

name: Fluctuation–dissipation theorem
fact: The fluctuation–dissipation theorem is a tool in statistical physics for predicting the behavior of systems that obey detailed balance.

name: Indistinguishable particles
fact: Indistinguishable particles are particles that cannot be distinguished from one another, even in principle.

name: Microstate
fact: A microstate is a specific configuration of a system that describes the precise positions and momenta of all its particles.

name: Molecular diffusion
fact: Molecular diffusion is the motion of atoms, molecules or other particles of a gas or liquid at temperatures above absolute zero.

name: Bose–Einstein statistics
fact: Bose–Einstein statistics describes one of two ways identical non-interacting particles may occupy a set of discrete energy states.

name: Fermi–Dirac statistics
fact: Fermi–Dirac statistics applies to systems of many identical non-interacting particles that obey the Pauli exclusion principle.

name: Fermi energy
fact: The Fermi energy is the energy difference between the highest and lowest occupied single-particle states of non-interacting fermions at absolute zero.

name: Partition function
fact: A partition function describes the statistical properties of a system in thermodynamic equilibrium.

name: H-theorem
fact: The H-theorem, introduced by Ludwig Boltzmann, describes a quantity that tends to decrease in a nearly ideal gas of molecules.

name: Loschmidt's paradox
fact: Loschmidt's paradox is the objection that it should not be possible to deduce an irreversible process from time-symmetric dynamics.

name: Maxwell relations
fact: The Maxwell relations in thermodynamics follow from the symmetry of second derivatives and the definitions of the thermodynamic potentials.

name: Thermal fluctuations
fact: Thermal fluctuations are random deviations of an atomic system from its average state.

name: Thermodynamic limit
fact: The thermodynamic limit of a system is the limit for a large number of particles with volume growing in proportion.

name: Boltzmann equation
fact: The Boltzmann equation describes the statistical behaviour of a thermodynamic system not in equilibrium.

name: Entropy of mixing
fact: The entropy of mixing is the increase in total entropy when initially separate systems of different composition are mixed.

name: Fluctuation theorem
fact: The fluctuation theorem deals with the probability that the entropy of a system away from equilibrium will increase or decrease over time.

name: Thermodynamic state
fact: A thermodynamic state of a system is its condition at a specific time, identified by values of state variables.

name: Nucleon
fact: A nucleon is either a proton or a neutron, considered in its role as a component of an atomic nucleus.

name: Radionuclide
fact: A radionuclide is an unstable nuclide that undergoes radioactive decay into a different nuclide.

name: Nuclear binding energy
fact: Nuclear binding energy is the minimum energy required to fully disassemble a nucleus into its protons and neutrons.

name: Cold fusion
fact: Cold fusion is a hypothesized type of nuclear reaction that would occur at or near room temperature.

name: Nuclear reaction
fact: A nuclear reaction is a process in which two nuclei, or a nucleus and a subatomic particle, collide to produce new nuclides.

name: Nuclear chain reaction
fact: A nuclear chain reaction occurs when one nuclear reaction causes on average one or more further reactions, so the series can sustain itself.

name: Nuclear isomer
fact: A nuclear isomer is a metastable state of an atomic nucleus in which one or more nucleons occupy higher energy levels.

name: Nuclear force
fact: The nuclear force acts between hadrons, most commonly between the protons and neutrons of atoms.

name: Nuclear structure
fact: Understanding the structure of the atomic nucleus is one of the central challenges in nuclear physics.

name: Nuclear magnetic resonance
fact: In nuclear magnetic resonance, nuclei in a strong magnetic field disturbed by a weak oscillating field respond with an electromagnetic signal.

name: Electron paramagnetic resonance
fact: Electron paramagnetic resonance is a method for studying materials that have unpaired electrons.

name: Magnetic resonance
fact: Magnetic resonance is a process by which a physical excitation is set up via magnetism.

name: Island of stability
fact: The island of stability is a predicted set of superheavy isotopes that may have considerably longer half-lives than known ones.

name: Hypernucleus
fact: A hypernucleus is like an ordinary atomic nucleus but contains at least one hyperon as well as protons and neutrons.

name: Isotope separation
fact: Isotope separation is the process of concentrating specific isotopes of an element by removing other isotopes.

name: Alpha decay
fact: Alpha decay is a type of radioactive decay in which an atomic nucleus emits an alpha particle.

name: Neutron radiation
fact: Neutron radiation is a form of ionizing radiation that presents as free neutrons.

name: Decay product
fact: A decay product is the remaining nuclide left over from radioactive decay.

name: Decay energy
fact: The decay energy is the energy change of a nucleus that has undergone radioactive decay.

name: Radioactive source
fact: A radioactive source is a known quantity of a radionuclide that emits ionizing radiation.

name: Semi-empirical mass formula
fact: The semi-empirical mass formula approximates the mass of an atomic nucleus from its numbers of protons and neutrons.

name: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
fact: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy is based on the re-orientation of atomic nuclei with nuclear spin in an external magnetic field.

name: Elastic scattering
fact: Elastic scattering is a form of particle scattering in which the internal states of the particles stay the same.

name: Inelastic scattering
fact: Inelastic scattering is a process in which the internal states of a particle or system change after a collision.

name: Annihilation
fact: Annihilation occurs when a subatomic particle collides with its antiparticle to produce other particles.

name: CP violation
fact: CP violation is a violation of charge conjugation parity symmetry, the combination of charge and parity symmetry.

name: CPT symmetry
fact: Charge, parity and time reversal symmetry is a fundamental symmetry of physical laws.

name: Electroweak interaction
fact: The electroweak interaction is the unified description of electromagnetism and the weak interaction.

name: Feynman diagram
fact: A Feynman diagram is a pictorial representation of the mathematics describing the behavior and interaction of subatomic particles.

name: Particle decay
fact: Particle decay is the spontaneous process of one unstable subatomic particle transforming into multiple other particles.

name: Free neutron decay
fact: A free neutron is a neutron that is not bound to an atomic nucleus.

name: Charge conservation
fact: Charge conservation is the principle that the total electric charge in an isolated system never changes.

name: Quark model
fact: The quark model is a classification scheme for hadrons in terms of their valence quarks.

name: Symmetry breaking
fact: Symmetry breaking is a phenomenon where a disordered but symmetric state collapses into an ordered but less symmetric state.

name: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
fact: In spontaneous symmetry breaking a physical system in a symmetric state spontaneously ends up in an asymmetric state.

name: Baryon asymmetry
fact: The baryon asymmetry problem is the observed imbalance of matter over antimatter in the observable universe.

name: Vacuum energy
fact: Vacuum energy is an underlying background energy that exists in space throughout the entire universe.

name: Baryon number
fact: The baryon number is an additive quantum number of a system.

name: Lepton number
fact: Lepton number is a conserved quantum number representing the difference between the numbers of leptons and antileptons in a reaction.

name: Color charge
fact: Color charge is a property of quarks and gluons related to their strong interactions.

name: Strangeness
fact: Strangeness is a property of particles, expressed as a quantum number, used to describe their decay.

name: Isospin
fact: Isospin is a quantum number related to the up and down quark content of a particle.

name: Hypercharge
fact: Hypercharge is a quantum number conserved under the strong interaction.

name: Chirality
fact: A chiral phenomenon is one that is not identical to its mirror image.

name: Linear particle accelerator
fact: A linear particle accelerator speeds up charged particles by subjecting them to oscillating electric potentials along a straight beamline.

name: Synchrotron
fact: A synchrotron is a cyclic particle accelerator in which the beam travels around a fixed closed-loop path.

name: Semiconductor detector
fact: A semiconductor detector uses a semiconductor, usually silicon or germanium, to measure incident charged particles or photons.

name: Calorimeter
fact: In particle physics, a calorimeter is a detector that measures the energy of particles.

name: Bubble chamber
fact: A bubble chamber is a vessel of superheated transparent liquid used to detect electrically charged particles moving through it.

name: Elementary particle
fact: An elementary particle is a subatomic particle that is not composed of other particles.

name: Massless particle
fact: A massless particle is an elementary particle whose invariant mass is zero.

name: Virtual particle
fact: A virtual particle is a theoretical transient particle whose existence is limited by the uncertainty principle.

name: Tachyon
fact: A tachyon is a hypothetical particle that always travels faster than light.

name: Hyperon
fact: A hyperon is any baryon containing one or more strange quarks, but no charm, bottom or top quarks.

name: Pentaquark
fact: A pentaquark is a subatomic particle consisting of four quarks and one antiquark bound together.

name: Pion
fact: A pion, or pi meson, is any of three subatomic particles, each made of a quark and an antiquark.

name: Kaon
fact: A kaon is any of a group of four mesons distinguished by a quantum number called strangeness.

name: Tetraquark
fact: A tetraquark is an exotic meson composed of four valence quarks.

name: Force carrier
fact: A force carrier is a type of particle that gives rise to forces between other particles.

name: Graviton
fact: The graviton is the hypothetical elementary particle that mediates the force of gravitational interaction.

name: Axion
fact: An axion is a hypothetical elementary particle theorized to solve the strong charge-parity problem.

name: Grand Unified Theory
fact: A Grand Unified Theory merges the electromagnetic, weak and strong forces into a single force at high energies.

name: Neutrino oscillation
fact: In neutrino oscillation, a neutrino created with one lepton family number can later be measured with a different one.

name: Proton decay
fact: Proton decay is a key process for testing the stability of matter and baryon number conservation.

name: Loop quantum gravity
fact: Loop quantum gravity is a theory of quantum gravity that incorporates the matter of the Standard Model.

name: D-brane
fact: In string theory, D-branes are extended objects upon which open strings can end.

name: M-theory
fact: M-theory is a theory that unifies all consistent versions of superstring theory.

name: Superstring theory
fact: Superstring theory tries to explain all particles and fundamental forces as vibrations of tiny supersymmetric strings.

name: Supergravity
fact: Supergravity is a modern field theory that combines the principles of supersymmetry and general relativity.

name: Theory of everything
fact: A theory of everything is a hypothetical coherent theoretical framework of physics containing all physical principles.

name: Unified field theory
fact: A unified field theory writes all fundamental forces of nature and all elementary particles in terms of a single physical field.

name: Higgs mechanism
fact: The Higgs mechanism explains how gauge bosons acquire the property of mass.

name: Yang–Mills theory
fact: Yang–Mills theory is a quantum field theory for nuclear binding devised by Chen Ning Yang and Robert Mills.

name: Dirac equation
fact: The Dirac equation is a relativistic wave equation derived by the British physicist Paul Dirac.

name: Pauli matrices
fact: The Pauli matrices are a set of three complex matrices that are traceless, Hermitian, involutory and unitary.

name: Expectation value
fact: In quantum mechanics, the expectation value is the probabilistic expected value of the result of an experiment.

name: Gyromagnetic ratio
fact: The gyromagnetic ratio of a particle or system is the ratio of its magnetic moment to its angular momentum.

name: De Broglie–Bohm theory
fact: The de Broglie–Bohm theory, or pilot wave theory, says a particle has a definite position at all times, even when unobserved.

name: Matrix mechanics
fact: Matrix mechanics is a formulation of quantum mechanics created by Werner Heisenberg, Max Born and Pascual Jordan.

name: Perturbation theory
fact: Perturbation theory finds an approximate solution to a problem by starting from the exact solution of a related, simpler one.

name: Probability amplitude
fact: A probability amplitude is a complex number used for describing the behaviour of quantum systems.

name: Quantization
fact: Quantization is the systematic transition from a classical understanding of physical phenomena to quantum mechanics.

name: Propagator
fact: The propagator is a function giving the probability amplitude for a particle to travel from one place to another in a given time.

name: Quantum number
fact: Quantum numbers are quantities that characterize the possible states of a system.

name: Bound state
fact: A bound state is a composite of two or more building blocks that behaves as a single object and needs energy to be split.

name: Topological order
fact: Topological order describes a phase of matter that arises in a system with non-local interactions such as entanglement.

name: Stationary state
fact: A stationary state is a quantum state with all observables independent of time.

name: WKB approximation
fact: The WKB approximation is a technique for finding approximate solutions to linear differential equations with spatially varying coefficients.

name: Finite potential well
fact: The finite potential well is a concept from quantum mechanics: a particle confined to a box with finite walls.

name: Delta potential
fact: The delta potential is a potential well described mathematically by the Dirac delta function.

name: Wu experiment
fact: The Wu experiment was a particle and nuclear physics experiment conducted by the physicist Chien-Shiung Wu.

name: Charge density
fact: Charge density is the amount of electric charge per unit length, surface area or volume.

name: Electric dipole moment
fact: The electric dipole moment is a measure of the separation of positive and negative charges within a system.

name: Electric displacement field
fact: The electric displacement field, also called electric flux density, is a vector field that appears in Maxwell's equations.

name: Electric-field screening
fact: Screening is the damping of electric fields caused by the presence of mobile charge carriers.

name: Debye length
fact: The Debye length measures a charge carrier's net electrostatic effect in a plasma or electrolyte and how far it persists.

name: Electric potential energy
fact: Electric potential energy results from conservative Coulomb forces and is associated with the configuration of a set of point charges.

name: Electric susceptibility
fact: The electric susceptibility indicates the degree of polarization of a dielectric material in response to an applied electric field.

name: Electrostatic induction
fact: Electrostatic induction is a redistribution of electric charge in an object caused by the influence of nearby charges.

name: Permittivity
fact: Permittivity is a measure of the electric polarizability of a dielectric material.

name: Polarization density
fact: Polarization density is the vector field that expresses the density of electric dipole moments in a dielectric material.

name: Ampère's force law
fact: Ampère's force law describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two current-carrying wires.

name: Biot–Savart law
fact: The Biot–Savart law describes the magnetic field generated by a constant electric current.

name: Magnetic monopole
fact: A magnetic monopole is a hypothetical particle that is an isolated magnet with only one magnetic pole.

name: Potts model
fact: The Potts model, a generalization of the Ising model, is a model of interacting spins on a crystalline lattice.

name: Permeability
fact: Permeability is the measure of magnetization produced in a material in response to an applied magnetic field.

name: Current density
fact: Current density is the electric current that flows through a unit area of a chosen cross section.

name: Gauss's law for magnetism
fact: Gauss's law for magnetism is one of the four Maxwell's equations that underlie classical electrodynamics.

name: Poynting's theorem
fact: Poynting's theorem is a statement of conservation of energy for electromagnetic fields.

name: Retarded time
fact: In electromagnetism, an electromagnetic wave in vacuum travels at a finite speed.

name: Electromagnetic wave equation
fact: The electromagnetic wave equation describes the propagation of electromagnetic waves through a medium or in a vacuum.

name: Absorption band
fact: An absorption band is a range of wavelengths in the electromagnetic spectrum characteristic of a particular transition in a substance.

name: Larmor formula
fact: The Larmor formula is used to calculate the total power radiated by a nonrelativistic point charge as it accelerates.

name: Near and far field
fact: The near field and far field are regions of the electromagnetic field around an object such as a transmitting antenna.

name: Point source
fact: A point source is a single identifiable localized source of something.

name: Poynting vector
fact: The Poynting vector represents the directional energy flux of an electromagnetic field.

name: Radiance
fact: Radiance is the radiant flux emitted, reflected, transmitted or received by a surface, per unit solid angle per unit projected area.

name: Radiant flux
fact: Radiant flux is the radiant energy emitted, reflected, transmitted or received per unit time.

name: Radiative transfer
fact: Radiative transfer is the physical phenomenon of energy transfer in the form of electromagnetic radiation.

name: Spectral density
fact: The power spectrum of a signal describes the distribution of power into its frequency components.

name: Transverse mode
fact: A transverse mode is a particular electromagnetic field pattern in the plane perpendicular to the radiation's direction of travel.

name: Electrical reactance
fact: Reactance is the opposition presented to alternating current by inductance and capacitance.

name: Depletion region
fact: The depletion region is an insulating region within a conductive, doped semiconductor where the mobile charge carriers have diffused away.

name: Ohmic contact
fact: An ohmic contact is a non-rectifying electrical junction between two conductors.

name: Classical electromagnetism
fact: Classical electromagnetism studies the interactions between electric charges and currents using an extension of the classical Newtonian model.

name: Physical constant
fact: A physical constant is a non-varying quantity that appears in a theory or model of some physical phenomena.

name: Elementary charge
fact: The elementary charge is the magnitude of the charge on an electron and a fundamental physical constant.

name: Gravitational constant
fact: The gravitational constant is an empirical physical constant that gives the strength of the gravitational field induced by a mass.

name: Planck constant
fact: The Planck constant is a fundamental physical constant of foundational importance in quantum mechanics.

name: Boltzmann constant
fact: The Boltzmann constant relates the average thermal energy of particles in a gas with the thermodynamic temperature of the gas.

name: Vacuum permittivity
fact: Vacuum permittivity is the value of the absolute dielectric permittivity of classical vacuum.

name: Vacuum permeability
fact: The vacuum permeability is the magnetic permeability in a classical vacuum.

name: Impedance of free space
fact: The impedance of free space is a physical constant relating the electric and magnetic fields of radiation travelling through free space.

name: Rydberg constant
fact: The Rydberg constant, named after the Swedish physicist Johannes Rydberg, relates to the electromagnetic spectra of an atom.

name: Principal quantum number
fact: The principal quantum number of an electron indicates which electron shell or energy level it is in.

name: Spin quantum number
fact: The spin quantum number describes the intrinsic angular momentum of an electron or other particle.

name: Fine structure
fact: The fine structure is the splitting of the spectral lines of atoms due to electron spin and relativistic corrections.

name: Hyperfine structure
fact: Hyperfine structure is defined by small shifts and splittings in the electronic energy levels of atoms, molecules and ions.

name: Spin–orbit interaction
fact: The spin–orbit interaction is a relativistic interaction of a particle's spin with its motion inside a potential.

name: Degenerate energy levels
fact: An energy level is degenerate if it corresponds to two or more different measurable states of a quantum system.

name: Hydrogen spectral series
fact: The emission spectrum of atomic hydrogen is divided into a number of spectral series, with wavelengths given by the Rydberg formula.

name: Hydrogen-alpha
fact: Hydrogen-alpha is a deep-red visible spectral line of the hydrogen atom.

name: Einstein coefficients
fact: The Einstein coefficients describe the probability of absorption or emission of a photon by an atom or molecule.

name: Rigid rotor
fact: The rigid rotor is a mechanical model of rotating systems.

name: Rotational spectroscopy
fact: Rotational spectroscopy measures the energies of transitions between quantized rotational states of gas-phase molecules.

name: Spherical harmonics
fact: Spherical harmonics are special functions defined on the surface of a sphere.

name: Density functional theory
fact: Density functional theory is a computational quantum mechanical method for investigating the electronic structure of many-body systems.

name: Exotic atom
fact: An exotic atom is an otherwise normal atom in which one or more subatomic particles have been replaced by other particles.

name: Triclinic crystal system
fact: The triclinic crystal system is the least symmetrical of the seven crystal systems.

name: Monoclinic crystal system
fact: The monoclinic crystal system is one of the seven crystal systems.

name: Orthorhombic crystal system
fact: The orthorhombic crystal system is one of the seven crystal systems.

name: Tetragonal crystal system
fact: The tetragonal crystal system is one of the seven crystal systems.

name: Brillouin zone
fact: The first Brillouin zone is a uniquely defined primitive cell in reciprocal space.

name: Fermi surface
fact: The Fermi surface separates occupied from unoccupied electron states at zero temperature.

name: Crystal optics
fact: Crystal optics describes the behaviour of light in anisotropic media such as crystals.

name: Interstitial defect
fact: An interstitial defect is a point defect in which an atom occupies an interstitial site in the crystal structure.

name: Atomic packing factor
fact: The atomic packing factor is the fraction of volume in a crystal structure that is occupied by constituent particles.

name: Coordination number
fact: The coordination number of a central atom is the number of atoms, molecules or ions bonded to it.

name: Crystal polymorphism
fact: Polymorphism is when a compound or element can crystallize into more than one crystal structure.

name: Crystal growth
fact: Crystal growth is the addition of new atoms, ions or polymer strings into the arrangement of the crystalline lattice.

name: Grain growth
fact: Grain growth is the increase in size of grains in a material at high temperature.

name: Bloch's theorem
fact: Bloch's theorem states that solutions to the Schrödinger equation in a periodic potential are plane waves modulated by periodic functions.

name: Free electron model
fact: The free electron model is a quantum mechanical model for the behaviour of charge carriers in a metallic solid.

name: Hubbard model
fact: The Hubbard model is a simplified model used to describe the transition between conducting and insulating systems.

name: Polaron
fact: A polaron is a quasiparticle used to understand the interactions between electrons and atoms in a solid.

name: Supersolid
fact: A supersolid is a spatially ordered, solid material with superfluid properties.

name: Superheating
fact: Superheating is the phenomenon in which a liquid is heated to a temperature higher than its boiling point without boiling.

name: Superheated steam
fact: Superheated steam is steam at a temperature higher than its vaporization point at the pressure where it is measured.

name: Phase rule
fact: The phase rule is a general principle governing multi-component, multi-phase systems in thermodynamic equilibrium.

name: Bose gas
fact: An ideal Bose gas is a quantum-mechanical phase of matter, analogous to a classical ideal gas.

name: Einstein solid
fact: The Einstein solid models a crystalline solid as a large number of independent quantum harmonic oscillators of the same frequency.

name: Nanoparticle
fact: A nanoparticle or ultrafine particle is a particle of matter between one and one hundred nanometres in diameter.

name: Mesoscopic physics
fact: Mesoscopic physics is a subdiscipline of condensed matter physics that deals with materials of an intermediate size.

name: Stress–energy tensor
fact: The stress–energy tensor describes the density and flux of energy and momentum at each point in spacetime.

name: Four-vector
fact: In special relativity, a four-vector is an object with four components that transform under Lorentz transformations.

name: Four-momentum
fact: Four-momentum is the generalization of the classical three-dimensional momentum to four-dimensional spacetime.

name: Rapidity
fact: In special relativity, velocity is converted to rapidity to accommodate the limit set by the speed of light.

name: Penrose diagram
fact: A Penrose diagram is a two-dimensional diagram capturing the causal relations between different points in spacetime.

name: Poincaré group
fact: The Poincaré group was first defined by Hermann Minkowski as the isometry group of Minkowski spacetime.

name: General covariance
fact: General covariance is the invariance of the form of physical laws under arbitrary differentiable coordinate transformations.

name: Einstein field equations
fact: The Einstein field equations relate the geometry of spacetime to the distribution of matter and energy within it.

name: Geodesics in general relativity
fact: In general relativity, a geodesic generalizes the notion of a straight line to curved spacetime.

name: Kerr–Newman metric
fact: The Kerr–Newman metric describes the spacetime geometry around a mass that is electrically charged and rotating.

name: Tests of general relativity
fact: Tests of general relativity serve to establish observational evidence for the theory.

name: Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems
fact: The Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems attempt to answer when gravitation produces singularities.

name: Absolute space and time
fact: Absolute space and time is a concept in physics and philosophy about the properties of the universe.

name: Galilean invariance
fact: Galilean invariance states that the laws of motion are the same in all inertial frames of reference.

name: Collision
fact: A collision is any event in which two or more bodies exert forces on each other in a relatively short time.

name: Force field
fact: A force field is a vector field corresponding with a non-contact force acting on a particle at various positions in space.

name: Impact
fact: In mechanics, an impact is when two bodies collide.

name: Moment
fact: A moment is a mathematical expression involving the product of a distance and a physical quantity such as a force.

name: Newtonian dynamics
fact: Newtonian dynamics is the study of the dynamics of a particle or small body according to Newton's laws of motion.

name: Scalar potential
fact: A scalar potential is a function of position, and possibly time, used to describe a related vector field.

name: Equipotential
fact: An equipotential is a region in space where every point is at the same potential.

name: Vector potential
fact: A vector potential is a vector field whose curl is a given vector field.

name: Analytical mechanics
fact: Analytical mechanics is a collection of closely related formulations of classical mechanics.

name: Poisson bracket
fact: The Poisson bracket is an important binary operation in Hamiltonian mechanics, central to Hamilton's equations of motion.

name: D'Alembert's principle
fact: D'Alembert's principle is a statement of the fundamental classical laws of motion.

name: Euler–Lagrange equation
fact: The Euler–Lagrange equations are a system of differential equations whose solutions are stationary points of the given action functional.

name: Generalized coordinates
fact: Generalized coordinates are a set of parameters used to represent the configuration of a system in a configuration space.

name: Virtual work
fact: Virtual work arises in applying the principle of least action to the forces and movement of a mechanical system.

name: Screw axis
fact: A screw axis is a line that is simultaneously the axis of rotation and the line along which a body translates.

name: Constant of motion
fact: A constant of motion is a physical quantity conserved throughout the motion.

name: Equations for a falling body
fact: These equations describe the trajectories of objects subject to a constant gravitational force under normal Earth-bound conditions.

name: N-body problem
fact: The n-body problem is the problem of predicting the motions of a group of celestial objects interacting gravitationally.

name: Angular displacement
fact: The angular displacement is the angle through which a body or figure has rotated about a specified axis.

name: Metacentric height
fact: The metacentric height is a measurement of the initial static stability of a floating body.

name: Kelvin's circulation theorem
fact: Kelvin's circulation theorem says that the circulation around a closed curve moving with an ideal fluid stays constant with time.

name: Hagen–Poiseuille equation
fact: The Hagen–Poiseuille equation gives the pressure drop in a fluid in laminar flow through a long cylindrical pipe.

name: Rayleigh problem
fact: The Rayleigh problem is determining the flow created by a sudden movement of an infinitely long plate from rest.

name: Slosh dynamics
fact: Slosh refers to the movement of liquid inside another object that is typically also undergoing motion.

name: Free surface effect
fact: The free surface effect is a mechanism which can cause a watercraft to become unstable and capsize.

name: Contact mechanics
fact: Contact mechanics is the study of the deformation of solids that touch each other at one or more points.

name: Crystallite
fact: A crystallite is a small or even microscopic crystal which forms, for example, during the cooling of many materials.

name: Rigid body dynamics
fact: Rigid body dynamics studies the movement of systems of interconnected bodies under the action of external forces.

name: Cauchy stress tensor
fact: The Cauchy stress tensor completely defines the state of stress at a point inside a material.

name: Granular convection
fact: In granular convection, shaken granular material shows circulation patterns similar to fluid convection.

name: Virial theorem
fact: The virial theorem relates the time-averaged total kinetic energy of a stable bound system of particles to its total potential energy.

name: Degrees of freedom
fact: The degrees of freedom of a mechanical system is the number of independent parameters required to specify its configuration.

name: Point particle
fact: A point particle is an idealization used in physics with negligible spatial extension.

name: Test particle
fact: A test particle is an idealized object whose properties are assumed negligible except for the one being studied.

name: CIE 1931 color space
fact: The International Commission on Illumination color spaces define the relationship between the visible spectrum and human colour vision.

name: Color space
fact: A color space is a specific organization of colors.

name: HSL and HSV
fact: HSL and HSV are the two most common cylindrical-coordinate representations of points in an RGB color model.

name: Munsell color system
fact: The Munsell color system specifies colors by three properties: hue, value and chroma.

name: RGB color spaces
fact: RGB color spaces are a category of additive colorimetric color spaces defined using the RGB color model.

name: RGBA color model
fact: RGBA stands for red green blue alpha.

name: RYB color model
fact: RYB is a subtractive color model in which red, yellow and blue pigments are considered primary colors.

name: Impossible color
fact: Impossible colors are colors that do not appear in ordinary visual functioning.

name: Chromaticity
fact: Chromaticity is an objective specification of the quality of a color regardless of its luminance.

name: Line of purples
fact: The line of purples is the locus on the edge of the chromaticity diagram between extreme spectral red and violet.

name: Tint, shade and tone
fact: A tint is a color mixed with white, while a shade is a mixture with black.

name: Web colors
fact: Web colors, also known as hex codes, are colors used in displaying web pages.

name: Blacklight
fact: A blacklight is a lamp that emits long-wave ultraviolet light and very little visible light.

name: Physical quantity
fact: A physical quantity is a property of a material or system that can be quantified by measurement.

name: Energy density
fact: Energy density is the amount of energy stored in a given system or region of space divided by its volume.

name: Homogeneity
fact: A homogeneous material or system has the same properties at every point.

name: Physical object
fact: A physical object is a collection of matter, usually contiguous, with a defined boundary, that exists in space and time.

name: Scalar
fact: Scalars are physical quantities that can be described by a single pure number, accompanied by a unit of measurement.

name: Classical field theory
fact: A classical field theory predicts how fields interact with matter through field equations, without considering quantization.

name: Mean-field theory
fact: Mean-field theory studies a complicated model by studying a simpler one that approximates it by averaging.

name: Renormalization
fact: Renormalization is a collection of techniques used to treat infinities arising in calculated quantities.

name: Naive physics
fact: Naive physics, or folk physics, is the untrained human perception of basic physical phenomena.

name: Scale invariance
fact: Scale invariance is a feature of objects or laws that do not change when scales of length or energy are multiplied by a common factor.

name: Classical limit
fact: The classical limit is the ability of a physical theory to approximate classical mechanics for special values of its parameters.

name: Macroscopic scale
fact: The macroscopic scale is the length scale on which things are large enough to be seen with the naked eye.

name: Time in physics
fact: In physics, time is defined by its measurement: time is what a clock reads.

name: Bohr magneton
fact: The Bohr magneton is a physical constant and the natural unit for the magnetic moment of an electron.

name: Electron magnetic moment
fact: The electron magnetic moment is the magnetic moment of an electron resulting from its spin and electric charge.

name: Nucleon magnetic moment
fact: The nucleon magnetic moments are the intrinsic magnetic dipole moments of the proton and neutron.

name: Foucault's light-speed measurements
