fact: Leon Foucault used a rotating mirror to compare the speed of light in water with its speed in air.

name: Onium
fact: An onium is a bound state of a particle and its antiparticle.

name: Rydberg formula
fact: The Rydberg formula calculates the wavelengths of a spectral line in many chemical elements.

name: Molecular dynamics
fact: Molecular dynamics is a computer simulation method for analyzing the physical movements of atoms and molecules.

name: Rotational–vibrational spectroscopy
fact: Rotational–vibrational spectroscopy is a branch of molecular spectroscopy concerned with the infrared and Raman spectra of gas molecules.

name: CIELAB color space
fact: The CIELAB color space was defined by the International Commission on Illumination in nineteen seventy-six.

name: CIELUV
fact: CIELUV is a color space adopted by the International Commission on Illumination as a simple transformation of the earlier CIE XYZ color space.

name: HCL color space
fact: HCL refers to any of many cylindrical color space models designed to accord with human perception of color.

name: ISCC–NBS color system
fact: The ISCC–NBS system is a system for naming colors based on a set of basic color terms and a few adjective modifiers.

name: Adobe RGB
fact: The Adobe RGB color space was developed by Adobe in nineteen ninety-eight to encompass most of the colors achievable on printers.

name: sRGB
fact: sRGB, or standard RGB, is a color space for use on monitors, printers, and the World Wide Web.

name: Bonding in solids
fact: Solids can be classified according to the nature of the bonding between their atomic or molecular components.

name: Rock magnetism
fact: Rock magnetism is the study of the magnetic properties of rocks, sediments and soils.

name: Reciprocal lattice
fact: The reciprocal lattice is a concept associated with solids with translational symmetry, important in diffraction and in the energies of electrons in a solid.

name: Misorientation
fact: Misorientation is the difference in crystallographic orientation between two crystallites in a polycrystalline material.

name: Crystal engineering
fact: Crystal engineering studies the design and synthesis of solid-state structures with desired properties.

name: Vlasov equation
fact: The Vlasov equation describes the time evolution of the distribution function of a collisionless plasma of charged particles.

name: Plasma recombination
fact: Plasma recombination is a process by which positive ions of a plasma capture a free electron to form new neutral atoms.

name: Self-organized criticality
fact: Self-organized criticality is a property of dynamical systems that have a critical point as an attractor.

name: Metallization pressure
fact: Metallization pressure is the pressure required for a non-metallic chemical element to become a metal.

name: Negative-index metamaterial
fact: A negative-index metamaterial is a metamaterial whose refractive index for an electromagnetic wave is negative over some frequency range.

name: Nonlinear metamaterial
fact: A nonlinear metamaterial is an artificially constructed material that can exhibit properties not yet found in nature.

name: Photonic metamaterial
fact: A photonic metamaterial, also known as an optical metamaterial, is a type of electromagnetic metamaterial that interacts with light.

name: Spontaneous magnetization
fact: Spontaneous magnetization is the appearance of an ordered spin state at zero applied magnetic field below the Curie temperature.

name: Displacement current density
fact: Displacement current density is the rate of change of the electric displacement field, appearing in Maxwell's equations.

name: Electromagnetic four-potential
fact: An electromagnetic four-potential is a relativistic vector function from which the electromagnetic field can be derived.

name: Lorenz gauge condition
fact: The Lorenz gauge condition is a partial gauge fixing of the electromagnetic vector potential.

name: Ampere's circuital law
fact: Ampere's circuital law relates the circulation of a magnetic field around a closed loop to the electric current passing through that loop.

name: Metal–semiconductor junction
fact: A metal–semiconductor junction is an electrical junction in which a metal comes in close contact with a semiconductor material.

name: Displacement
fact: A displacement is a vector whose length is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of a point undergoing motion.

name: Free particle
fact: A free particle is a particle that is not bound by an external force, or not in a region where its potential energy varies.

name: Quantum
fact: A quantum is the minimum amount of any physical entity involved in an interaction.

name: AdS/CFT correspondence
fact: The anti-de Sitter and conformal field theory correspondence is a conjectured relationship between two kinds of physical theories.

name: Bra–ket notation
fact: Bra–ket notation, or Dirac notation, is a mathematical notation for linear algebra and linear operators on complex vector spaces.

name: Ehrenfest theorem
fact: The Ehrenfest theorem relates the time derivative of the expectation values of position and momentum to the expectation value of the force on a particle.

name: g-factor
fact: A g-factor is a dimensionless quantity that characterizes the magnetic moment and angular momentum of an atom, a particle, or a nucleus.

name: Interpretations of quantum mechanics
fact: An interpretation of quantum mechanics is an attempt to explain how its mathematical theory might correspond to experienced reality.

name: Mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics
fact: The mathematical formulations of quantum mechanics are the formalisms that permit a rigorous description of quantum mechanics.

name: BKS theory
fact: The Bohr–Kramers–Slater theory was perhaps the final attempt to understand the interaction of matter and radiation on the basis of the old quantum theory.

name: Measurement in quantum mechanics
fact: In quantum physics, a measurement is the testing or manipulation of a physical system to yield a numerical result.

name: Observable
fact: In physics, an observable is a physical property or quantity that can be measured.

name: Invariant
fact: An invariant is an observable of a physical system which remains unchanged under some transformation.

name: Quantum contextuality
fact: Quantum contextuality is a feature of quantum mechanics whereby measurements cannot simply be thought of as revealing pre-existing values.

name: Angular momentum operator
fact: The angular momentum operator is one of several related operators analogous to classical angular momentum.

name: Hamiltonian
fact: The Hamiltonian of a system is an operator corresponding to the total energy of that system, kinetic and potential.

name: Momentum operator
fact: The momentum operator is the operator associated with the linear momentum.

name: Planck postulate
fact: The Planck postulate says that the energy of oscillators in a black body is quantized.

name: Position and momentum spaces
fact: Position space and momentum space are two closely related vector spaces, usually three-dimensional but in general of any finite dimension.

name: Problem of time
fact: The problem of time is a conceptual conflict between quantum mechanics and general relativity.

name: Wheeler–Feynman absorber theory
fact: The Wheeler–Feynman absorber theory is a theory of electrodynamics based on a relativistically correct extension of action at a distance.

name: Conformal field theory
fact: A conformal field theory is a quantum field theory that is invariant under conformal transformations.

name: QCD vacuum
fact: The QCD vacuum is the quantum vacuum state of quantum chromodynamics.

name: QED vacuum
fact: The QED vacuum is the field-theoretic vacuum of quantum electrodynamics.

name: Quantum foam
fact: Quantum foam is a theoretical quantum fluctuation of spacetime on very small scales due to quantum mechanics.

name: Relativistic quantum mechanics
fact: Relativistic quantum mechanics is any Poincare-covariant formulation of quantum mechanics.

name: Symmetry in quantum mechanics
fact: Symmetries in quantum mechanics describe features of spacetime and particles which are unchanged under some transformation.

name: Compton wavelength
fact: The Compton wavelength of a massive particle is the wavelength of a photon whose energy is the same as the rest energy of that particle.

name: Energy–momentum relation
fact: The energy–momentum relation is the relativistic equation relating total energy to mass and momentum.

name: Moving magnet and conductor problem
fact: The moving magnet and conductor problem is a famous thought experiment on the intersection of classical electromagnetism and special relativity.

name: Principle of covariance
fact: The principle of covariance emphasizes formulating physical laws using only quantities that observers in different frames of reference can correlate.

name: Lorentz covariance
fact: Lorentz symmetry is an equivalence of observation due to special relativity, implying that the laws of physics stay the same for all observers.

name: Mathematics of general relativity
fact: Studying and formulating Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity uses various mathematical structures and techniques.

name: Reaction
fact: By Newton's third law, if one object exerts a force on another, the second exerts an equal and opposite reaction force on the first.

name: Chasles' theorem
fact: Chasles' theorem says that the most general rigid body displacement can be produced by a screw motion.

name: Locomotion in space
fact: Locomotion in space includes all methods used to move one's body in microgravity through outer space.

name: Position
fact: A position vector is a Euclidean vector that represents a point in space.

name: Kepler problem
fact: The Kepler problem is a special case of the two-body problem, in which two bodies interact by a central force that varies as the inverse square of their distance.

name: Diffusion equation
fact: The diffusion equation is a parabolic partial differential equation.

name: Euler equations
fact: The Euler equations are a set of partial differential equations governing adiabatic and inviscid flow.

name: Volumetric flow rate
fact: The volumetric flow rate is the volume of fluid which passes per unit time.

name: Vertical pressure variation
fact: Vertical pressure variation is the variation in pressure as a function of elevation.

name: Young's modulus
fact: Young's modulus is a mechanical property of solid materials that measures their stiffness when force is applied lengthwise.

name: Boltzmann distribution
fact: A Boltzmann distribution gives the probability that a system will be in a certain state as a function of that state's energy and the temperature of the system.

name: Distribution function
fact: A system's distribution function gives the number of particles per unit volume in single-particle phase space.

name: Entropy as an arrow of time
fact: Entropy is one of the few quantities in physics that requires a particular direction for time, sometimes called an arrow of time.

name: Maxwell–Boltzmann statistics
fact: Maxwell–Boltzmann statistics describes the distribution of classical particles over various energy states in thermal equilibrium.

name: High-energy nuclear physics
fact: High-energy nuclear physics studies the behavior of nuclear matter in energy regimes typical of high-energy physics.

name: Yang–Mills mass gap
fact: The Yang–Mills existence and mass gap problem is an unsolved problem and one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems.

name: Mathematical formulation of the Standard Model
fact: The Standard Model of particle physics is a gauge quantum field theory containing the internal symmetries of a unitary product group.

name: Hierarchy problem
fact: The hierarchy problem is the large discrepancy between aspects of the weak force and gravity.

name: QCD matter
fact: QCD matter refers to hypothetical phases of matter built from quarks and gluons, of which the prominent example is quark-gluon plasma.

name: Scalar field theory
fact: Scalar field theory can refer to a relativistically invariant classical or quantum theory of scalar fields.

name: Spin one-half
fact: In quantum mechanics, spin is an intrinsic property of all elementary particles; all known fermions have a spin of one half.

name: Flavour
fact: In particle physics, flavour refers to the species of an elementary particle.

name: Collider
fact: A collider is a type of particle accelerator that brings two opposing particle beams together so that the particles collide.

name: Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider
fact: The Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider is the first and one of only two operating heavy-ion colliders.

name: Cowan–Reines neutrino experiment
fact: The Cowan–Reines neutrino experiment, in nineteen fifty-six, confirmed the existence of neutrinos.

name: Eightfold way
fact: The eightfold way is an organizational scheme for hadrons that led to the development of the quark model.

name: Parton
fact: The parton model is a model of hadrons, such as protons and neutrons, proposed by Richard Feynman.

name: J/psi meson
fact: The J/psi meson is a flavor-neutral meson consisting of a charm quark and a charm antiquark.

name: Biophoton
fact: Biophotons are photons of light in the ultraviolet and visible range that are produced by a biological system.

name: Antineutron
fact: The antineutron is the antiparticle of the neutron.

name: Neutral particle oscillation
fact: Neutral particle oscillation is the transmutation of a particle with zero electric charge into another neutral particle.

name: Brane
fact: A brane is a physical object that generalizes the notion of a point particle, a string, or a membrane to higher-dimensional objects.

name: Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model
fact: The Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model is an extension to the Standard Model that realizes supersymmetry.

name: Classical unified field theories
fact: Since the nineteenth century, some physicists, notably Albert Einstein, have tried to develop a single framework that accounts for all the fundamental forces of nature.

name: Internal pressure
fact: Internal pressure is a measure of how the internal energy of a system changes when it expands or contracts at constant temperature.

name: Particle number
fact: The particle number of a thermodynamic system is the number of constituent particles in that system.

name: Fundamental thermodynamic relation
fact: The fundamental thermodynamic relation is a set of equations showing how important thermodynamic quantities depend on variables that can be measured experimentally.

name: Specific heat capacity
fact: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the heat that must be added to one unit of its mass to raise its temperature by one unit.

name: Van der Waals equation
fact: The van der Waals equation is an equation of state that relates the pressure, molar volume, and temperature in fluids.

name: Virial expansion
fact: The virial expansion is a model of thermodynamic equations of state.

name: Thermodynamic equilibrium
fact: Thermodynamic equilibrium is a notion of thermodynamics referring to an internal state of a single system, or a relation between several connected systems.

name: Equilibrium thermodynamics
fact: Equilibrium thermodynamics is the systematic study of transformations of matter and energy in terms of thermodynamic equilibrium.

name: Helmholtz free energy
fact: The Helmholtz free energy measures the useful work obtainable from a closed thermodynamic system at a constant temperature.

name: Thermodynamic process
fact: A thermodynamic process is a process in which the thermodynamic state of a system is changed.

name: Intensive and extensive properties
fact: Properties of materials and systems can often be categorized as intensive or extensive, according to how they change when the size of the system changes.

name: Thermodynamic equations
fact: Thermodynamics is expressed by a mathematical framework of equations relating thermodynamic quantities and physical properties measured in a laboratory.

name: Radio frequency
fact: Radio frequency is the oscillation rate of an alternating current or voltage or of an electromagnetic field, in the range from about nine kilohertz to three hundred gigahertz.

name: Wavefront
fact: The wavefront of a wave field is the set of all points having the same phase.

name: Phase velocity
fact: The phase velocity of a wave is the speed of any wavefront, a surface of constant phase.

name: Wave packet
fact: A wave packet is a short burst of localized wave action that travels as a unit, outlined by an envelope.

name: Plane wave
fact: A plane wave is a wave whose value, at any given moment, is constant through any plane perpendicular to a fixed direction in space.

name: Darkness
fact: Darkness is the condition resulting from a lack of illumination, or an absence of visible light.

name: Geometrical optics
fact: Geometrical optics, or ray optics, is a model of optics that describes light propagation in terms of rays.

name: Optical path length
fact: Optical path length is the vacuum length that light travels in the same time it takes to travel through a given length of medium.

name: Physical optics
fact: Physical optics, or wave optics, is the branch of optics that studies interference, diffraction, polarization and other phenomena the ray approximation cannot explain.

name: Linear polarization
fact: Linear polarization is a confinement of the electric or magnetic field vector of radiation to a given plane along the direction of propagation.

name: Transmission coefficient
fact: The transmission coefficient is used when wave propagation in a medium containing discontinuities is considered.

name: Nonlinear optics
fact: Nonlinear optics studies the case when optical properties of matter depend on the intensity of the input light.

name: Dichroism
fact: A dichroic material causes visible light to be split into two distinct beams of different wavelengths.

name: Intensity
fact: Intensity is the power transferred per unit area, measured on the plane perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the energy.

name: Newton's rings
fact: Newton's rings is a phenomenon in which an interference pattern is created by the reflection of light between a spherical surface and a touching flat surface.

name: Rayleigh scattering
fact: Rayleigh scattering is the scattering of light, or other electromagnetic radiation, by particles much smaller than the wavelength of the radiation.

name: Angle of incidence
fact: The angle of incidence is the angle between a ray falling on a surface and the line perpendicular to the surface at that point.

name: Shadow
fact: A shadow is a dark area on a surface where light from a light source is blocked by an object.

name: Beer–Lambert law
fact: The Beer–Lambert law is used to determine the concentration of substances in a solution.

name: Invisibility
fact: Invisibility is the state of an object that cannot be seen.

name: Brightness
fact: Brightness is an attribute of visual perception in which a source appears to be radiating or reflecting light.

name: Colorfulness
fact: Colorfulness, chroma and saturation are attributes of perceived color relating to chromatic intensity.

name: Academic discipline
fact: An academic discipline is a subdivision of knowledge that is taught and researched at the college or university level.

name: Interdisciplinarity
fact: Interdisciplinarity is the combination of multiple academic disciplines into one activity.

name: Analysis
fact: Analysis is the process of breaking a complex topic or substance into smaller parts in order to understand it better.

name: Branches of science
fact: The branches of science are commonly divided into three major groups: the formal, natural and social sciences.

name: Formal science
fact: Formal science is a branch of science studying disciplines concerned with abstract structures described by formal systems.

name: Data science
fact: Data science is an interdisciplinary academic field that uses statistics, computing and algorithms to extract knowledge from data.

name: Classification
fact: Classification is the activity of assigning objects to pre-existing classes or categories.

name: Data analysis
fact: Data analysis is the process of inspecting, cleansing, transforming and modeling data to discover useful information and support decisions.

name: Data sharing
fact: Data sharing is the dissemination of research datasets to enable access and use by other investigators.

name: Error
fact: An error is an inaccurate or incorrect action, thought, or judgement.

name: Blinded experiment
fact: In a blinded experiment, information that could influence participants or investigators is withheld until the experiment is completed.

name: Forecasting
fact: Forecasting is the process of making predictions based on past and present data.

name: Fringe science
fact: Fringe science refers to ideas that are highly speculative or rely on premises already refuted.

name: Funding of science
fact: Research funding generally encompasses any funding for scientific research in the natural sciences, technology and the social sciences.

name: Learned society
fact: A learned society is an organization that exists to promote an academic discipline, profession, or a group of related disciplines.

name: Metascience
fact: Metascience, also known as the science of science, is the systematic study of science itself.

name: Open science
fact: Open science is the movement to make scientific research, data and models transparent and accessible to all levels of society.

name: Peer review
fact: Peer review is the evaluation of work by one or more people with similar competencies as the producers of the work.

name: Scholarly peer review
fact: Scholarly peer review is the process of having a researcher's methods and findings reviewed, usually anonymously, by experts in the same field.

name: Polymath
fact: A polymath is an individual whose knowledge spans many different subjects, known to draw on complex bodies of knowledge to solve specific problems.

name: Protoscience
fact: Protoscience is a research field with the characteristics of an undeveloped science that may ultimately develop into an established science.

name: Reproducibility
fact: Reproducibility, closely related to replicability and repeatability, is a major principle underpinning the scientific method.

name: Replication crisis
fact: The replication crisis is a widespread phenomenon in which published scientific results cannot be reproduced.

name: Basic research
fact: Basic research is a type of scientific research with the aim of improving scientific theories for better understanding and prediction of phenomena.

name: Scientific community
fact: The scientific community is a diverse network of interacting scientists.

name: Scientific evidence
fact: Scientific evidence is evidence that serves to either support or counter a scientific theory or hypothesis.

name: Scientific misconduct
fact: Scientific misconduct is the violation of ethical and professional standards in research, including fabrication, falsification and plagiarism.

name: Computational science
fact: Computational science, also known as scientific computing, uses advanced computing capabilities to understand and solve complex physical problems.

name: Self-replication
fact: Self-replication is any behavior of a dynamical system that yields construction of an identical or similar copy of itself.

name: Complex system
fact: A complex system is a system composed of many components that interact with one another.

name: Animal testing
fact: Animal testing is the use of non-human animals, as model organisms, in experiments that seek answers to scientific and medical questions.

name: Clinical trial
fact: Clinical trials are research studies on human participants designed to answer specific questions about biomedical or behavioral interventions.

name: Case study
fact: A case study is an in-depth, detailed examination of a particular case within a real-world context.

name: Medical laboratory
fact: A medical laboratory is a laboratory where tests are conducted on clinical specimens to obtain information about the health of a patient.

name: Dry measure
fact: Dry measures are units of volume to measure bulk commodities that are not fluids.

name: Buckingham pi theorem
fact: The Buckingham pi theorem is a key theorem in dimensional analysis.

name: System of units of measurement
fact: A system of units of measurement is a collection of units of measurement and rules relating them to each other.

name: Approximate measures
fact: Approximate measures are units of measurement not defined by any government, yet which remain in use.

name: Astronomical system of units
fact: The astronomical system of units is a system of measurement developed for use in astronomy.

name: Biblical and Talmudic units of measurement
fact: Biblical and Talmudic units of measurement were used primarily by ancient Israelites and appear frequently within the Hebrew Bible.

name: Chinese units of measurement
fact: Chinese units of measurement are the traditional units of measurement of the Han Chinese.

name: Cooking weights and measures
fact: In recipes, quantities of ingredients may be specified by mass, by volume, or by count.

name: Japanese units of measurement
fact: The traditional Japanese units of measurement are the traditional system of measurement used by the people of the Japanese archipelago.

name: Korean units of measurement
fact: The Korean units of measurement are the traditional system of measurement used by the people of the Korean Peninsula.

name: Atomic units
fact: The atomic units are a system of natural units of measurement especially convenient for calculations in atomic physics.

name: Geometrized unit system
fact: A geometrized unit system is a system of natural units in which the speed of light and the gravitational constant are the defining constants.

name: Heaviside–Lorentz units
fact: Heaviside–Lorentz units are a system of units that defines electromagnetic quantities, named for Oliver Heaviside and Hendrik Antoon Lorentz.

name: Typographic unit
fact: Typographic units are the units of measurement used in typography or typesetting.

name: Unit of account
fact: A unit of account is a standard unit of measurement of the market value of goods, services and other transactions.

name: Winchester measure
fact: Winchester measure is a set of legal standards of volume instituted by King Henry the Seventh of England.

name: Imperial and US customary measurement systems
fact: The imperial and United States customary measurement systems are both derived from an earlier English system of measurement.

name: Imperial versus US customary units
fact: The British imperial and United States customary systems of measurement both derive from earlier English unit systems.

name: Foot–pound–second system
fact: The foot–pound–second system is built on three fundamental units: the foot for length, the pound for mass or force, and the second for time.

name: Caesium standard
fact: The caesium standard is a primary frequency standard in which transitions between two hyperfine ground states of caesium atoms control the output frequency.

name: International System of Quantities
fact: The International System of Quantities is a standard system of quantities used in physics and in modern science in general.

name: MKS units
fact: The metre, kilogram, second system is a physical system of measurement based on the metre, kilogram and second as base units.

name: Centimetre–gram–second system
fact: The centimetre–gram–second system is a variant of the metric system based on the centimetre, the gram and the second.

name: Minute and second of arc
fact: A minute of arc is a unit of angular measurement equal to one sixtieth of a degree.

name: Milliradian
fact: A milliradian is a unit for angular measurement defined as a thousandth of a radian.

name: Kilometre
fact: The kilometre is a unit of length equal to one thousand metres.

name: Angstrom
fact: The angstrom is a unit of length equal to one ten-billionth of a metre.

name: Palm
fact: The palm is an obsolete unit of length, originally based on the width of the human palm.

name: Chi
fact: The chi is a traditional Chinese unit of length, often translated as the Chinese foot.

name: Cun
fact: A cun, often translated as the Chinese inch, is a traditional Chinese unit of length.

name: Ken
fact: The ken is a traditional Japanese unit of length, equal to six shaku.

name: Li
fact: The li is a traditional Chinese unit of distance, usually about one third of an English mile.

name: Shaku
fact: The shaku, or Japanese foot, is a Japanese unit of length derived from the Chinese chi.

name: Biblical mile
fact: The biblical mile is a unit of distance principally used by Jews during the Herodian dynasty to ascertain distances between cities and to mark the Sabbath limit.

name: Pace
fact: A pace is a unit of length consisting either of one normal walking step, or of a double step.

name: Stadion
fact: The stadion was an ancient Greek unit of length consisting of six hundred ancient Greek feet.

name: X unit
fact: The x unit is a unit of length used to quote the wavelength of X-rays and gamma rays.

name: Square kilometre
fact: The square kilometre is a multiple of the square metre, the International System unit of area.

name: Square mile
fact: The square mile is an imperial and United States unit of measure for area.

name: Pyeong
fact: A pyeong is a Korean unit of area and floorspace.

name: Acre-foot
fact: The acre-foot is a unit of volume commonly used in the western United States for large-scale water resources such as reservoirs and irrigation.

name: Ge
fact: The ge is a traditional Chinese unit of volume equal to a tenth of a sheng.

name: Koku
fact: The koku is a Chinese-based Japanese unit of volume, about the amount of rice one person eats in a year.

name: Cubic metre per second
fact: The cubic metre per second is the unit of volumetric flow rate in the International System of Units.

name: Erg
fact: The erg is a unit of energy originating from the older centimetre–gram–second system of units.

name: Millimetre of mercury
fact: A millimetre of mercury is a unit of pressure, formerly defined as the extra pressure generated by a column of mercury one millimetre high.

name: Newton-second
fact: The newton-second is the unit of impulse in the International System of Units.

name: Poise
fact: The poise is the unit of dynamic viscosity in the centimetre–gram–second system, named after Jean Léonard Marie Poiseuille.

name: Solar mass
fact: The solar mass is a frequently used unit of mass in astronomy, approximately equal to the mass of the Sun.

name: Jupiter mass
fact: The Jupiter mass is the unit of mass equal to the total mass of the planet Jupiter.

name: Earth mass
fact: An Earth mass is a unit of mass equal to the mass of the planet Earth.

name: Tonne
fact: The tonne is a unit of mass equal to one thousand kilograms.

name: Gram
fact: The gram is a unit of mass equal to one thousandth of a kilogram.

name: Carat
fact: The carat is a unit of mass used for measuring gemstones and pearls.

name: Ton
fact: A ton is any of several units of measure of mass, volume or force.

name: Long ton
fact: The long ton, also known as the imperial ton, is the unit called the ton in the avoirdupois system of weights.

name: Short ton
fact: The short ton, also known as the United States ton, is a measurement unit equal to two thousand pounds.

name: Bushel
fact: A bushel is an imperial and United States customary unit of volume, based upon an earlier measure of dry capacity.

name: Ounce
fact: The ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight or volume, derived almost unchanged from the Roman uncia.

name: Hundredweight
fact: The hundredweight is a British imperial and United States customary unit of weight or mass.

name: Pennyweight
fact: A pennyweight is a unit of mass equal to twenty-four grains, one twentieth of a troy ounce.

name: Electron mass
fact: The electron mass is the mass of a stationary electron, one of the fundamental constants of physics.

name: Jin
fact: The jin, or catty, is a traditional Chinese unit of mass used across East and Southeast Asia for weighing food.

name: Picul
fact: The picul is a traditional Asian unit of weight, defined as as much as a man can carry on a shoulder-pole.

name: Kilometres per hour
fact: The kilometre per hour is a unit of speed, expressing the number of kilometres travelled in one hour.

name: Metre per second
fact: The metre per second is the unit of both speed and velocity in the International System of Units.

name: Miles per hour
fact: Miles per hour is a unit of speed expressing the number of miles travelled in one hour.

name: Metre per second squared
fact: The metre per second squared is the unit of acceleration in the International System of Units.

name: Standard gravity
fact: Standard gravity is the nominal gravitational acceleration of an object in a vacuum near the surface of the Earth.

name: Inverse second
fact: The inverse second is a unit defined as the multiplicative inverse of the second.

name: Radian per second
fact: The radian per second is the unit of angular velocity in the International System of Units.

name: Revolutions per minute
fact: Revolutions per minute is a unit of rotational speed for rotating machines.

name: Joule-second
fact: The joule-second is the unit of action and of angular momentum in the International System of Units.

name: Mole fraction
fact: The mole fraction is the ratio between the amount of a constituent substance and the total amount of all constituents in a mixture.

name: Mass fraction
fact: The mass fraction of a substance within a mixture is the ratio of its mass to the total mass of the mixture.

name: Neper
fact: The neper is a logarithmic unit for ratios of measurements of field and power quantities, such as gain and loss of electronic signals.

name: Relative density
fact: Relative density, also called specific gravity, is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of a reference material.

name: Volume fraction
fact: The volume fraction is the volume of a constituent divided by the volume of all constituents of the mixture before mixing.

name: Gram per cubic centimetre
fact: The gram per cubic centimetre is a unit of density, commonly used in chemistry.

name: Kilogram per cubic metre
fact: The kilogram per cubic metre is the unit of density in the International System of Units.

name: Molar concentration
fact: Molar concentration is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution.

name: Molality
fact: Molality is a measure of the amount of solute in a solution relative to a given mass of solvent.

name: Parts-per notation
fact: Parts-per notation is a set of pseudo-units to describe small values of dimensionless quantities.

name: Shake
fact: A shake is a metric unit of time equal to ten nanoseconds, coined for nuclear physics.

name: Epoch
fact: An epoch is an instant in time chosen as the origin of a particular calendar era.

name: Aeon
fact: The word aeon originally meant life, vital force, generation or a period of time.

name: Eternity
fact: Eternity is time with no end, that is, infinite.

name: Jansky
fact: The jansky is a unit of spectral flux density used especially in radio astronomy.

name: Ampere-hour
fact: An ampere-hour is a unit of electric charge, recommended for specifying the capacity of batteries.

name: Gauss
fact: The gauss is a unit of measurement of magnetic flux density.

name: Henry
fact: The henry is the unit of electrical inductance in the International System of Units.

name: Rankine scale
fact: The Rankine scale is an absolute scale of thermodynamic temperature named after the engineer and physicist William Rankine.

name: Candlepower
fact: Candlepower is the unit of luminous intensity in the United States customary systems of measurement.

name: Lumen
fact: The lumen is the International System unit of luminous flux, which quantifies the perceived power of visible light emitted by a source.

name: Lux
fact: The lux is the unit of illuminance, or luminous flux per unit area.

name: Curie
fact: The curie is a unit of radioactivity, named in honour of Pierre Curie and perhaps also of Marie Skłodowska-Curie.

name: Roentgen
fact: The roentgen is a legacy unit of measurement for the exposure of X-rays and gamma rays.

name: Rad
fact: The rad is a unit of absorbed radiation dose.

name: Katal
fact: The katal is a unit used for quantifying the catalytic activity of enzymes and other catalysts.

name: Enzyme unit
fact: The enzyme unit is a unit measuring an enzyme's catalytic activity.

name: Baud
fact: Baud is a common unit of measurement of symbol rate, one of the components that determine the speed of communication over a data channel.

name: Nat
fact: The nat is a unit of information based on natural logarithms and powers of the number e.

name: Shannon
fact: The shannon is a unit of information named after Claude Shannon, the founder of information theory.

name: Qubit
fact: A qubit is a basic unit of quantum information, the quantum version of the classic binary bit.

name: Dots per inch
fact: Dots per inch is a measure of spatial printing, video or image scanner dot density.

name: Pixel density
fact: Pixel density is measured in pixels per inch or per centimetre on a screen or image scanner.

name: Alcohol by volume
fact: Alcohol by volume is a common measure of the amount of alcohol contained in a given alcoholic beverage.

name: Air quality index
fact: An air quality index is an approximation of how polluted the air currently is or how polluted it is forecast to become.

name: Ultraviolet index
fact: The ultraviolet index is an international standard measurement of the strength of the sunburn-producing ultraviolet radiation at a place and time.

name: Appropriate technology
fact: Appropriate technology is technological choice that is small-scale, affordable, labor-intensive, energy-efficient and locally autonomous.

name: Emerging technologies
fact: Emerging technologies are technologies whose development, practical applications, or both are still largely unrealized.

name: Maintenance
fact: Maintenance involves functional checks, servicing, repairing or replacing of necessary devices, equipment and machinery.

name: Heuristic
fact: A heuristic is an approach to problem solving that is not necessarily optimized or perfected, but is sufficient for reaching an immediate goal.

name: Research and development
fact: Research and development is the set of innovative activities undertaken in developing new services or products, or improving existing ones.

name: Scientific instrument
fact: A scientific instrument is a device or tool used for scientific purposes, including the study of natural phenomena and theoretical research.

name: Simulation
fact: A simulation is an imitative representation of a process or system that could exist in the real world.

name: Technological convergence
fact: Technological convergence is the tendency for originally unrelated technologies to become more closely integrated and even unified.

name: Technological determinism
fact: Technological determinism is the theory that a society's technology progresses by its own internal logic of efficiency, determining its social structure and cultural values.

name: Technology adoption life cycle
fact: The technology adoption lifecycle is a sociological model describing the adoption of a new product or innovation by defined groups of adopters.

name: Technology and society
fact: Technology and society refers to the inter-dependency and co-influence of technology and society upon one another.

name: Technology assessment
fact: Technology assessment is a practical process of determining the value of a new or emerging technology.

name: Technology life cycle
fact: The technology life cycle describes the commercial gain of a product through the expense of research and the financial return during its vital life.

name: Technology transfer
fact: Technology transfer is the process of transferring technology from the person or organization that owns it to another.

name: Molecular machine
fact: Molecular machines are molecules assembled from a discrete number of components to produce mechanical movements in response to specific stimuli.

name: Engineering ethics
fact: Engineering ethics is the field concerned with the system of moral principles that apply to the practice of engineering.

name: Risk management
fact: Risk management is the identification, evaluation and prioritization of risks, followed by minimizing, monitoring and controlling their impact.

name: Engineering management
fact: Engineering management is the application of engineering methods, tools and techniques to business management systems.

name: Requirements analysis
fact: Requirements analysis focuses on the tasks that determine the needs or conditions to meet a new or altered product or project.

name: Engineering economics
fact: Engineering economics is a subset of economics concerned with the application of economic principles to engineering decisions.

name: Applied mechanics
fact: Applied mechanics is the branch of science concerned with the motion of any substance that humans can perceive without instruments.

name: Biochemical engineering
fact: Biochemical engineering, also known as bioprocess engineering, has roots in chemical engineering and biological engineering.

name: Pharmaceutical engineering
fact: Pharmaceutical engineering is a branch of engineering focused on discovering, formulating and manufacturing medication.

name: Molecular engineering
fact: Molecular engineering is concerned with the design and testing of molecular properties in order to assemble better materials and systems.

name: Process engineering
fact: Process engineering is a field of study focused on the development and optimization of industrial processes.

name: Polymer engineering
fact: Polymer engineering is an engineering field that designs, analyses and modifies polymer materials.

name: Construction engineering
fact: Construction engineering is a sub-discipline of civil engineering that deals with the designing, planning, construction and operations management of infrastructure.

name: Directional drilling
fact: Directional drilling, or slant drilling, is the practice of drilling non-vertical bores.

name: Highway engineering
fact: Highway engineering is a discipline branching from the civil engineering subdiscipline of transportation engineering.

name: Computer engineering
fact: Computer engineering is a branch of engineering specialized in developing computer hardware and software.

name: Energy engineering
fact: Energy engineering is a multidisciplinary field that focuses on optimizing energy systems, developing renewable energy technologies and improving energy efficiency.

name: Power engineering
fact: Power engineering is a subfield of electrical engineering that deals with the generation, transmission, distribution and use of electric power.

name: Radio-frequency engineering
fact: Radio-frequency engineering applies transmission line, waveguide, antenna, radar and electromagnetic field principles to the design of devices.

name: Engineering physics
fact: Engineering physics is the field of study combining pure science disciplines with engineering disciplines.

name: Computer-aided engineering
fact: Computer-aided engineering is the general use of technology to aid in tasks related to engineering analysis.

name: Manufacturing engineering
fact: Manufacturing engineering is a branch of professional engineering that shares concepts with mechanical, chemical, electrical and industrial engineering.

name: Sanitary engineering
fact: Sanitary engineering is the application of engineering methods to improve sanitation of human communities.

name: Security engineering
fact: Security engineering is the process of incorporating security controls into an information system so that they become an integral part of its operation.

name: Structural analysis
fact: Structural analysis is a branch of solid mechanics which uses simplified models for solids like bars, beams and shells.

name: Energy development
fact: Energy development is the field of activities focused on obtaining sources of energy from natural resources.

name: Yakhchāl
fact: A yakhchal, whose name means ice pit, is an ancient type of ice house.

name: Jack-o'-lantern
fact: A jack-o'-lantern is a carved lantern, most commonly made from a pumpkin.

name: Prism lighting
fact: Prism lighting is the use of prisms to improve the distribution of light in a space.

name: Light tube
fact: Light tubes, also known as solar pipes or sun tunnels, are structures that transmit or distribute natural or artificial light.

name: Microgeneration
fact: Microgeneration is the small-scale production of heat or electric power from a low carbon source.

name: Micro combined heat and power
fact: Micro combined heat and power extends the idea of cogeneration to the single or multi family home or small office building.

name: Gas-fired power plant
fact: A gas-fired power plant is a thermal power station that burns natural gas to generate electricity.

name: Inertial confinement fusion
fact: Inertial confinement fusion initiates nuclear fusion reactions by compressing and heating targets filled with fuel.

name: Pressurized heavy-water reactor
fact: A pressurized heavy-water reactor is a nuclear reactor that uses heavy water as its coolant and neutron moderator.

name: Nuclear marine propulsion
fact: Nuclear marine propulsion is propulsion of a ship or submarine with heat provided by a nuclear reactor.

name: Home energy storage
fact: Home energy storage refers to residential devices that store electrical energy locally for later consumption.

name: Power-to-X
fact: Power-to-X refers to electricity conversion, energy storage and reconversion pathways from surplus renewable energy.

name: Availability factor
fact: The availability factor of a power plant is the time it produces electricity divided by the time it was planned to produce electricity.

name: Automatic generation control
fact: Automatic generation control adjusts the power output of multiple generators at different power plants in response to changes in the load.

name: Backfeeding
fact: Backfeeding is the flow of electric power in the direction reverse to the typical flow of power.

name: Droop speed control
fact: Droop speed control is a control mode for generators whereby the power output reduces as the line frequency increases.

name: Efficient energy use
fact: Efficient energy use is the process of reducing the amount of energy required to provide products and services.

name: Energy demand management
fact: Energy demand management is the modification of consumer demand for energy through methods such as education and incentives.

name: Energy return on investment
fact: Energy return on investment is the ratio of the usable energy delivered from a resource to the energy used to obtain it.

name: Grid code
fact: A grid code is a technical specification defining the parameters a facility connected to a public electric grid has to meet.

name: Load factor
fact: In electrical engineering the load factor is the average load divided by the peak load in a specified time period.

name: Nameplate capacity
fact: Nameplate capacity is the intended full-load sustained output of a facility such as a power station.

name: Electric power quality
fact: Electric power quality is the degree to which the voltage, frequency and waveform of a power supply conform to established specifications.

name: Power-flow study
fact: A power-flow study is a numerical analysis of the flow of electric power in an interconnected system.

name: Repowering
fact: Repowering is the process of replacing older power stations with newer ones of greater capacity or efficiency.

name: Variable renewable energy
fact: Variable renewable energy sources are not dispatchable on demand because of their fluctuating nature, such as wind power and solar power.

name: Dynamic demand
fact: Dynamic demand is a semi-passive technology to support demand response by adjusting the load demand on an electrical power grid.

name: Load management
fact: Load management is the process of balancing the supply of electricity on the network with the electrical load by controlling the load.

name: Transmission system operator
fact: A transmission system operator is an entity entrusted with transporting natural gas or electrical power on a national or regional level.

name: Overhead cable
fact: An overhead cable is a cable for the transmission of information, laid on utility poles.

name: Wide area synchronous grid
fact: A wide area synchronous grid is a three-phase electric power grid of regional scale or greater operating at a synchronized frequency.

name: Arc-fault circuit interrupter
fact: An arc-fault circuit interrupter is a circuit breaker that breaks the circuit when it detects electric arcs.

name: Earth-leakage circuit breaker
fact: An earth-leakage circuit breaker is a safety device used in electrical installations to prevent shock.

name: Power system protection
fact: Power system protection is a set of techniques and equipment used to limit the damage caused by an electrical fault.

name: Numerical relay
fact: A numerical relay is a computer-based system with software-based protection algorithms for the detection of electrical faults.

name: Sulfur hexafluoride circuit breaker
fact: Sulfur hexafluoride circuit breakers protect power stations and distribution systems by interrupting electric currents.

name: Continental Europe synchronous area
fact: The Continental Europe Synchronous Area is the second largest synchronous electrical grid in the world.

name: Conveyor system
fact: A conveyor system is a common piece of mechanical handling equipment that moves materials from one location to another.

name: Pelletizing
fact: Pelletizing is the process of compressing or molding a material into the shape of a pellet.

name: Disposable product
fact: A disposable product is designed for a single use after which it is recycled or disposed of as solid waste.

name: Food coloring
fact: Food coloring is any dye, pigment or substance that imparts color when it is added to food or beverages.

name: Sugar substitute
fact: A sugar substitute is a food additive that provides a sweetness like that of sugar with significantly less food energy.

name: Sewage
fact: Sewage is a type of wastewater that is produced by a community of people.

name: Extractive metallurgy
fact: Extractive metallurgy studies the process and methods of extraction of metals from their natural mineral deposits.

name: Gold dredge
fact: A gold dredge is a placer mining machine that extracts gold from sand, gravel and dirt using water and mechanical methods.

name: Mineral processing
fact: Mineral processing is the process of separating commercially valuable minerals from their ores.

name: Mechanical screening
fact: Mechanical screening is the practice of taking crushed material and separating it into grades by particle size.

name: Spiral separator
fact: A spiral separator is a device for sorting particles by density or by shape.

name: Stamp mill
fact: A stamp mill is a type of mill that crushes material by pounding rather than grinding.

name: Trommel screen
fact: A trommel screen, also known as a rotary screen, is a mechanical screening machine used to separate materials.

name: Bending
fact: Bending is a manufacturing process that produces a bent shape along a straight axis in ductile materials, most commonly sheet metal.

name: Electrical discharge machining
fact: Electrical discharge machining is a metal cutting process whereby a desired shape is obtained by using electrical sparks.

name: Machining
fact: Machining is a manufacturing process where a desired shape is created by the controlled removal of material by cutting.

name: Metal fabrication
fact: Metal fabrication is the creation of metal structures by cutting, bending and assembling processes.

name: Chino cloth
fact: Chino cloth is a twill fabric originally made from pure cotton; the trousers made from it are widely called chinos.

name: Fire brick
fact: A fire brick is a block of ceramic material used in lining furnaces, kilns, fireboxes and fireplaces.

name: Concrete slab
fact: A concrete slab is a common structural element of modern buildings, a flat, horizontal surface made of cast concrete.

name: Construction aggregate
fact: Construction aggregate is a broad category of coarse to medium-grained particulate material used in construction.

name: Siding
fact: Siding is the protective material attached to the exterior side of the wall of a house or other building.

name: Stone slab
fact: A stone slab is a big stone, flat and relatively thin, often rectangular, used for paving floors, covering walls or as headstones.

name: Tile
fact: Tiles are usually thin, square or rectangular coverings made from hard-wearing material such as ceramic, stone, metal, baked clay or glass.

name: Engineered wood
fact: Engineered wood includes a range of wood products manufactured by binding the strands, particles, fibres, veneers or boards of wood together with adhesives.

name: Wood drying
fact: Wood drying reduces the moisture content of wood before its use.

name: Environmental remediation
fact: Environmental remediation is the removal, treatment and containment of pollution from soil, groundwater and sediment.

name: Bioaugmentation
fact: Bioaugmentation is a type of bioremediation commonly used in municipal wastewater treatment to restart activated sludge bioreactors.

name: Phytoremediation
fact: Phytoremediation technologies use living plants to clean up soil, air and water contaminated with pollutants.

name: Groundwater remediation
fact: Groundwater remediation treats polluted groundwater by removing the pollutants or converting them into harmless products.

name: Soil vapor extraction
fact: Soil vapor extraction is a physical treatment process for remediation of volatile contaminants in unsaturated soils.

name: Marina
fact: A marina is a dock or area of water with piers and moorings for securing and parking yachts and small boats.

name: Maritime passenger terminal
fact: A passenger terminal is a structure in a port which services passengers boarding and leaving ferries, cruise ships and ocean liners.

name: Container port
fact: A container port is a facility where cargo containers are transshipped between different transport vehicles.

name: Convention center
fact: A convention center is a large building designed to hold a convention, where individuals and groups gather to share common interests.

name: Data center
fact: A data center is a facility dedicated to housing computer equipment for the storage, manipulation and transmission of digital information.

name: Military base
fact: A military base is a facility owned and operated by or for the military that shelters equipment and personnel and facilitates training and operations.

name: Fire safety
fact: Fire safety is the set of practices intended to reduce destruction caused by fire.

name: Flood control in the Netherlands
fact: Flood control is an important issue for the Netherlands, as about two thirds of its low-lying area is vulnerable to flooding.

name: Bratsk Hydroelectric Power Station
fact: The Bratsk Hydroelectric Power Station is a concrete gravity dam on the Angara River with an adjacent power station.

name: New Croton Dam
fact: The New Croton Dam is a masonry gravity dam forming the New Croton Reservoir, part of the New York City water supply.

name: Euphrates Dam
fact: The Euphrates Dam, most commonly known as Tabqa Dam, is an embankment dam on the Euphrates in Syria.

name: Gordon Dam
fact: The Gordon Dam is a major gated double-curvature concrete arch dam across the Gordon River in Tasmania, Australia.

name: Enguri Dam
fact: The Enguri Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Enguri River in Georgia and one of the highest concrete arch dams in the world.

name: Mangla Dam
fact: The Mangla Dam is a multipurpose dam situated on the Jhelum River in Pakistan.

name: Rogun Dam
fact: The Roghun Dam is an embankment dam on the Vakhsh River in southern Tajikistan.

name: Banpo Bridge
fact: The Banpo Bridge is a major bridge for vehicular traffic over the Han River in central Seoul.

name: Bridge of the Americas
fact: The Bridge of the Americas is a road bridge in Panama which spans the Pacific entrance to the Panama Canal.

name: Confederation Bridge
fact: The Confederation Bridge is a box girder bridge linking Prince Edward Island with the mainland province of New Brunswick.

name: Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge
fact: The Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge is a very long viaduct on the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway.

name: El Ferdan Railway Bridge
fact: The El Ferdan Railway Bridge is a swing bridge that spans the western shipping lane of the Suez Canal.

name: Kapellbrücke
fact: The Kapellbrücke is a covered wooden footbridge spanning the river Reuss in the city of Lucerne.

name: Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge
fact: The Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge is a historic bridge over the Drina River in Višegrad, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

name: Si-o-se-pol
fact: The Allahverdi Khan Bridge, popularly known as Si-o-se-pol, is the largest of the eleven historical bridges on the Zayanderud in Isfahan.

name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge–Tunnel
fact: The Chesapeake Bay Bridge–Tunnel is a bridge–tunnel that crosses the mouth of the Chesapeake Bay in Virginia.

name: Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge
fact: The Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge is a bridge–tunnel system of three cable-stayed bridges, an undersea tunnel and four artificial islands.

name: Tokyo Bay Aqua-Line
fact: The Tokyo Bay Aqua-Line is an expressway made up mainly of a bridge–tunnel combination across Tokyo Bay in Japan.

name: MEMS
fact: Micro-electromechanical systems are microscopic devices incorporating both electronic and moving parts.

name: Micromachinery
fact: Micromachines are mechanical objects that are fabricated in the same general manner as integrated circuits.

name: Nanoelectromechanical systems
fact: Nanoelectromechanical systems are devices integrating electrical and mechanical functionality on the nanoscale.

name: Leg mechanism
fact: A leg mechanism is a mechanical system designed to provide a propulsive force by intermittent frictional contact with the ground.

name: User guide
fact: A user guide is intended to assist users in using a particular product, service or application.

name: Net
fact: A net comprises threads or yarns knotted and twisted into a grid-like structure which blocks large items while letting small items and fluids pass.

name: Fisherman's knot
fact: The fisherman's knot is a knot, specifically a bend, that joins two lines.

name: Flexible shaft
fact: A flexible shaft is a device for transmitting rotary motion between two objects which are not fixed relative to one another.

name: Washer
fact: A washer is a thin plate with a hole that is normally used to distribute the load of a threaded fastener such as a bolt or nut.

name: Alarm
fact: An alarm is a mechanism that gives an audible or visual signal to alert someone to a problem that requires urgent attention.

name: Disc tumbler lock
fact: A disc tumbler lock is a lock composed of slotted rotating detainer discs.

name: Lever tumbler lock
fact: A lever tumbler lock is a type of lock whose mechanism uses a set of levers to prevent the bolt from moving.

name: Kinematic pair
fact: A kinematic pair is a connection between two physical objects that imposes constraints on their relative movement.

name: Tappet
fact: A tappet is a valve train component which converts rotational motion into linear motion in activating a valve.

name: Whippletree
fact: A whippletree is a mechanism to distribute force evenly through linkages.

name: Capstan
fact: A capstan is a vertical-axled rotating machine used on sailing ships to multiply the pulling force of sailors hauling ropes and cables.

name: Pistonless rotary engine
fact: A pistonless rotary engine is an internal combustion engine that does not use reciprocating pistons.

name: Flat engine
fact: A flat engine is a piston engine where the cylinders are located on either side of a central crankshaft.

name: Straight engine
fact: A straight engine is a multi-cylinder piston engine where all of the cylinders are arranged in a single row.

name: Hydraulic machinery
fact: Hydraulic machines use liquid fluid power to perform work.

name: Hydraulic manifold
fact: A hydraulic manifold is a component that regulates fluid flow between pumps and actuators in a hydraulic system.

name: Portable toilet
fact: A portable toilet is any type of toilet that can be moved around, some by one person, some by a truck and crane.

name: Squat toilet
fact: A squat toilet is a toilet used by squatting rather than sitting.

name: Toilet seat
fact: A toilet seat is a hinged unit consisting of a round or oval open seat, and usually a lid, bolted onto the bowl of a toilet.

name: Urinal
fact: A urinal is a sanitary plumbing fixture similar to a toilet, but for urination only.

name: Inflatable
fact: An inflatable is an object that can be inflated with a gas, usually air.

name: Planter
fact: A planter is a farm implement, usually towed behind a tractor, that sows seeds in rows throughout a field.

name: Reaper-binder
fact: The reaper-binder is a farm implement that improved upon the simple reaper.

name: Swather
fact: A swather is a farm implement that cuts hay or small grain crops and forms them into a windrow for drying.

name: Transplanter
fact: A transplanter is an agricultural machine used for transplanting seedlings to the field.

name: Major appliance
fact: A major appliance is a machine used for routine housekeeping tasks such as cooking, washing laundry or food preservation.

name: Water dispenser
fact: A water dispenser is a machine that dispenses, and often also cools or heats, water.

name: Water heating
fact: Water heating is a heat transfer process that uses an energy source to heat water above its initial temperature.

name: Quern-stone
fact: A quern-stone is a stone tool for hand-grinding a wide variety of materials, especially grains.

name: Milling
fact: Milling is the process of machining using rotary cutters by advancing a workpiece into the cutter.

name: Trip hammer
fact: A trip hammer is a massive powered hammer, usually raised by a cam and then released to fall under the force of gravity.

name: Lifting equipment
fact: Lifting equipment is a general term for any equipment that can be used to lift and lower loads.

name: Hoist
fact: A hoist is a device used for lifting or lowering a load by means of a drum or lift-wheel around which rope or chain wraps.

name: Jack
fact: A jack is a mechanical lifting device.

name: Roller
fact: The roller is an agricultural tool used for flattening land or breaking up large clumps of soil.

name: Scythe
fact: A scythe is an agricultural hand-tool for mowing grass or harvesting crops.

name: Drafting machine
fact: A drafting machine is a tool used in technical drawing, consisting of a pair of scales mounted at a right angle on an articulated protractor head.

name: Enamel paint
fact: Enamel paint is paint that air-dries to a hard, usually glossy finish, used for coating surfaces subject to hard wear.

name: Cage
fact: A cage is an enclosure often made of mesh, bars or wires, used to confine, contain or protect something or someone.

name: Locker
fact: A locker is a small, usually narrow storage compartment.

name: Pressure vessel
fact: A pressure vessel is a container designed to hold gases or liquids at a pressure substantially different from the ambient pressure.

name: Safe
fact: A safe is a secure, lockable enclosure that protects objects against theft or fire.

name: Steel and tin cans
fact: A steel can or tin can is a container made of thin metal, for distribution or storage of goods.

name: Funnel
fact: A funnel is a tube or pipe that is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom, used for guiding liquid or powder into a small opening.

name: Clovis point
fact: Clovis points are the characteristically fluted projectile points of the prehistoric Paleo-American Clovis culture.

name: Ground stone
fact: Ground stone is a category of stone tool formed by the grinding of a coarse-grained tool stone.

name: Microlith
fact: A microlith is a small stone tool usually made of flint or chert.

name: Prismatic blade
fact: A prismatic blade is a long, narrow, specialized stone flake tool with a sharp edge, like a small razor blade.

name: Breathalyzer
fact: A breathalyzer is a device for measuring breath alcohol content.

name: Electronic tagging
fact: Electronic tagging is a form of surveillance that uses an electronic device affixed to a person to monitor their location.

name: Feeler gauge
fact: A feeler gauge is a tool used to measure gap widths.

name: Metre-stick
fact: A metre-stick is a straightedge or foldable ruler used to measure length, especially common in the construction industry.

name: Optical spectrometer
fact: An optical spectrometer is an instrument used to measure properties of light over a portion of the electromagnetic spectrum.

name: Vernier scale
fact: A vernier scale is a visual aid to take an accurate measurement reading between two graduation markings on a linear scale.

name: Graphometer
fact: The graphometer is a surveying instrument used for angle measurements.

name: Gunter's chain
fact: Gunter's chain is a distance-measuring device used for surveying.

name: Laser rangefinder
fact: A laser rangefinder is a rangefinder that uses a laser beam to determine the distance to an object.

name: Level
fact: A level is an optical instrument used to establish or verify points in the same horizontal plane.

name: Level staff
fact: A level staff is a graduated rod used with a levelling instrument to determine the difference in height between points.

name: Tiltmeter
fact: A tiltmeter is a sensitive inclinometer designed to measure very small changes from the vertical level.

name: Plane table
fact: A plane table is a surveying device that provides a solid and level surface on which to make field drawings, charts and maps.

name: Stadimeter
fact: A stadimeter is an optical device for estimating the range to an object of known height by measuring the angle between its top and bottom.

name: Surveyor's wheel
fact: A surveyor's wheel is a device for measuring distance.

name: Quill
fact: A quill is a writing tool made from a moulted flight feather of a large bird.

name: Chemical law
fact: Chemical laws are laws of nature relevant to chemistry, the most fundamental being the conservation of mass.

name: Chemical safety
fact: Chemical safety includes all the policies and practices designed to minimize the risk of exposure to hazardous chemicals.

name: Dangerous goods
fact: Dangerous goods are substances that are a risk to health, safety, property or the environment during transport.

name: Regulation of chemicals
fact: The regulation of chemicals is the legislative intent of national laws and international agreements, strategies and conventions.

name: Wet lab
fact: A wet lab is a laboratory where various chemicals and wet hazards are handled, so the room must be designed to avoid spillage and contamination.

name: Molecular modelling
fact: Molecular modelling encompasses all theoretical and computational methods used to model or mimic the behaviour of molecules.

name: Electron counting
fact: Electron counting is a formalism for assigning a number of valence electrons to individual atoms in a molecule.

name: Mass concentration
fact: In chemistry, the mass concentration is the mass of a constituent divided by the volume of the mixture.

name: Number density
fact: The number density is an intensive quantity used to describe the degree of concentration of countable objects in physical space.

name: Sol
fact: A sol is a colloid made out of tiny solid particles in a continuous liquid medium.

name: Organic nomenclature
fact: The nomenclature of organic chemistry is a method of naming organic compounds as recommended by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry.

name: Inorganic nomenclature
fact: The nomenclature of inorganic chemistry is a systematic method of naming inorganic compounds, as recommended by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry.

name: Standard atomic weight
fact: The standard atomic weight of an element is the weighted mean of the relative isotopic masses of all its isotopes.

name: Main-group element
fact: The main group is the group of elements, sometimes called the representative elements, whose lightest members include lithium, boron, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and fluorine.

name: Periodic trends
fact: Periodic trends are specific patterns in the periodic table that illustrate different aspects of elements when grouped by period or group.

name: Van der Waals radius
fact: The van der Waals radius of an atom is the radius of an imaginary hard sphere representing the distance of closest approach for another atom.

name: Reactivity
fact: In chemistry, reactivity is the impulse for which a substance undergoes a chemical reaction, with an overall release of energy.

name: Law of multiple proportions
fact: The law of multiple proportions states that in compounds of two elements, the amount of one per measure of the other differs by ratios of small whole numbers.

name: Natural product
fact: A natural product is a natural compound or substance produced by a living organism.

name: Chemical composition
fact: A chemical composition specifies the identity, arrangement and ratio of the elements making up a compound.

name: Tautomer
fact: Tautomers are a subset of structural isomers of chemical compounds that readily interconvert.

name: Structural formula
fact: The structural formula of a compound is a graphic representation of its molecular structure, showing how the atoms are connected.

name: Molecular model
fact: A molecular model is a physical model of an atomistic system that represents molecules and their processes.

name: Molecular graphics
fact: Molecular graphics is the study of molecules and their properties through graphical representation.

name: Fragrance compound
fact: A fragrance compound is a chemical compound with a pleasant odor.

name: Open-chain compound
fact: An open-chain compound is a compound with a linear structure, rather than a cyclic one.

name: Hydrogen atom
fact: A hydrogen atom is an atom of the element hydrogen, with a single proton in the nucleus and a single bound electron.

name: Isotopes of hydrogen
fact: Hydrogen has three naturally occurring isotopes, of which two are stable and one is radioactive.

name: Solid hydrogen
fact: Solid hydrogen is the solid state of the element hydrogen.

name: Helium atom
fact: A helium atom is an atom of the element helium, with two electrons bound to a nucleus of protons and neutrons.

name: Superfluid helium
fact: Superfluid helium-four is the superfluid form of the most common isotope of helium.

name: Boron group
fact: The boron group are the elements in the thirteenth group of the periodic table, consisting of boron, aluminium, gallium, indium, thallium and nihonium.

name: Carbon group
fact: The carbon group is a periodic table group consisting of carbon, silicon, germanium, tin, lead and flerovium.

name: Pnictogen
fact: A pnictogen is any of the elements in the fifteenth group of the periodic table, also known as the nitrogen group.

name: Chalcogen
fact: The chalcogens are the elements in the sixteenth group of the periodic table, also known as the oxygen family.

name: Octasulfur
fact: Octasulfur is an odourless and tasteless yellow solid made of rings of eight sulfur atoms, and a major industrial chemical.

name: Base metal
fact: A base metal is a common and inexpensive metal, as opposed to a precious metal such as gold or silver.

name: Noble metal
fact: A noble metal is a metallic element that is resistant to corrosion and is usually found in nature in its raw form.

name: Precious metal
fact: Precious metals are rare, naturally occurring metallic minerals of high economic value.

name: Rare-earth element
fact: The rare-earth elements are a set of nearly indistinguishable lustrous silvery-white soft heavy metals.

name: Extended periodic table
fact: An extended periodic table theorizes about chemical elements beyond those currently known and proven.

name: Solid acid
fact: Solid acids are acids that are insoluble in the reaction medium and often used as heterogeneous catalysts.

name: Base anhydride
fact: A base anhydride is an oxide of an alkali metal or alkaline earth metal, obtained by removing water from the corresponding hydroxide.

name: Superbase
fact: A superbase is a compound that has a particularly high affinity for protons.

name: Brønsted–Lowry theory
fact: The Brønsted–Lowry theory is an acid–base reaction theory, developed independently by Johannes Brønsted and Thomas Lowry, in which acids donate protons.

name: Electrophile
fact: An electrophile is a chemical species that forms bonds with nucleophiles by accepting an electron pair.

name: Acidity function
fact: An acidity function is a measure of the acidity of a medium or solvent system.

name: Fluoroantimonic acid
fact: Fluoroantimonic acid is a mixture of hydrogen fluoride and antimony pentafluoride, and the strongest known superacid.

name: Magic acid
fact: Magic acid is a superacid consisting of a mixture of fluorosulfuric acid and antimony pentafluoride.

name: Non-stoichiometric compound
fact: Non-stoichiometric compounds are almost always solid inorganic compounds whose elemental proportions cannot be represented by a ratio of small natural numbers.

name: Mischmetal
fact: Mischmetal is an alloy of rare-earth elements, also called cerium mischmetal.

name: Ferrite magnet
fact: A ferrite is one of a family of iron-oxide-containing magnetic ceramic materials.

name: Cyanogen
fact: Cyanogen is the simplest stable carbon nitride, a colorless and highly toxic gas with a pungent odor.

name: Oxygen difluoride
fact: Oxygen difluoride is a chemical compound of oxygen and fluorine whose molecule adopts a bent molecular geometry.

name: Diborane
fact: Diborane is an inorganic compound of boron and hydrogen, a highly toxic, colorless and pyrophoric gas.

name: Hydrogen selenide
fact: Hydrogen selenide is the simplest and most commonly encountered hydride of selenium.

name: Hydrogen halide
fact: Hydrogen halides are diatomic, inorganic compounds of hydrogen and a halogen that function as acids.

name: Tritiated water
fact: Tritiated water is a radioactive form of water in which the usual protium atoms are replaced with tritium atoms.

name: Polymer backbone
fact: The backbone of a polymer is its main chain.

name: Side chain
fact: A side chain is a chemical group attached to a core part of the molecule called the main chain or backbone.

name: Lipophilicity
fact: Lipophilicity is the ability of a chemical compound to dissolve in fats, oils, lipids and non-polar solvents.

name: Substituent
fact: A substituent is one or a group of atoms that replaces one or more atoms, thereby becoming a moiety in the new molecule.

name: Enol
fact: Enols are a type of functional group or intermediate in organic chemistry, formally derivatives of vinyl alcohol.

name: Tar
fact: Tar is a dark brown or black viscous liquid of hydrocarbons and free carbon, obtained from organic materials through destructive distillation.

name: Aliphatic compound
fact: Aliphatic compounds are carbon compounds that are not aromatic compounds.

name: Alicyclic compound
fact: An alicyclic compound contains one or more all-carbon rings which may be saturated or unsaturated, but are not aromatic.

name: Cyclobutane
fact: Cyclobutane is a cycloalkane made of a ring of four carbon atoms, a colourless gas commercially available as a liquefied gas.

name: Cyclopentane
fact: Cyclopentane is a highly flammable alicyclic hydrocarbon consisting of a ring of five carbon atoms.

name: Polyyne
fact: A polyyne is any organic compound with alternating single and triple bonds.

name: Antiaromaticity
fact: Antiaromaticity is a property of a cyclic molecule with a pi electron system that is less stable, as opposed to aromaticity.

name: Hückel's rule
fact: Hückel's rule predicts that a planar ring molecule will have aromatic properties if it has a particular number of pi electrons.

name: Fatty alcohol
fact: Fatty alcohols are usually high-molecular mass, straight-chain primary alcohols derived from natural fats and oils.

name: Cetyl alcohol
fact: Cetyl alcohol is a fatty alcohol that at room temperature takes the form of a waxy white solid or flakes.

name: Diol
fact: A diol is a chemical compound containing two hydroxyl groups.

name: Sugar alcohol
fact: Sugar alcohols are organic compounds, typically derived from sugars, containing one hydroxyl group attached to each carbon atom.

name: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid
fact: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid is a white, slightly water-soluble solid widely used to bind to iron and calcium ions.

name: Dimethylformamide
fact: Dimethylformamide is an organic compound, the amide of formic acid with two methyl groups on the nitrogen.

name: Cadaverine
fact: Cadaverine is a diamine, a colorless liquid with an unpleasant odor.

name: Ethylenediamine
fact: Ethylenediamine is a colorless liquid with an ammonia-like odor and a basic amine.

name: Putrescine
fact: Putrescine is a diamine, a colorless solid that melts near room temperature.

name: Propylene carbonate
fact: Propylene carbonate is a cyclic carbonate ester derived from propylene glycol.

name: Dioxane
fact: Dioxane is a heterocyclic ether, a colorless liquid with a faint sweet odor.

name: Halocarbon
fact: Halocarbon compounds are compounds in which carbon atoms are linked by covalent bonds with halogen atoms.

name: Dichlorodifluoromethane
fact: Dichlorodifluoromethane is a colorless gas, popularly known as Freon, used as a refrigerant and aerosol spray propellant.

name: Organochlorine chemistry
fact: Organochlorine chemistry is concerned with organic compounds that contain one or more carbon–chlorine bonds.

name: Fluorocarbon
fact: Fluorocarbons are chemical compounds with carbon-fluorine bonds.

name: Hydrofluorocarbon
fact: Hydrofluorocarbons are synthetic organic compounds that contain fluorine and hydrogen atoms.

name: Imidazole
fact: Imidazole is a white or colourless solid that is soluble in water, producing a mildly alkaline solution.

name: Xanthine
fact: Xanthine is a purine base found in most human body tissues and fluids.

name: Phenylpropanoid
fact: The phenylpropanoids are a diverse family of organic compounds biosynthesized by plants from the amino acids phenylalanine and tyrosine.

name: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
fact: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances are synthetic organofluorine compounds that have multiple fluorine atoms attached to an alkyl chain.

name: Polypropylene glycol
fact: Polypropylene glycol is the polymer of propylene glycol, chemically a polyether.

name: Polyvinyl acetate
fact: Polyvinyl acetate is commonly known as wood glue, white glue, carpenter's glue or school glue.

name: Anthoxanthin
fact: Anthoxanthins are flavonoid pigments in plants, ranging from white to yellow, often found on the petals of flowers.

name: Catechin
