fact: Catechin is a type of secondary metabolite providing antioxidant roles in plants.

name: Humulene
fact: Humulene is a naturally occurring monocyclic sesquiterpene consisting of three isoprene units.

name: Zingiberene
fact: Zingiberene is a monocyclic sesquiterpene that is the predominant constituent of the oil of ginger.

name: Terpenoid
fact: Terpenoids are a class of naturally occurring organic chemicals derived from the five-carbon compound isoprene.

name: Citronellal
fact: Citronellal is a monoterpenoid aldehyde, the main component that gives citronella oil its distinctive lemon scent.

name: Quaternary ammonium cation
fact: Quaternary ammonium cations are positively charged polyatomic ions with four organic groups attached to a central nitrogen.

name: Acid salt
fact: Acid salts are a class of salts that produce an acidic solution after being dissolved in a solvent.

name: Borohydride
fact: Borohydride refers to the anion of boron and four hydrogen atoms, and its salts.

name: Sodium borohydride
fact: Sodium borohydride is an inorganic compound, a white crystalline solid usually encountered as an aqueous basic solution.

name: Lithium aluminium hydride
fact: Lithium aluminium hydride is an inorganic compound of lithium, aluminium and hydrogen, a white solid.

name: Ferricyanide
fact: Ferricyanide is the anion of iron and six cyanide groups, whose most common salt is the red crystalline potassium ferricyanide.

name: Potassium ferricyanide
fact: Potassium ferricyanide is a bright red salt containing the octahedrally coordinated ferricyanide ion.

name: Boron trifluoride
fact: Boron trifluoride is a pungent, colourless and toxic gas that forms white fumes in moist air.

name: Silver nitride
fact: Silver nitride is an explosive black, metallic-looking solid formed when silver oxide or silver nitrate is dissolved in concentrated ammonia.

name: Azide
fact: An azide is a linear, polyatomic anion of three nitrogen atoms, the conjugate base of hydrazoic acid.

name: Lead azide
fact: Lead azide is an explosive inorganic compound used in detonators to initiate secondary explosives.

name: Silver azide
fact: Silver azide is a silver salt of hydrazoic acid.

name: Noble gas compound
fact: Noble gas compounds are chemical compounds that include one of the noble gases, although these are generally unreactive elements.

name: Helium compounds
fact: Helium is one of the most unreactive elements, so it was assumed that helium compounds could not exist under normal conditions.

name: Neon compounds
fact: Neon compounds are chemical compounds containing the element neon with other molecules or elements.

name: Argon compounds
fact: Argon compounds are rarely encountered due to the inertness of the argon atom.

name: Benzalkonium chloride
fact: Benzalkonium chloride is a cationic surfactant, an organic salt classified as a quaternary ammonium compound.

name: Merbromin
fact: Merbromin, marketed as Mercurochrome, is an organomercuric salt used as a topical antiseptic for minor cuts and scrapes.

name: Thiomersal
fact: Thiomersal is an organomercury compound and a well-established antiseptic and antifungal agent.

name: Chromium acetate
fact: Chromium acetate hydrate, also known as chromous acetate, is a coordination compound of chromium and acetate.

name: Calcium citrate
fact: Calcium citrate is the calcium salt of citric acid, commonly used as a food additive.

name: Iron citrate
fact: Ferric citrate describes any of several complexes of citric acid with ferric ions, most of them orange or red-brown.

name: Magnesium citrate
fact: Magnesium citrates are salts formed from citrate and magnesium ions.

name: Potassium citrate
fact: Potassium citrate is a potassium salt of citric acid, a white, hygroscopic crystalline powder.

name: Trisodium citrate
fact: Trisodium citrate is one of the three sodium salts of citric acid.

name: Zirconium dioxide
fact: Zirconium dioxide, sometimes known as zirconia, is a white crystalline oxide of zirconium.

name: Potassium peroxide
fact: Potassium peroxide is an inorganic compound formed as potassium reacts with oxygen in the air.

name: Superoxide
fact: A superoxide is a compound that contains the superoxide ion, a negatively charged oxygen molecule.

name: Borate
fact: A borate is any of a range of anions containing boron and oxygen, or any salt of such anions, such as borax.

name: Sodium metaborate
fact: Sodium metaborate is a chemical compound of sodium, boron and oxygen.

name: Ammonium carbonate
fact: Ammonium carbonate is an ammonium salt of carbonic acid.

name: Chlorite
fact: The chlorite ion, or chlorine dioxide anion, is made of one chlorine and two oxygen atoms.

name: Ammonium perchlorate
fact: Ammonium perchlorate is an inorganic compound, a colorless or white solid that is soluble in water.

name: Lead chromate
fact: Lead chromate is a bright yellow salt that is very poorly soluble in water.

name: Manganate
fact: A manganate is any negatively charged molecular entity with manganese as the central atom.

name: Potassium manganate
fact: Potassium manganate is a green-colored salt, an intermediate in the industrial synthesis of potassium permanganate.

name: Sodium permanganate
fact: Sodium permanganate is an inorganic compound closely related to the more commonly encountered potassium permanganate.

name: Vanadate
fact: A vanadate is an anionic coordination complex of vanadium.

name: Ammonium metavanadate
fact: Ammonium metavanadate is an inorganic white salt, often yellow owing to impurities.

name: Sodium orthovanadate
fact: Sodium orthovanadate is an inorganic compound of sodium, vanadium and oxygen.

name: Lead nitrate
fact: Lead nitrate is an inorganic compound that commonly occurs as a colourless crystal or white powder and is soluble in water.

name: Diammonium phosphate
fact: Diammonium phosphate is a water-soluble ammonium phosphate salt produced when ammonia reacts with phosphoric acid.

name: Trisodium phosphate
fact: Trisodium phosphate is a white, granular or crystalline solid, highly soluble in water, producing an alkaline solution.

name: Sodium dithionite
fact: Sodium dithionite is a white crystalline powder with a sulfurous odor.

name: Potassium alum
fact: Potassium alum is the double sulfate of potassium and aluminium.

name: Calcium sulfate
fact: Calcium sulfate is an inorganic salt that occurs in several hydrated forms, the anhydrous state being known as anhydrite.

name: Thiosulfate
fact: Thiosulfate is an oxyanion of sulfur, and also refers to the salts of thiosulfuric acid.

name: Cadmium sulfide
fact: Cadmium sulfide is a yellow salt of cadmium and sulfur.

name: Calcium sulfide
fact: Calcium sulfide is a white material that crystallizes in cubes like rock salt.

name: Iron sulfide
fact: Iron sulfide, or ferrous sulfide, is one of a family of compounds and minerals of iron and sulfur.

name: Mercury sulfide
fact: Mercury sulfide is a chemical compound composed of the elements mercury and sulfur.

name: Molybdenum disulfide
fact: Molybdenum disulfide is an inorganic compound composed of molybdenum and sulfur.

name: Quantitative analysis
fact: Quantitative analysis is the determination of the absolute or relative abundance of particular substances present in a sample.

name: Instrumental chemistry
fact: Instrumental analysis is a field of analytical chemistry that investigates analytes using scientific instruments.

name: Electroanalytical methods
fact: Electroanalytical methods study an analyte by measuring the potential or current in an electrochemical cell containing it.

name: Radioanalytical chemistry
fact: Radioanalytical chemistry focuses on the analysis of samples for their radionuclide content.

name: Chemical test
fact: A chemical test is a procedure designed to identify, quantify or characterise a chemical compound or chemical group.

name: Complexometric indicator
fact: A complexometric indicator is an ionochromic dye that undergoes a definite color change in presence of specific metal ions.

name: pH indicator
fact: An acidity indicator is a halochromic compound added in small amounts to a solution so its acidity or basicity can be determined visually.

name: Redox indicator
fact: A redox indicator is an indicator which undergoes a definite color change at a specific electrode potential.

name: Thermogravimetric analysis
fact: Thermogravimetric analysis is a method of thermal analysis in which the mass of a sample is measured over time as the temperature changes.

name: Coulometry
fact: Coulometry is the measure of charge transfer during an electrochemical redox reaction.

name: Voltammetry
fact: Voltammetry is a category of electroanalytical methods in which information about an analyte is obtained by measuring current as the potential is varied.

name: Polarography
fact: Polarography is a type of voltammetry where the working electrode is a dropping mercury electrode.

name: Dielectric spectroscopy
fact: Dielectric spectroscopy measures the dielectric properties of a medium as a function of frequency.

name: Atomic spectroscopy
fact: Atomic spectroscopy is the study of the electromagnetic radiation absorbed and emitted by atoms.

name: Atomic emission spectroscopy
fact: Atomic emission spectroscopy uses the intensity of light emitted from a flame, plasma, arc or spark to determine the quantity of an element in a sample.

name: Fluorescence correlation spectroscopy
fact: Fluorescence correlation spectroscopy is a statistical analysis, via time correlation, of stationary fluctuations of the fluorescence intensity.

name: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
fact: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy is a technique used to obtain an infrared spectrum of absorption or emission of a material.

name: Microwave spectroscopy
fact: Microwave spectroscopy employs microwaves, electromagnetic radiation at very high frequencies, for the study of matter.

name: Ultrafast laser spectroscopy
fact: Ultrafast laser spectroscopy uses ultrashort pulse lasers for the study of dynamics on extremely short time scales.

name: Dissociation
fact: Dissociation is a general process in which molecules, salts or complexes separate into atoms, ions or radicals, usually reversibly.

name: Arrow pushing
fact: Arrow pushing is a technique used to describe the progression of organic chemistry reaction mechanisms.

name: Reversible reaction
fact: A reversible reaction is a reaction in which the conversion of reactants to products and of products to reactants occur simultaneously.

name: Leaving group
fact: A leaving group is a molecular fragment that departs with an electron pair during a reaction step with heterolytic bond cleavage.

name: Addition reaction
fact: An addition reaction is an organic reaction in which two or more molecules combine to form a larger molecule called the adduct.

name: Cycloaddition
fact: A cycloaddition is a chemical reaction in which unsaturated molecules combine with the formation of a cyclic adduct.

name: Electrophilic addition
fact: An electrophilic addition is an addition reaction where a compound containing a double or triple bond has a pi bond broken, with the formation of two new sigma bonds.

name: Nucleophilic addition
fact: A nucleophilic addition is an addition reaction where a compound with an electrophilic double or triple bond reacts with a nucleophile.

name: Aldol condensation
fact: An aldol condensation is a condensation reaction in which two carbonyl moieties of aldehydes or ketones react to form a hydroxy aldehyde or ketone.

name: Diels–Alder reaction
fact: The Diels–Alder reaction is a chemical reaction between a conjugated diene and a substituted alkene, the dienophile, to form a substituted cyclohexene.

name: Elimination reaction
fact: An elimination reaction is a type of organic reaction in which two substituents are removed from a molecule.

name: Grignard reaction
fact: The Grignard reaction is an organometallic reaction in which alkyl, allyl, vinyl or aryl magnesium halides are added to the carbonyl group of an aldehyde or ketone.

name: Haloform reaction
fact: The haloform reaction is a chemical reaction in which a haloform is produced by the exhaustive halogenation of an acetyl group in the presence of a base.

name: Hydroformylation
fact: Hydroformylation is an industrial process for the production of aldehydes from alkenes.

name: Polymerization
fact: Polymerization is a process of reacting monomer molecules together in a chemical reaction to form polymer chains or three-dimensional networks.

name: Step-growth polymerization
fact: Step-growth polymerization is a mechanism in which bi-functional or multifunctional monomers react to form first dimers, then trimers, then longer oligomers and long chain polymers.

name: Chain-growth polymerization
fact: Chain-growth polymerization is a technique where monomer molecules add onto the active site on a growing polymer chain one at a time.

name: Radical polymerization
fact: Radical polymerization is a method by which a polymer forms by the successive addition of a radical to building blocks.

name: Ring-opening polymerization
fact: Ring-opening polymerization is a form of chain-growth polymerization in which the end of a polymer chain attacks cyclic monomers to form a longer polymer.

name: Chain transfer
fact: A chain transfer reaction is an event during polymerization by which the activity of a growing polymer chain is transferred to another molecule.

name: Emulsion polymerization
fact: Emulsion polymerization is a type of radical polymerization that usually starts with an emulsion incorporating water, monomers and surfactants.

name: Rearrangement reaction
fact: A rearrangement reaction is a broad class of organic reactions that involves a change of connectivity.

name: Allylic rearrangement
fact: An allylic rearrangement is an organic reaction in which reaction next to a double bond causes the double bond to shift to an adjacent pair of atoms.

name: Olefin metathesis
fact: Olefin metathesis is an organic reaction that entails the redistribution of fragments of alkenes by the breaking and regeneration of carbon-carbon double bonds.

name: Pericyclic reaction
fact: A pericyclic reaction is an organic reaction wherein the transition state has a cyclic geometry and the reaction progresses in a concerted fashion.

name: Acyl group
fact: An acyl group is a moiety derived by the removal of one or more hydroxyl groups from an oxoacid.

name: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution
fact: A nucleophilic aromatic substitution is a reaction in which the nucleophile displaces a good leaving group, such as a halide, on an aromatic ring.

name: Electrophilic substitution
fact: Electrophilic substitution reactions are reactions in which an electrophile displaces a functional group in a compound, typically an aromatic one.

name: Wittig reaction
fact: The Wittig reaction is a chemical reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with a triphenyl phosphonium ylide called a Wittig reagent.

name: Half-reaction
fact: A half reaction is either the oxidation or reduction reaction component of a redox reaction.

name: Oxidation state
fact: The oxidation state is the hypothetical charge of an atom assuming all of its bonds to other atoms are fully ionic.

name: Oxidizing agent
fact: An oxidizing agent is a substance in a redox reaction that gains or accepts an electron from a reducing agent.

name: Flame
fact: A flame is the visible, gaseous part of a fire, caused by a highly exothermic chemical reaction made in a thin zone.

name: Galvanic corrosion
fact: Galvanic corrosion is an electrochemical process in which one metal corrodes when it is in electrical contact with another, different metal.

name: Passivation
fact: Passivation refers to coating a material so it becomes passive, that is, less readily affected or corroded by the environment.

name: Disproportionation
fact: Disproportionation is a redox reaction in which one compound of intermediate oxidation state converts to two compounds, one of higher and one of lower oxidation state.

name: Chemical decomposition
fact: Chemical decomposition is the process of simplifying a single chemical entity into two or more fragments.

name: Kipp's apparatus
fact: Kipp's apparatus is an apparatus designed for preparation of small volumes of gases.

name: Thermal decomposition
fact: Thermal decomposition is a chemical decomposition of a substance caused by heat.

name: Cracking
fact: Cracking is the process whereby complex organic molecules such as long-chain hydrocarbons are broken down into simpler molecules.

name: Destructive distillation
fact: Destructive distillation is a chemical process in which decomposition of unprocessed material is achieved by heating it to a high temperature.

name: Salt metathesis reaction
fact: A salt metathesis reaction is a type of chemical reaction in which two compounds exchange their component ions.

name: Water–gas shift reaction
fact: The water–gas shift reaction describes the reaction of carbon monoxide and water vapor to form carbon dioxide and hydrogen.

name: Convergent synthesis
fact: A convergent synthesis is a strategy that aims to improve the efficiency of multistep synthesis.

name: Divergent synthesis
fact: A divergent synthesis is a strategy with the aim to improve the efficiency of chemical synthesis.

name: Electrosynthesis
fact: Electrosynthesis is the synthesis of chemical compounds in an electrochemical cell.

name: Enantioselective synthesis
fact: Enantioselective synthesis, also called asymmetric synthesis, is a form of chemical synthesis.

name: One-pot synthesis
fact: A one-pot synthesis is a strategy to improve the efficiency of a chemical reaction in which a reactant is subjected to successive reactions in just one reactor.

name: Organic synthesis
fact: Organic synthesis is a branch of chemical synthesis concerned with the construction of organic compounds.

name: Retrosynthetic analysis
fact: Retrosynthetic analysis is a technique for solving problems in the planning of organic syntheses.

name: Semisynthesis
fact: Semisynthesis is a type of chemical synthesis that uses compounds isolated from natural sources as the starting materials.

name: Total synthesis
fact: Total synthesis focuses on constructing complex organic compounds, especially those found in nature, using laboratory methods.

name: Separation process
fact: A separation process converts a mixture or a solution of chemical substances into two or more distinct product mixtures.

name: Theoretical plate
fact: A theoretical plate is a hypothetical zone or stage in which two phases, such as liquid and vapor, establish an equilibrium with each other.

name: Column chromatography
fact: Column chromatography is a chromatography method used to separate the individual components of a mixture.

name: High-performance liquid chromatography
fact: High-performance liquid chromatography is a chromatography technique used to separate, identify and quantify specific components in mixtures.

name: Ion chromatography
fact: Ion chromatography is a form of chromatography that separates ions and ionizable polar molecules based on their affinity to the ion exchanger.

name: Gas chromatography
fact: Gas chromatography is a common type of chromatography for separating and analyzing compounds that can be vaporized without decomposition.

name: Gel permeation chromatography
fact: Gel permeation chromatography is a type of size-exclusion chromatography that separates high molecular weight or colloidal analytes by size.

name: Thin-layer chromatography
fact: Thin-layer chromatography is a chromatography technique that separates components in non-volatile mixtures.

name: Air separation
fact: An air separation plant separates atmospheric air into its primary components, typically nitrogen and oxygen.

name: Desiccant
fact: A desiccant is a hygroscopic substance that is used to induce or sustain a state of dryness in its vicinity.

name: Vacuum drying
fact: Vacuum drying is the mass transfer operation in which moisture in a substance, usually a wet solid, is removed by creating a vacuum.

name: Spray drying
fact: Spray drying is a method of forming a dry powder from a liquid or slurry by rapidly drying with a hot gas.

name: Flash evaporation
fact: Flash evaporation is the partial vapor that occurs when a saturated liquid stream undergoes a reduction in pressure by passing through a throttling valve.

name: Vapor–liquid separator
fact: A vapor–liquid separator is a device used to separate a vapor–liquid mixture into its constituent phases.

name: Fractional freezing
fact: Fractional freezing is a process used to separate substances with different melting points.

name: Eutectic system
fact: A eutectic system is a homogeneous mixture that has a melting point lower than those of its constituents.

name: Azeotrope
fact: An azeotrope is a mixture of two or more liquids whose proportions cannot be changed by simple distillation.

name: Azeotropic distillation
fact: Azeotropic distillation is any of a range of techniques used to break an azeotrope in distillation.

name: Dean–Stark apparatus
fact: The Dean–Stark apparatus is a piece of laboratory glassware used in synthetic chemistry to collect water from a reaction mixture.

name: Continuous distillation
fact: Continuous distillation is an ongoing separation in which a mixture is continuously fed into the process and separated fractions are removed continuously.

name: Fractional distillation
fact: Fractional distillation is the separation of a mixture into its component parts, or fractions.

name: Fractionating column
fact: A fractionating column is equipment used in the distillation of liquid mixtures to separate them into fractions based on differences in volatility.

name: Steam distillation
fact: Steam distillation is a separation process that consists of distilling water together with other volatile and non-volatile components.

name: Vacuum distillation
fact: Vacuum distillation is a type of distillation performed under reduced pressure.

name: Adsorption
fact: Adsorption is the adhesion of atoms, ions or molecules from a gas, liquid or dissolved solid to a surface.

name: Physisorption
fact: Physisorption, also called physical adsorption, is a process in which the electronic structure of the atom or molecule is barely perturbed upon adsorption.

name: Chemisorption
fact: Chemisorption is a kind of adsorption which involves a chemical reaction between the surface and the adsorbate.

name: Langmuir adsorption model
fact: The Langmuir adsorption model explains adsorption by assuming an adsorbate behaves as an ideal gas at isothermal conditions.

name: Freundlich equation
fact: The Freundlich equation is an empirical relationship between the quantity of a gas adsorbed into a solid surface and the gas pressure.

name: Hygroscopy
fact: Hygroscopy is the phenomenon of attracting and holding water molecules from the surrounding environment.

name: Cyclonic separation
fact: Cyclonic separation is a method of removing particulates from an air, gas or liquid stream, without filters, through vortex separation.

name: Dialysis
fact: Dialysis is the process of separating molecules in solution by the difference in their rates of diffusion through a semipermeable membrane.

name: Extraction
fact: Extraction is a separation process consisting of the separation of a substance from a matrix.

name: Liquid–liquid extraction
fact: Liquid–liquid extraction separates compounds based on their relative solubilities in two different immiscible liquids, often water and an organic solvent.

name: Soxhlet extractor
fact: A Soxhlet extractor is a piece of laboratory apparatus originally designed for the extraction of a lipid from a solid material.

name: Cross-flow filtration
fact: Cross-flow filtration, also known as tangential flow filtration, is a type of filtration used in chemical and biochemical engineering.

name: Microfiltration
fact: Microfiltration passes a contaminated fluid through a special pore-sized membrane filter to separate microorganisms and suspended particles.

name: Ultrafiltration
fact: Ultrafiltration is a variety of membrane filtration in which pressure or concentration gradients lead to a separation through a semipermeable membrane.

name: Nanofiltration
fact: Nanofiltration is a membrane filtration process that uses nanometer sized pores.

name: Reverse osmosis
fact: Reverse osmosis is a water purification process that uses a semi-permeable membrane to separate water molecules from other substances.

name: Recrystallization
fact: Recrystallization is a broad class of purification techniques characterized by the dissolution of an impure sample in a solvent.

name: Fractional crystallization
fact: Fractional crystallization is a stage-wise separation technique that relies on the liquid–solid phase change.

name: Sedimentation
fact: Sedimentation is the deposition of sediments when particles in suspension settle out of the fluid and come to rest against a barrier.

name: Flocculation
fact: Flocculation is a process by which colloidal particles come out of suspension to sediment in the form of floc or flake.

name: Settling
fact: Settling is the process by which particulates move towards the bottom of a liquid and form a sediment.

name: Stripping
fact: Stripping is a physical separation process where components are removed from a liquid stream by a vapor stream.

name: Chemical process
fact: A chemical process is a means by which one or more substances undergoes a change in chemical identity.

name: Chemical reactor
fact: A chemical reactor is an enclosed volume in which a chemical reaction takes place.

name: Batch reactor
fact: A batch reactor is a chemical reactor in which the reactants, products and solvent do not flow in or out of the vessel during the reaction.

name: Semibatch reactor
fact: Semibatch reactors operate much like batch reactors, in a single stirred tank with similar equipment.

name: Continuous stirred-tank reactor
fact: The continuous stirred-tank reactor is a common model for a chemical reactor in chemical and environmental engineering.

name: Plug flow reactor
fact: The plug flow reactor model is used to describe chemical reactions in continuous, flowing systems of cylindrical geometry.

name: Laminar flow reactor
fact: A laminar flow reactor is a type of chemical reactor that uses laminar flow to control reaction rate or reaction distribution.

name: Microreactor
fact: A microreactor is a device in which chemical reactions take place in a confinement with lateral dimensions below one millimetre.

name: Unit operation
fact: A unit operation is a basic step in a process, such as separation, crystallization, evaporation or filtration.

name: Mixing
fact: Mixing is a unit operation that involves manipulation of a heterogeneous physical system with the intent to make it more homogeneous.

name: Coordination complex
fact: Many compounds of the transition metals are coordination complexes.

name: Chelation
fact: The word comes from the Greek word for a claw.

name: Coordination geometry
fact: The number of atoms bound to the central atom is its coordination number.

name: Coordination sphere
fact: A second coordination sphere can surround the first through weaker forces.

name: Ligand cone angle
fact: Chadwick Tolman introduced it for phosphine ligands.

name: Crystal field theory
fact: It helps explain the colours of many transition metal complexes.

name: Ligand
fact: The bonding generally involves donation of one or more of the ligand's electron pairs.

name: Ligand field theory
fact: It grew out of crystal field theory.

name: Molecular geometry
fact: Shape strongly affects a molecule's polarity and reactivity.

name: Bent molecular geometry
fact: Water is the best-known bent molecule.

name: Linear molecular geometry
fact: Carbon dioxide and acetylene are linear molecules.

name: Octahedral molecular geometry
fact: Sulfur hexafluoride is a classic octahedral molecule.

name: Tetrahedral molecular geometry
fact: Methane is the classic example.

name: Trigonal planar molecular geometry
fact: Boron trifluoride is a standard example.

name: Trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry
fact: Ammonia has this shape.

name: Electron-pair repulsion theory
fact: It is also named the Gillespie–Nyholm theory after its two main developers.

name: Linear combination of atomic orbitals
fact: Adding or subtracting atomic orbital wave functions gives bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals.

name: Orbital hybridisation
fact: Linus Pauling introduced the idea to explain the shape of methane.

name: Pi bond
fact: Double and triple bonds contain pi bonds.

name: Sigma bond
fact: Every single bond is a sigma bond.

name: Electrochemical cell
fact: A battery is made of one or more electrochemical cells.

name: Electrolytic cell
fact: Electrolytic cells can split water into hydrogen and oxygen.

name: Galvanic cell
fact: Ordinary batteries are galvanic cells.

name: Half-cell
fact: A complete cell is built from two half-cells.

name: Salt bridge
fact: It lets ions pass between two half-cells while keeping their solutions apart.

name: Reduction potential
fact: It is measured in volts.

name: Absolute electrode potential
fact: Ordinary potentials are measured against a reference electrode instead.

name: Standard hydrogen electrode
fact: Its potential is defined as zero volts at every temperature.

name: Nernst equation
fact: It is named after the German chemist Walther Nernst.

name: Standard electrode potential
fact: Values are given relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.

name: Galvanic series
fact: Engineers use it to avoid pairing metals that corrode each other.

name: Reactivity series
fact: Potassium sits near the top and gold near the bottom.

name: Rate equation
fact: The exponents in it must be found by experiment.

name: Law of mass action
fact: Cato Guldberg and Peter Waage formulated it in the nineteenth century.

name: Rate-determining step
fact: It acts as a bottleneck for the whole reaction.

name: Reaction rate
fact: Rates range from the slow rusting of iron to the near-instant burst of an explosion.

name: Reaction rate constant
fact: It changes with temperature.

name: Transition state theory
fact: Henry Eyring, Meredith Evans and Michael Polanyi developed it in the nineteen thirties.

name: Activated complex
fact: It sits at the top of the energy barrier between reactants and products.

name: Activation energy
fact: Svante Arrhenius introduced the term.

name: Hammond's postulate
fact: It is named after the American chemist George Hammond.

name: Reaction coordinate
fact: Energy diagrams plot energy against it.

name: Transition state
fact: It lasts only an instant and cannot normally be isolated.

name: Arrhenius equation
fact: It is named for the Swedish chemist Svante Arrhenius.

name: Pre-exponential factor
fact: It reflects how often collisions occur with a suitable orientation.

name: Collision theory
fact: Only collisions with enough energy and the right orientation lead to a reaction.

name: Collision frequency
fact: It rises with temperature and concentration.

name: Entropy of activation
fact: A negative value suggests the transition state is more ordered than the reactants.

name: Thermostability
fact: Enzymes from heat-loving microbes are often thermostable.

name: Thermolabile
fact: Many enzymes and vaccines are thermolabile.

name: Stereochemistry
fact: It is sometimes called three-dimensional chemistry.

name: Stereoisomerism
fact: Enantiomers and diastereomers are its two kinds.

name: Priority rules
fact: They assign the labels R and S to stereocentres.

name: Absolute configuration
fact: It is often labelled with R and S.

name: Enantiomer
fact: Like a left hand and a right hand, the pair cannot be laid exactly over each other.

name: Racemic mixture
fact: Racemic mixtures are rare in nature.

name: Racemization
fact: The result is optically inactive.

name: Stereocenter
fact: A carbon atom bearing four different groups is the commonest stereocentre.

name: Rotamer
fact: Ethane has staggered and eclipsed rotamers.

name: Atropisomer
fact: The name comes from the Greek for not turning.

name: Cyclohexane conformation
fact: The chair is its most stable shape.

name: Ring flip
fact: Axial and equatorial positions swap places.

name: Eclipsed conformation
fact: It is less stable than the staggered form because of torsional strain.

name: Gauche effect
fact: Molecules with neighbouring fluorine atoms show it.

name: Newman projection
fact: It is named after the American chemist Melvin Newman.

name: Staggered conformation
fact: It is the lowest-energy conformation of ethane.

name: Steric effects
fact: Bulky groups can slow or block a reaction.

name: A value
fact: They are taken from the energy preference of a group on cyclohexane for the equatorial position.

name: Chemical strain
fact: Small rings such as cyclopropane are strained.

name: Diastereomer
fact: Unlike enantiomers, they differ in physical properties.

name: Cis–trans isomerism
fact: Trans fats are named for the trans arrangement around a double bond.

name: E–Z notation
fact: It extends the older cis–trans notation.

name: Supramolecular chemistry
fact: Pedersen, Cram and Lehn shared a Nobel Prize for work that founded the field.

name: Molecular self-assembly
fact: It can happen within one molecule or between many.

name: Host–guest chemistry
fact: Crown ethers are classic hosts.

name: Clathrate compound
fact: Methane hydrate is a clathrate in which methane sits inside cages of ice.

name: Endohedral fullerene
fact: The first one made held a lanthanum atom.

name: Chemical polarity
fact: Water is a polar molecule.

name: Amphiphile
fact: Soaps and detergents are amphiphiles.

name: Hydrophile
fact: Sugar and salt are hydrophilic.

name: Hydrophobe
fact: Oils and waxes are hydrophobic.

name: London dispersion force
fact: They are named for Fritz London, and help geckos cling to walls.

name: Chemical thermodynamics
fact: It predicts whether a reaction can happen on its own.

name: Thermochemistry
fact: A reaction may release or absorb energy.

name: Colligative properties
fact: Boiling point elevation and osmotic pressure are colligative.

name: Boiling-point elevation
fact: Salted water boils at a slightly higher temperature than pure water.

name: Osmotic pressure
fact: Reverse osmosis desalination works by applying more pressure than this.

name: Vapor pressure
fact: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the pressure around it.

name: Volatility
fact: Acetone is highly volatile.

name: Reaction quotient
fact: Comparing it with the equilibrium constant shows which way a reaction will run.

name: Thermodynamic activity
fact: It corrects concentration for non-ideal behaviour.

name: Activity coefficient
fact: In an ideal mixture it equals one.

name: Equilibrium constant
fact: A large constant means the products are favoured.

name: Thermal runaway
fact: It can cause battery fires.

name: Flory–Huggins solution theory
fact: Paul Flory and Maurice Huggins developed it independently in the nineteen forties.

name: Isotopes of carbon
fact: Carbon-fourteen is used to date ancient remains.

name: Isotopes of nitrogen
fact: Thirteen radioisotopes of nitrogen are also known.

name: Isotopes of oxygen
fact: Its radioisotopes are all short-lived, the most stable lasting only a couple of minutes.

name: Allotropes of phosphorus
fact: Red phosphorus is the form used on matchboxes.

name: Isotopes of uranium
fact: Uranium is used as fuel in nuclear reactors.

name: Technetium-99m
fact: It lets doctors see inside the body without surgery.

name: Group 3 element
fact: Scandium and yttrium head the group.

name: Group 4 element
fact: Titanium is the lightest of them.

name: Group 5 element
fact: This group lies in the d-block of the periodic table.

name: Group 6 element
fact: Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal.

name: Group 7 element
fact: Technetium has no stable isotopes.

name: Group 8 element
fact: Iron is by far the commonest member.

name: Group 9 element
fact: Iridium is among the densest elements.

name: Group 10 element
fact: Platinum and palladium are valued in catalytic converters.

name: Group 11 element
fact: Copper, silver and gold are the coinage metals.

name: Group 12 element
fact: Mercury is liquid at room temperature.

name: Period 1 element
fact: Only hydrogen and helium belong to it.

name: Period 2 element
fact: It runs from lithium to neon.

name: Period 3 element
fact: It runs from sodium to argon.

name: Period 4 element
fact: It runs from potassium to krypton.

name: Period 5 element
fact: It runs from rubidium to xenon.

name: Period 6 element
fact: It runs from caesium to radon.

name: Period 7 element
fact: It runs from francium to oganesson.

name: Non-nucleophilic base
fact: Bulky groups around the reactive atom keep it from attacking other atoms.

name: Conjugate acid and base
fact: Every acid has a conjugate base and every base has a conjugate acid.

name: Hard and soft acids and bases
fact: Ralph Pearson proposed it in the nineteen sixties.

name: Carborane acid
fact: They are built on cages of boron and carbon atoms.

name: Triflic acid
fact: It contains fluorine atoms that make it so strong.

name: Copper alloys
fact: Bronze and brass are the best-known examples.

name: Yttrium barium copper oxide
fact: It is a ceramic that is brittle like pottery.

name: Boranes
fact: Many boranes are reactive and toxic.

name: Carborane
fact: Their atoms form cages shaped like solid figures.

name: Pnictogen hydride
fact: Ammonia is the best-known example.

name: Stibine
fact: Its name comes from the Latin word for antimony.

name: Hydrogen chalcogenide
fact: Water is the first compound in this series.

name: Polysulfane
fact: Compounds containing two to eight sulfur atoms have been isolated.

name: Degree of unsaturation
fact: Chemists use it to work out the structure of an unknown compound.

name: Pendant group
fact: Side groups strongly affect a polymer's properties.

name: Arene substitution pattern
fact: Ortho, meta and para describe the three common patterns on a benzene ring.

name: 1-Propanol
fact: It is used as a solvent in the pharmaceutical industry.

name: Dodecanol
fact: It is a common ingredient in soaps and shampoos.

name: Stearyl alcohol
fact: It is a common ingredient in creams and lotions.

name: Geminal diol
fact: Most are unstable and lose water.

name: N,N-Diethyl-meta-toluamide
fact: It is a colourless to slightly yellow oil applied to the skin or to clothing.

name: Poly(methyl methacrylate)
fact: It is often sold as acrylic glass.

name: Alkali salt
fact: Rather than being neutral, alkali salts are bases, as their name suggests.

name: Lithium borohydride
fact: It dissolves well in ethers.

name: Aluminium carbide
fact: It reacts with water to release methane.

name: Disodium helide
fact: It is a rare compound of an inert gas.

name: Argon fluorohydride
fact: It was among the first compounds made from argon.

name: Xenon hexafluoroplatinate
fact: Neil Bartlett made it, overturning the belief that noble gases form no compounds.

name: Sodium calcium edetate
fact: It works by binding lead so the body can pass it out.

name: Tetrasodium ethylenediaminetetraacetate
fact: It is used to bind metal ions in cleaners and cosmetics.

name: Aluminium triacetate
fact: It is used as a mordant in dyeing.

name: Ammonium ferric citrate
fact: It is used in blueprint paper.

name: Monosodium citrate
fact: It is used as a food additive.

name: Disodium citrate
fact: It is used as a food additive.

name: Ammonium dihydrogen phosphate
fact: It is a salt that forms crystals.

name: Phosphite ion
fact: Phosphite is a different ion from phosphate.

name: Cyclic voltammetry
fact: The current is plotted against the potential to give a loop-shaped trace.

name: Free-radical addition
fact: Many plastics are made by chains of such reactions.

name: E1cB elimination reaction
fact: It proceeds through a negatively charged intermediate.

name: Ei mechanism
fact: Vicinal means that the two groups are on adjacent atoms.

name: 1,2-rearrangement
fact: The movement involves two adjacent atoms.

name: SN1 reaction
fact: Its rate-determining step is unimolecular.

name: SN2 reaction
fact: A strong nucleophile attacks from the back side of the carbon atom.

name: SNi reaction
fact: It is encountered only rarely.

name: Van Deemter equation
fact: It helps pick the best flow speed for a column.

name: Random column packing
fact: The packing is simply poured in rather than stacked by hand.

name: Brunauer–Emmett–Teller theory
fact: It is named for Stephen Brunauer, Paul Emmett and Edward Teller.

name: Interstellar object
fact: The first one seen passing through the Solar System was Oumuamua.

name: Substellar object
fact: Brown dwarfs and planets are substellar objects.

name: Astrobiology
fact: It draws on biology, chemistry, astronomy and geology.

name: Extraterrestrial intelligence
fact: No such beings have yet been found.

name: Search for extraterrestrial intelligence
fact: Radio telescopes listen for narrow signals that nature is unlikely to make.

name: Astrochemistry
fact: The discipline overlaps with astronomy and chemistry.

name: Cosmochemistry
fact: Meteorites are a main source of evidence.

name: Cosmology
fact: The word was first used in English in sixteen fifty-six in Thomas Blount's Glossographia.

name: Space physics
fact: It includes the topic of aeronomy.

name: Time-domain astronomy
fact: It is said to have begun with Galileo's Letters on Sunspots.

name: Night sky
fact: It is darkest far from city lights.

name: Amateur astronomy
fact: Amateurs have discovered comets and supernovae.

name: Astrophotography
fact: Long exposures reveal faint objects the eye cannot see.

name: Bayer designation
fact: Johann Bayer introduced the system in his star atlas.

name: Messier object
fact: There are one hundred and ten of them.

name: Airglow
fact: It is why the night sky is never fully black.

name: Effective temperature
fact: It gives astronomers a common way to compare the heat of stars.

name: Light curve
fact: A dip in a star's light curve can reveal a planet crossing in front of it.

name: Proper motion
fact: Barnard's Star has the largest known proper motion.

name: Radial velocity
fact: It is measured from shifts in a star's spectral lines.

name: Fraunhofer lines
fact: They are named for the German physicist Joseph von Fraunhofer.

name: Infrared astronomy
fact: Infrared light can pass through dust that blocks visible light.

name: Neutrino astronomy
fact: Detectors are buried deep underground or under ice.

name: Gravitational-wave astronomy
fact: It opened a new way to observe the universe.

name: First observation of gravitational waves
fact: The waves came from two black holes merging.

name: Astronomical seeing
fact: Telescopes on high mountains see better.

name: Twinkling
fact: Stars twinkle because their light passes through Earth's turbulent air.

name: Luminosity distance
fact: It tells how far away an object is from how bright it looks compared with how bright it truly is.

name: Recessional velocity
fact: It can be measured from the redshift of its light.

name: Spectral energy distribution
fact: It shows how an object's energy is spread across wavelengths.

name: Angular resolution
fact: Larger telescope mirrors give finer resolution.

name: Angular diameter
fact: The Sun and the Moon look nearly the same size in the sky.

name: Bortle scale
fact: It was devised by the amateur astronomer John Bortle.

name: Radio astronomy
fact: It started in nineteen thirty-three, when Karl Jansky reported radiation coming from the Milky Way.

name: Radio spectrum pollution
fact: It can drown out faint signals from space.

name: Submillimetre astronomy
fact: It sees cold dust and gas.

name: Astronomical radio source
fact: Pulsars and quasars are examples.

name: Astrophysical maser
fact: A maser is like a laser, but for microwaves.

name: Brightness temperature
fact: It is the temperature a black body would need to have to give the same intensity.

name: High-energy astrophysics
fact: It includes X-ray astronomy and gamma-ray astronomy.

name: Ultraviolet astronomy
fact: Earth's atmosphere blocks most of it, so telescopes must fly in space.

name: X-ray astronomy
fact: Earth's atmosphere absorbs X-rays, so detectors must fly above it.

name: Astrophysical X-ray source
fact: Several types of astrophysical objects emit X-rays.

name: Gamma-ray astronomy
fact: Gamma rays are the most energetic form of light.

name: Nice model
fact: It is named for the city of Nice in France, where it was developed.

name: Solar core
fact: It extends outward about a fifth of the Sun's radius.

name: Solar neutrino
fact: Billions pass through each fingertip every second.

name: Interplanetary dust cloud
fact: It is the source of the zodiacal light.

name: Geology of Mercury
fact: Its surface is covered with craters.

name: Atmosphere of Venus
fact: It is mostly carbon dioxide.

name: Geology of Venus
fact: Venus is the planet nearest to Earth and most like it in mass.

name: Earth's orbit
fact: Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.

name: Earth's shadow
fact: It can be seen at twilight as a dark band low on the horizon.

name: Earthlight
fact: Earthshine makes the dark part of the Moon glow faintly.

name: Future of Earth
fact: In the very long run, the Sun's growing brightness will make Earth uninhabitable.

name: Location of Earth
fact: Earth was once believed to be the center of the universe.

name: Geology of the Moon
fact: Its surface is covered with craters.

name: Internal structure of the Moon
fact: The structure is believed to have come from a magma ocean soon after the Moon formed.

name: Orbit of the Moon
fact: Most models describe it as centred on Earth.

name: Origin of the Moon
fact: This is called the giant-impact hypothesis.

name: Theia (hypothetical planet)
fact: Debris from the collision is thought to have formed the Moon.

name: Selenography
fact: It is a subdiscipline of planetary science.

name: Near side of the Moon
fact: Tidal locking keeps this side turned toward us.

name: Far side of the Moon
fact: It is not actually always dark.

name: Lunar south pole
fact: Spacecraft have been sent to study it.

name: Geology of Mars
fact: Mars has the largest volcano in the Solar System, Olympus Mons.

name: Geological history of Mars
fact: Evidence shows that liquid water once flowed on its surface.

name: Martian polar ice caps
fact: Slabs of dry ice lie above thick layers of water ice.

name: Life on Mars
fact: Rovers continue to search for signs of past life.

name: Near-Earth object
fact: Some may one day threaten Earth with an impact.

name: Eros (asteroid)
fact: A spacecraft landed on it in two thousand one.

name: Vesta (asteroid)
fact: It is made largely of rock.

name: Pallas (asteroid)
fact: It is probably a remnant protoplanet.

name: Juno (asteroid)
fact: It is named for the Roman goddess Juno.

name: Hygiea (asteroid)
fact: It was the tenth known asteroid.

name: Ida (asteroid)
fact: It has a tiny moon named Dactyl.

name: Jupiter trojan
fact: They gather ahead of and behind the planet.

name: Atmosphere of Jupiter
fact: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm in it.

name: Magnetosphere of Jupiter
fact: It is the largest planetary magnetosphere in the Solar System.

name: Rings of Jupiter
fact: They are made mostly of dust.

name: Magnetosphere of Saturn
fact: It was discovered in nineteen seventy-nine by the Pioneer eleven spacecraft.

name: Moons of Saturn
fact: They range from tiny moonlets to Titan, which is larger than the planet Mercury.

name: Tethys (moon)
fact: It is mostly made of ice.

name: Dione (moon)
fact: It is composed of an icy mantle and crust over a silicate rocky core.

name: Iapetus (moon)
fact: It is the third-largest moon of Saturn.

name: Lakes and rivers of Titan
fact: Titan is the only moon known to have stable liquid on its surface.

name: Atmosphere of Uranus
fact: Methane gives the planet its blue-green colour.

name: Moons of Uranus
fact: Titania is the largest.

name: Ariel (moon)
fact: It is named for a sprite in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

name: Umbriel
fact: It is named after a character in a poem by Alexander Pope.

name: Rings of Uranus
fact: They are narrow and dark.

name: Moons of Neptune
fact: The largest is Triton.

name: Rings of Neptune
fact: They are faint and dusty.

name: Atmosphere of Pluto
fact: It thins out and partly freezes as Pluto moves away from the Sun.

name: Moons of Pluto
fact: Charon is the largest.

name: Scattered disc
fact: It extends far beyond the Kuiper belt.

name: Planet Nine
fact: It has never been directly observed.

name: Kepler-22b
fact: It lies in the constellation Cygnus.

name: Kepler-186f
fact: It was the first Earth-sized planet found in a habitable zone.

name: Kepler-442b
fact: It lies in the constellation Lyra.

name: Kepler-452b
fact: News reports nicknamed it Earth's cousin.

name: Proxima Centauri b
fact: It is the closest known exoplanet to the Solar System.

name: K2-18b
fact: It is a sub-Neptune, much larger than Earth.

name: HD 189733 b
fact: Astronomers in France discovered it.

name: HD 209458 b
fact: It was the first exoplanet seen crossing in front of its star.

name: Double Cluster
fact: It is visible to the naked eye.

name: Trapezium Cluster
fact: Its brightest stars light up the nebula around them.

name: 47 Tucanae
fact: It can be seen with the naked eye.

name: Messier four (star cluster)
fact: It lies close to the bright star Antares.

name: Messier thirteen (star cluster)
fact: It is also called the Great Globular Cluster in Hercules.

name: Messier fifteen (star cluster)
fact: It was included in Charles Messier's catalogue of comet-like objects.

name: Messier twenty-two (star cluster)
fact: It is among the brightest globular clusters in the sky.

name: Supernova of one thousand and six
fact: It was recorded by astronomers in many lands.

name: Supernova of one thousand and fifty-four
fact: It left behind the Crab Nebula.

name: Tycho's Supernova
fact: It is named for the astronomer Tycho Brahe, who studied it.

name: Supernova 1987A
fact: It was among the closest supernovae seen in centuries.

name: GW170817
fact: It came from two neutron stars merging.

name: Arp 220
fact: It is listed in Halton Arp's Atlas of Peculiar Galaxies.

name: IC 1101
fact: It is one of the largest known galaxies.

name: Markarian 421
fact: It is a strong source of gamma rays.

name: Markarian 501
fact: It is a blazar, an active galactic nucleus with a jet pointed toward Earth.

name: NGC 1275
fact: It is a member of the Perseus Cluster.

name: NGC 4151
fact: It is about fifty-two million light-years from Earth.

name: NGC 6946
fact: It earns the nickname from its many observed supernovae.

name: Sculptor Galaxy
fact: It lies close enough to be seen with small telescopes.

name: Fornax Cluster
fact: It lies in the southern constellation Fornax.

name: Perseus Cluster
fact: It is one of the most massive known structures in the universe.

name: Orbital eccentricity
fact: A circle has no eccentricity and a long thin ellipse has a lot.

name: Orbital elements
fact: In celestial mechanics they are considered in two-body systems using a Kepler orbit.

name: Orbital inclination
fact: It is expressed as an angle between a reference plane and the orbital plane.

name: Orbital period
fact: Earth's orbital period is one year.

name: Eclipse cycle
fact: The Saros is the best-known eclipse cycle.

name: Transit of Mercury
fact: During a transit, Mercury appears as a tiny black dot moving across the Sun.

name: Transit of Venus
fact: Transits of Venus come in pairs separated by about eight years.

name: Libration
fact: It lets us see slightly more than half of the Moon's surface over time.

name: Sidereal time
fact: It is measured by the stars rather than the Sun.

name: Lunar phase
fact: The cycle of phases takes one lunar month.

name: Full moon
fact: It happens when Earth lies between the Sun and the Moon.

name: New moon
fact: It is the best time to see faint stars.

name: Apsis
fact: They are called the apoapsis and the periapsis.

name: Gravitational collapse
fact: It is how stars begin to form.

name: Tidal acceleration
fact: It is slowly pushing the Moon away from Earth.

name: Dawn
fact: It is recognized by the appearance of indirect daylight scattered in Earth's atmosphere.

name: Dusk
fact: It comes just before the sky turns fully dark.

name: Noon
fact: Solar noon is when the Sun crosses the local celestial meridian.

name: Midnight
fact: It falls twelve hours after noon.

name: Midnight sun
fact: The Sun does not set for days or months.

name: Polar night
fact: It only occurs inside the polar circles.

name: Space rendezvous
fact: It is the first step before two spacecraft dock.

name: Orbital resonance
fact: Pluto and Neptune are in an orbital resonance.

name: Polar orbit
fact: Many mapping and weather satellites use polar orbits.

name: Horseshoe orbit
fact: The path traced looks like a horseshoe.

name: Celestial cartography
fact: Star charts are its best-known product.

name: Asterism (astronomy)
fact: The Big Dipper is a famous asterism.

name: Spherical astronomy
fact: It treats the sky as a great sphere around the observer.

name: Right ascension
fact: It is measured in hours, minutes and seconds.

name: Declination
fact: It works like latitude on Earth.

name: Stellar nucleosynthesis
fact: The elements heavier than hydrogen and helium are made inside stars.

name: Carbon nitrogen oxygen cycle
fact: Carbon acts as a catalyst, and comes out of the cycle unchanged.

name: Slow neutron capture process
fact: It builds heavy elements one neutron at a time, slowly enough for decay to keep up.

name: Stellar core
fact: The core is where the temperature and pressure allow fusion.

name: Radiative zone
fact: Light carries the heat outward, bouncing between particles.

name: Convection zone
fact: Hot gas rises, cools and sinks, carrying the heat with it.

name: Stellar atmosphere
fact: It is the part of a star whose light reaches us directly.

name: Stellar rotation
fact: It can be measured from the star's spectrum, or by timing features on the surface.

name: Stellar mass
fact: It is usually given as a proportion of the mass of the Sun.

name: Initial mass function
fact: Small stars greatly outnumber large ones at birth.

name: Stellar wind
fact: A star loses mass steadily, all its life, into space.

name: Chemically peculiar star
fact: Their surfaces show elements in strange proportions.

name: Circumstellar disc
fact: Material left over from a star's birth settles into a flat disc.

name: Debris disk
fact: The dust is ground from collisions between larger bodies.

name: Protoplanetary disk
fact: Planets form out of this disc.

name: Proplyd
fact: A nearby hot star boils the disc away from the outside.

name: Sub-brown dwarf
fact: It formed like a star but came out the size of a planet.

name: Double star
fact: Some are truly paired, others merely line up by chance.

name: Compact object
fact: What is left when a star stops burning and collapses.

name: Black dwarf
fact: The universe is not yet old enough to contain one.

name: Chandrasekhar limit
fact: Above it, electron pressure can no longer hold the star up.

name: X-ray pulsar
fact: Matter pulled from a companion falls onto the magnetic poles.

name: Magnetar
fact: Its field is strong enough to crack the star's own crust.

name: Radio-quiet neutron star
fact: It shows itself in X-rays rather than radio.

name: Exotic star
fact: Matter in a form nobody has yet observed.

name: Quark star
fact: Denser even than a neutron star.

name: Intergalactic star
fact: It drifts in the dark between the galaxies.

name: Red giant branch
fact: The star swells and reddens while its core is still inert helium.

name: Helium flash
fact: The core ignites all at once, and nothing shows on the outside.

name: Asymptotic giant branch
fact: Shells of hydrogen and helium burn in turn around a dead core.

name: Starburst region
fact: Stars form far faster than the galaxy could keep up for long.

name: Jeans instability
fact: Past a certain size, a cloud can no longer hold itself up.

name: Pre-stellar core
fact: A cold dense knot of cloud, about to fall in on itself.

name: Hayashi track
fact: A young star dims at almost constant surface temperature.

name: Pre-main-sequence star
fact: It shines by shrinking, not yet by fusing hydrogen.

name: Young stellar object
fact: The class covers protostars and pre-main-sequence stars.

name: Binary pulsar
fact: Their orbits are the strictest test of general relativity we have.

name: Common envelope
fact: Two stars end up orbiting inside a single shared atmosphere.

name: X-ray binary
fact: The X-rays come from matter falling from one star onto the other.

name: Roche lobe
fact: Fill it, and your gas begins to flow to your companion.

name: Stellar association
fact: Born together, already drifting apart.

name: Open cluster
fact: One cloud, one age, a few thousand stars.

name: Blue straggler
fact: It looks younger than the cluster it belongs to.

name: Super star cluster
fact: Globular clusters may be made this way today.

name: Hypernova
fact: A very massive star collapsing straight to a black hole.

name: Type two supernova
fact: Its spectrum still shows the hydrogen the star kept.

name: Superluminous supernova
fact: Bright enough to outshine the galaxy it sits in.

name: Pair instability supernova
fact: The star's own light turns into matter, and the support gives way.

name: Supernova nucleosynthesis
fact: The explosion itself forges elements and scatters them.

name: Fast radio burst
fact: A flash lasting a thousandth of a second, from halfway across the universe.

name: Kilonova
fact: Much of the gold and platinum in the universe is made here.

name: Asteroseismology
fact: Sound trapped inside a star tells you what it is made of.

name: Mass luminosity relation
fact: A little more mass buys a great deal more light.

name: Subdwarf
fact: It is dimmer than a main sequence star of its colour, being poor in metals.

name: Subgiant
fact: The stage between leaving the main sequence and becoming a giant.

name: Blue giant
fact: Hot, blue and short-lived.

name: Carbon star
fact: Soot in the atmosphere makes it one of the reddest things in the sky.

name: Blue supergiant
fact: Tens of times the mass of the Sun, and burning through it fast.

name: Red supergiant
fact: The largest stars there are, by volume.

name: Hypergiant
fact: It sheds its own outer layers faster than it can hold them.

name: Be star
fact: Spinning so fast that gas is flung off into a disc.

name: Cataclysmic variable star
fact: A white dwarf is stealing gas from a companion.

name: Classical Cepheid variable
fact: Their period tells you their true brightness, and so their distance.

name: Lyrae variable star
fact: Old, faint and regular, they measure distances within our own galaxy.

name: Type two Cepheid
fact: They are old, metal poor and lighter than the classical Cepheids.

name: Luminous blue variable
fact: Enormous stars in an unstable phase, throwing off shells of gas.

name: Mira variable
fact: A red giant swelling and shrinking over about a year.

name: Instability strip
fact: Cross this part of the diagram and a star cannot help pulsating.

name: Galactic astronomy
fact: Our own galaxy, studied from the inside.

name: Extragalactic astronomy
fact: Everything beyond our own galaxy.

name: Astrophysical jet
fact: Magnetic fields fling matter out along the axis of a spinning disc.

name: Intermediate mass black hole
fact: The missing middle of the black hole family.

name: Micro black hole
fact: If they exist, they evaporate almost at once.

name: Schwarzschild radius
fact: Squeeze anything inside this radius and light cannot get out.

name: Interstellar cloud
fact: A denser than average patch of the space between stars.

name: Interstellar ice
fact: Water and other ices coat dust grains in cold clouds.

name: Reflection nebula
fact: The dust shines blue with borrowed starlight.

name: Emission nebula
fact: Starlight strips electrons from the gas, and the gas glows.

name: Superbubble
fact: Many supernovae together blow a hole in the galaxy.

name: High velocity cloud
fact: Gas raining down onto the galaxy from outside.

name: Ultra high energy cosmic ray
fact: A single particle carrying the energy of a thrown ball.

name: Galactic plane
fact: The band of the Milky Way across the sky is this plane, seen edge on.

name: Thin disk
fact: The young, flat, star forming layer of a galaxy.

name: Thick disk
fact: An older, puffier layer above and below the thin one.

name: Galactic bulge
fact: The crowded old heart of a spiral galaxy.

name: Galaxy rotation curve
fact: The outer stars move too fast, which is how dark matter was found.

name: Galactic halo
fact: Globular clusters and old stars orbit out here.

name: Dark matter halo
fact: Every galaxy sits inside a much larger invisible cloud.

name: Interacting galaxy
fact: Tides pull out bridges and tails of stars.

name: Galaxy merger
fact: The stars almost never hit; the gas does.

name: Andromeda and Milky Way collision
fact: It is expected in about four thousand million years.

name: Galactic tide
fact: The galaxy itself pulls harder on one side of a cluster than the other.

name: Satellite galaxy
fact: The Milky Way has dozens of them.

name: Weak gravitational lensing
fact: Faint distortions in distant galaxies weigh the matter in front of them.

name: Intergalactic dust
fact: Even the emptiest space is not quite clean.

name: Intracluster medium
fact: Most of a cluster's ordinary matter is this gas, not its galaxies.

name: Field galaxy
fact: A galaxy with no neighbours worth the name.

name: Dark flow
fact: A claim that clusters drift together towards something unseen.

name: Wormhole
fact: A tunnel with two mouths, allowed by the equations but never seen.

name: Galaxy filament
fact: Galaxies hang in threads around enormous voids.

name: Large quasar group
fact: Dozens of quasars strung across a thousand million light years.

name: Hubble sequence
fact: Galaxies sorted by shape, in a tuning fork.

name: Unbarred spiral galaxy
fact: Its arms wind straight out of the nucleus.

name: Grand design spiral galaxy
fact: Two clear arms, sweeping all the way round.

name: Flocculent spiral galaxy
fact: Fluffy scraps of arm instead of a clean spiral.

name: Magellanic spiral
fact: A lopsided little spiral, named for the Magellanic Clouds.

name: Density wave theory
fact: The arms are a traffic jam, not a fixed set of stars.

name: Tully Fisher relation
fact: How fast it spins tells you how bright it really is.

name: Dwarf elliptical galaxy
fact: The commonest kind of galaxy in a cluster.

name: Faber Jackson relation
fact: The faster its stars mill about, the brighter the galaxy.

name: Dark galaxy
fact: A galaxy that never managed to light up.

name: Brightest cluster galaxy
fact: It sits at the centre, having eaten its neighbours.

name: Ring galaxy
fact: A small galaxy fell straight through the middle of a larger one.

name: Peculiar galaxy
fact: Between one and two galaxies in twenty will not fit the scheme.

name: Eddington luminosity
fact: Shine any brighter and you blow yourself apart.

name: Luminous infrared galaxy
fact: Dust swallows the starlight and re-emits it as heat.

name: Lyman alpha forest
fact: Every cloud between here and the quasar cuts its own line.

name: Cosmological horizon
fact: The edge of what can be seen, not the edge of what exists.

name: Particle horizon
fact: Nothing further away has had time to reach us.

name: Shape of the universe
fact: As far as anyone can measure, space is flat.

name: Heat death of the universe
fact: Everything the same temperature, and nothing left to happen.

name: Big Rip
fact: If dark energy strengthens, even atoms come apart.

name: Big Crunch
fact: The expansion runs backwards and everything falls together.

name: Cyclic model
fact: Bang, crunch, bang again, without end.

name: Cosmic neutrino background
fact: Neutrinos set loose a second after the beginning, still passing through you.

name: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
fact: Most of the helium in the universe was made in the first few minutes.

name: Missing baryon problem
fact: Half of the ordinary matter was unaccounted for, hiding as thin hot gas.

name: Baryogenesis
fact: Why there is matter and almost no antimatter is still unexplained.

name: Expansion of the universe
fact: Space itself stretches; the galaxies are not flying through it.

name: Accelerating expansion of the universe
fact: Found by watching distant supernovae, and quite unexpected.

name: Hubble volume
fact: A sphere about the size of the visible universe.

name: Scale factor in cosmology
fact: One number saying how much bigger space is now than then.

name: Baryon acoustic oscillations
fact: Sound waves from the first instants left a fixed ruler in the sky.

name: Primordial fluctuations
fact: Every galaxy grew from a tiny early ripple.

name: Lambda cold dark matter model
fact: Dark energy, cold dark matter, and ordinary matter last.

name: Quintessence in physics
fact: A dark energy that could change with time.

name: Comoving and proper distances
fact: One grows with the expansion, the other is scaled to take it out.

name: Anthropic principle
fact: We could only have found ourselves somewhere that allows us.

name: Flatness problem
fact: Space is so nearly flat now that it must have started almost exactly flat.

name: Horizon problem
fact: Opposite sides of the sky are the same temperature, having never met.

name: Steady state model
fact: It needed matter to be created continuously, and the observations went against it.

name: Age of the universe
fact: Close to fourteen thousand million years.

name: Grand unification epoch
fact: Three of the four forces were still one.

name: Electroweak epoch
fact: The electric and weak forces were still a single force.

name: Quark epoch
fact: Quarks ran free, too hot to settle into particles.

name: Photon epoch
fact: For hundreds of thousands of years, light held the upper hand.

name: Reionization
fact: The first stars and galaxies lit the universe up again.

name: Planetary science
fact: Geology, chemistry and weather, practised on other worlds.

name: Definition of planet
fact: It now requires a body to have cleared its own orbit.

name: Carbon planet
fact: Its mantle would be graphite, and perhaps diamond beneath.

name: Iron planet
fact: Mercury is the nearest thing we have to one.

name: Chthonian planet
fact: The bare core of a gas giant that strayed too close to its star.

name: Earth analog
fact: The thing every exoplanet survey is really looking for.

name: Asteroid family
fact: They are the fragments of one asteroid that was broken up.

name: Satellite system in astronomy
fact: Moons and rings, keeping their own order around a planet.

name: Exomoon
fact: None has yet been confirmed.

name: Sungrazing comet
fact: Most do not survive the pass.

name: Bolide
fact: A fireball bright enough to cast shadows, often ending in a bang.

name: Axial tilt
fact: The tilt of the Earth is what makes the seasons.

name: Planetary differentiation
fact: The iron sinks to the centre and the light rock floats.

name: Planetary habitability
fact: Mostly a question of whether liquid water can last.

name: Galactic habitable zone
fact: Too far out and there are no heavy elements, too far in and the radiation is fierce.

name: Geometric albedo
fact: How much of the light falling on a world it throws back.

name: Planetary mass
fact: Usually quoted against the mass of the Earth or of Jupiter.

name: Antlia
fact: One of the faint southern constellations named after an instrument.

name: Apus
fact: Named from a traveller's tale about a bird with no feet.

name: Caelum
fact: Its name is Latin for the engraver's chisel.

name: Camelopardalis
fact: A large patch of sky with almost nothing bright in it.

name: Carina
fact: The keel of the ship Argo, now sailing alone.

name: Cetus
fact: The sea monster sent against Andromeda.

name: Chamaeleon
fact: One of the southern constellations named by Dutch navigators.

name: Circinus
fact: The dividers a draughtsman draws circles with.

name: Columba
fact: The dove that Noah sent out, set beside the ship Argo.

name: Coma Berenices
fact: The only constellation named for a real person's hair.

name: Corona Australis
fact: A small arc of faint stars making a wreath.

name: Delphinus
fact: A tight little diamond of stars called Job's Coffin.

name: Dorado
fact: It holds most of the Large Magellanic Cloud.

name: Draco
fact: It coils right round the northern pole and never sets.

name: Equuleus
fact: The second smallest of all the constellations.

name: Eridanus
fact: A long winding chain of stars, ending at Achernar.

name: Fornax
fact: Named for a chemist's furnace, and full of distant galaxies.

name: Grus
fact: One of the southern birds charted from the first Dutch voyages.

name: Hercules constellation
fact: It holds the finest globular cluster in the northern sky.

name: Horologium
fact: Lacaille named it for the clock that times an observation.

name: Hydrus
fact: The little water snake, not to be confused with the long Hydra.

name: Indus
fact: It depicts a man holding spears, drawn as the navigators imagined him.

name: Lacerta
fact: A zigzag of faint stars squeezed between Cygnus and Andromeda.

name: Leo Minor
fact: Hevelius made it out of the leftover stars between Leo and the Great Bear.

name: Lepus
fact: It crouches at Orion's feet, under the hunter's dogs.

name: Lupus
fact: Once drawn as an unnamed beast speared by the Centaur.

name: Mensa
fact: Named for Table Mountain, where Lacaille did his observing.

name: Microscopium
fact: A faint square of stars named for the microscope.

name: Monoceros
fact: The unicorn, holding the Rosette Nebula.

name: Musca
fact: The only constellation that is an insect.

name: Norma
fact: The carpenter's set square, with no bright star of its own.

name: Octans
fact: It contains the south celestial pole, but no bright pole star.

name: Pavo
fact: Its brightest star is simply called Peacock.

name: Pictor
fact: Short for the painter's easel, which is what Lacaille drew.

name: Piscis Austrinus
fact: Its mouth is Fomalhaut, drinking the water poured by Aquarius.

name: Puppis
fact: The stern of the ship, the largest of its three pieces.

name: Pyxis
fact: The ship's compass, set beside the broken-up Argo.

name: Sagitta
fact: The third smallest constellation, and shaped exactly like its name.

name: Sculptor
fact: It holds the south galactic pole, so we look clean out of our own galaxy through it.

name: Sextans
fact: Hevelius named it for the sextant he lost in a fire.

name: Telescopium
fact: Named for the long aerial telescopes of the day.

name: Triangulum
fact: It holds the Triangulum Galaxy, the third largest of our Local Group.

name: Triangulum Australe
fact: Smaller than the northern triangle, but far brighter.

name: Tucana
fact: It holds the Small Magellanic Cloud and the cluster Tucanae.

name: Vela
fact: The sails of the ship Argo, carrying a famous pulsar.

name: Volans
fact: The fish the Dutch navigators watched leaping beside their ships.

name: Vulpecula
fact: It holds the Dumbbell Nebula, the first planetary nebula ever found.

name: Argo Navis
fact: Broken into keel, stern and sails because it was simply too big.

name: Quadrans Muralis
fact: Long abolished, but the Quadrantid meteors still carry its name.

name: March equinox
fact: Day and night are nearly equal everywhere on Earth.

name: September equinox
fact: Autumn in the north, spring in the south.

name: Summer solstice
fact: The longest day, after which the nights draw in again.

name: Winter solstice
fact: The shortest day, and the turning point of the year.

name: Hour angle
fact: How long since the star crossed your meridian, measured as an angle.

name: Position angle
fact: Measured from north, going round through east.

name: Meridian in astronomy
fact: Everything is highest in the sky as it crosses your meridian.

name: Nadir
fact: Straight down, the opposite of the zenith.

name: Zenith
fact: Straight up, wherever you happen to be standing.

name: Celestial equator
fact: The Earth's equator, projected onto the sky.

name: Tropical year
fact: This, not the orbit, is the year the calendar keeps.

name: Galactic coordinate system
fact: The sky measured from the plane of our own galaxy.

name: Twilight
fact: Light without a sun in the sky.

name: Sunrise
fact: Refraction lifts the Sun into view before it is really there.

name: Morning
fact: Which of the two you mean depends on who is asking.

name: Daytime
fact: Half the planet is in it at any moment.

name: Afternoon
fact: The sun is coming down again, though the heat still rises.

name: Evening
fact: It starts when the sun gets close to the horizon.

name: Belt of Venus
fact: A pink band opposite the sun, above the Earth's own rising shadow.

name: Blue hour
fact: Photographers and painters wait for it.

name: Golden hour in photography
fact: Low sun, long shadows, and warm light.

name: Velocity dispersion
fact: How fast the members of a cluster mill about tells you its mass.

name: Umbra penumbra and antumbra
fact: Total, partial and annular eclipses, in one diagram.

name: Astronomical transit
fact: A planet crossing a star's face is how most exoplanets are found.

name: Supermoon
fact: Slightly bigger and brighter, though you would be hard pressed to tell.

name: Axial precession
fact: The Earth's axis traces a circle every twenty six thousand years.

name: Observational astronomy
fact: You cannot run an experiment on a star; you can only watch.

name: Sky brightness
fact: The night sky is never truly black, even far from any town.

name: Absolute magnitude
fact: Every star rated as if it stood at the same distance.

name: Zone of Avoidance
fact: Our own galaxy hides about a fifth of the universe from us.

name: Photometric system
fact: Agreed filters, so one observatory's colours mean the same as another's.

name: Polarization in astronomy
fact: The twist in starlight reveals dust grains and magnetic fields.

name: Forbidden mechanism
fact: Impossible in a laboratory, commonplace in a nebula, because the gas is so thin.

name: Telluric contamination
fact: Our own air writes its lines across every spectrum we take.

name: Surface brightness
fact: Spread the same light wider and it gets harder to see.

name: Megamaser
fact: A whole galaxy acting as one enormous microwave laser.

name: Spectral index
fact: One number saying which way a source's brightness slopes with frequency.

name: Stellar corona
fact: Far hotter than the surface beneath it, and nobody is quite sure why.

name: Orcus
fact: It circles the Sun in step with Pluto, but always on the far side.

name: Gonggong
fact: One of the reddest bodies known, and among the largest unvisited.

name: Moons of Haumea
fact: They were knocked loose when something struck Haumea and set it spinning.

name: Dysnomia
fact: Weighing it is how we learned what Eris is made of.

name: Hills cloud
fact: A denser reservoir that keeps resupplying the outer cloud with comets.

name: Sednoid
fact: They never come near Neptune, so something else must have put them there.

name: Planets beyond Neptune
fact: The search that turned up Pluto, and has not stopped since.

name: Kreutz sungrazer
fact: All the fragments of one giant comet that came apart long ago.

name: Acrux
fact: The foot of the Southern Cross, and the most southerly first magnitude star.

name: Beta Centauri
fact: One of the two Pointers that lead the eye to the Southern Cross.

name: Leonis carbon star
fact: It is wrapped in so much soot that it is among the brightest things in the infrared sky.

name: Gamma Cassiopeiae
fact: The first star ever seen with emission lines, and the type for a whole class.

name: Hydrae young star
fact: The nearest young star with a planet-forming disc, seen face on.

name: Zeta Ophiuchi
fact: Thrown out of its birth cluster, it now ploughs a bow shock through the dust.

name: Rho Ophiuchi cloud complex
fact: One of the closest star nurseries to the Sun.

name: Sagittarius cloud of molecules
fact: Chemists have found alcohol and sugar in it, among much else.

name: Local Interstellar Cloud
fact: The patch of the galaxy our own Sun happens to be crossing.

name: Perseus Arm
fact: The arm just outside our own, seen as a band of young stars.

name: Magellanic Stream
fact: Gas torn out of the Clouds by the Milky Way's pull.

name: Sagittarius Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxy
fact: The Milky Way is pulling it to pieces as it orbits.

name: Lacertae blazar
fact: Mistaken for a variable star for forty years, it is a jet pointed straight at us.

name: Seyfert galaxy of Bootes
fact: One of the best-watched feeding black holes in the sky.

name: Satellite galaxies of the Milky Way
fact: Dozens are known, and more keep turning up in survey data.

name: Group of Ursa Major galaxies
fact: One of the nearest galaxy groups beyond our own.

name: Shapley Supercluster
fact: Much of the local flow of galaxies is heading towards it.

name: South Pole Wall
fact: It was hiding in plain sight behind the Milky Way until recently.

name: Great Wall of superclusters
fact: One of the largest structures known, and hard to square with a smooth universe.

name: Local Hole
fact: We may be sitting near the middle of an unusually empty patch.

name: Giant Void
fact: Hundreds of millions of light years across, and nearly empty.

name: Dipole repeller
fact: An empty region pushing us away, as surely as a cluster pulls.

name: Cold spot of the microwave background
fact: Either a very large void lies in front of it, or it is simply a fluke.

name: Orbital station keeping
fact: Without small regular nudges, every useful orbit drifts.

name: Bi elliptic transfer
fact: Going further out first can cost less fuel than going direct.

name: Frozen orbit
fact: Chosen so the lumpiness of the planet stops mattering.

name: Halo orbit
fact: It is where telescopes are parked to keep the Sun and Earth behind them.

name: Lissajous orbit
fact: It drifts in a figure that never quite repeats.

name: Graveyard orbit
fact: Dead satellites are pushed up here to clear the useful lanes.

name: Great Filter
fact: If it is behind us we were lucky, and if it is ahead of us that is worse.

name: Computational astrophysics
fact: You cannot collide two galaxies in a laboratory, so you do it in a machine.

name: Timeline of the far future
fact: It runs from the end of the Sun out past the last black hole.

name: Astrophysics Data System
fact: Nearly every astronomy paper ever written, in one place.

name: Astronomical database of objects
fact: It knows every name a given object has ever been given.

name: Catalogue service of tables
fact: Thousands of published tables, served as one.

name: Henry Draper Catalogue
fact: Classified almost single-handedly by Annie Jump Cannon.

name: New General Catalogue
fact: Its numbers are still the everyday names for most galaxies and nebulae.

name: Uppsala General Catalogue
fact: Measured by hand from photographic plates.

name: Sloan Digital Sky Survey
fact: It mapped millions of galaxies and gave everyone the data.

name: Methods of detecting exoplanets
fact: Mostly we watch the star wobble, or dim.

name: Hypothetical types of biochemistry
fact: Silicon instead of carbon, or ammonia instead of water.

name: Geochemistry
fact: Chemistry applied to the planet itself.

name: Biogeochemistry
fact: Life, rock and water are one system, not three.

name: Organic geochemistry
